news.Title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Q4 Earnings Call Highlights
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company? Here are five stocks we like better.

HPE delivered strong quarterly results: Fiscal Q4 revenue rose 50% to $14.5 billion, adjusted earnings per share increased 131% to $1.43, and orders surged 88%, building a record year-end backlog.

AI demand is driving growth, but supply and margins remain challenges: AI systems orders topped $4.5 billion, while component shortages are expected to persist until at least the second half of calendar 2028. HPE forecast fiscal 2027 revenue growth of 27%–35%, but expects adjusted operating margin to ease to 14%–15% as AI systems weigh on margins.

HPE plans substantial shareholder returns: The company is targeting about $3 billion in fiscal 2027 share repurchases and raised its quarterly dividend 19% to $0.17 per share.

AMD Bets $8.2B on Physical AI: Could Robotics Be Its Next Growth Frontier?

Hewlett Packard Enterprise (NYSE:HPE) reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $14.5 billion, up 50% from a year earlier, as orders surged and demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure and networking equipment expanded its backlog.

The company said fourth-quarter adjusted earnings were $1.43 per share, up 131% and above its guidance range. GAAP earnings were $1.26 per share. Free cash flow for the quarter was $1.9 billion.

→ ZIM Just Posted Huge Profits, But Its $35 Buyout Is Still in Limbo

4 Stocks With Demand So Sticky That the AI Sell-Off Barely Touched Them at All

For fiscal 2027, HPE forecast revenue growth of 27% to 35% and adjusted earnings of $5.05 to $5.35 per share. Management said the outlook incorporates strong demand, backlog conversion and expected improvements in component availability, although supply constraints remain.

"Based on what we see today, demand across our customer base remains very strong and durable," President and CEO Antonio Neri said. He added that the company expects supplies of memory, NAND and other critical components to remain constrained until at least the second half of calendar 2028.

Orders outpace revenue growth

→ Anthropic's Record IPO Could Ease a Major Concern for Broadcom Investors

Super Micro's Vera Rubin Shipments Put Its AI Infrastructure Advantage to the Test

Fourth-quarter orders rose 88% across HPE, contributing to what management described as a record backlog at year-end. Adjusted operating profit increased 108% to $2.5 billion, while adjusted operating margin expanded to 16.9% from a year earlier.

In the cloud and AI segment, quarterly revenue rose 69% to $11.3 billion and orders more than doubled. Server revenue increased 95%, supported by higher average selling prices for traditional servers, even as supply constrained unit volumes. Storage revenue rose 34%, helped by large public-sector and enterprise deals.

Story Continues

→ MarketBeat Week in Review – 11/16 - 11/20

Networking revenue increased 12% to $3.1 billion, while networking orders rose 56%. CFO Marie Myers said data center networking and routing revenue benefited from cloud demand but were partly constrained by supply. Campus and branch revenue grew 17%.

HPE reported $4.5 billion in AI systems orders during the quarter, up more than 130%, and $2.5 billion in AI systems revenue. Orders for networks used in AI reached $1.2 billion, while that business ended the year with a $1.7 billion backlog.

For the full fiscal year, revenue reached $46.7 billion, up 23% on a basis that included Juniper Networks results from the start of fiscal 2025. Adjusted earnings per share more than doubled to $3.97, and free cash flow totaled $4.5 billion.

AI growth expected to weigh on margins

HPE expects fiscal 2027 networking revenue to grow in the high teens to low 20% range and cloud and AI revenue to rise 30% to 40%. Myers said contributions from the AMD Helios platform and an Oracle agreement are expected to be weighted toward the second half of the year.

Management forecast a companywide adjusted operating margin of 14% to 15%, compared with 15.1% in fiscal 2026. It expects cloud and AI operating margin to be approximately 14%, down from 18.4% in the fourth quarter.

Myers attributed the anticipated decline partly to a greater mix of AI systems, which she said tend to dilute margins, and to moderating price increases. HPE expects gross profit dollars to grow even as its gross margin rate moderates in the second half, when AI server volumes are expected to increase.

Responding to an analyst's question, Myers said HPE would continue to pass component price increases through to customers. She also said the company expects more sequential unit growth in fiscal 2027, though supply will continue to constrain volumes.

For the first quarter, HPE forecast revenue of $14 billion to $14.6 billion and adjusted earnings of $1.30 to $1.40 per share. It projected GAAP earnings of $0.88 to $0.98 per share.

Higher dividend and buyback plans

HPE said it is targeting approximately $3 billion in share repurchases in fiscal 2027 and raised its quarterly dividend by 19% to $0.17 per share, beginning in the first quarter. The company returned $2 billion to common shareholders in fiscal 2026 and reiterated its target of returning at least 75% of free cash flow through dividends and buybacks over time.

Myers said HPE had raised its fiscal 2028 annualized run-rate cost synergy target for the Juniper integration to $800 million from $450 million. Together with the company's Catalyst modernization initiative, the programs are expected to deliver about $1.2 billion in annual gross run-rate savings by the end of fiscal 2028.

HPE noted that the financial information discussed on the call reflects estimates that could differ materially from the amounts ultimately reported in its annual filing.

About Hewlett Packard Enterprise (NYSE:HPE)

Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is a global information technology company that provides products and services for businesses, governments and other organizations. Its offerings span servers and computing systems, data storage, networking, hybrid cloud, artificial intelligence and edge computing. HPE sells systems such as HPE ProLiant servers and HPE Alletra storage, along with networking products through HPE Aruba Networking. Its HPE GreenLake platform provides cloud and IT services through a flexible, consumption-based model.

news.Title: 黃仁勳回歸亞股嗨翻！日股狂飆2000點 韓股噴6％觸發熔斷
news.Content:
輝達（NVIDIA）創辦人黃仁勳重掌執行長職位，激勵全球AI概念股強勢反彈，美股率先在23日展開慶祝行情，輝達股價終場大漲31.5%，帶動市場信心回溫。亞洲股市24日也接棒上攻，日、韓股市同步大漲。

南韓股市表現尤其亮眼，KOSPI指數盤中一度飆升逾6%，創近1個月來最大單日漲幅。由於KOSPI 200期貨漲幅超過5%，南韓交易所隨即啟動買方Sidecar機制，暫停程式買單5分鐘，以緩和短時間內過度集中的買盤。

其中與輝達高頻寬記憶體（HBM）供應鏈關係密切的SK海力士，盤中股價一度大漲12%，創下8月以來最大漲幅。由於輝達約占SK海力士營收的27%，因此黃仁勳重返領導職位，也讓投資人對AI晶片需求及供應鏈穩定性重新燃起信心。另一家南韓科技巨頭三星同樣表現強勁，盤中漲幅一度達9.1%，與SK海力士聯手推升韓股大盤。

日本股市也不遑多讓。由於日股23日適逢假日休市，24日恢復交易後出現補漲行情，日經225指數早盤大漲超過2000點。

整體而言，黃仁勳回歸不僅提振輝達股價，也帶動亞洲AI供應鏈信心回升，從韓國記憶體大廠到日本半導體相關企業，均受惠於這波市場買氣。不過，短線股價急漲後，後續能否延續漲勢，仍有待觀察AI需求及企業基本面的實際表現。

news.Title: 日經指數週二早盤漲4%落後韓股，週一因假期休市躲過美股上週五急殺
news.Content:
【財訊快報／陳孟朔】日本股市週二(24日)在假期後恢復交易，日經225指數開高近3%，早盤漲幅擴大至4%，仍落後韓國首爾綜合股價指數(KOSPI)一度大漲6.3%的表現。東京股市週一因勤勞感謝日休市，未在當天反映美股上週五收盤重挫，韓股則先在週一追低3.31%，週二從較低基期大幅反彈。東證股價指數(TOPIX)早盤上漲約1.6%，漲幅小於日經。東京股市上週五收盤早於當天美股交易，週二開市時，投資人一併消化美股上週五急跌及本週一強彈。韓股週一則已承受上一個美股交易日的賣壓，KOSPI收在4,708.54點。兩地前一交易日的基期不同，影響週二早盤漲幅的比較。

輝達共同創辦人黃仁勳(Jensen Huang)重返執行長職位，帶動輝達週一股價飆漲31.48%，費城半導體指數勁揚14.03%，那指大漲6.51%。日本半導體設備股成為早盤焦點，晶片測試設備商愛德萬測試(Advantest)上週五已重挫10.32%，收在24,255日圓。

news.Title: AMD registers up to 337 million shares for resale tied to OpenAI, Meta warrants
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Advanced Micro Devices Inc (NASDAQ:AMD) filed a Form S-3 registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday to register up to 336,934,324 shares of common stock for potential future resale by existing shareholders and strategic partners. The filing accommodates stock-based consideration from recent acquisitions alongside massive performance-linked warrants held by OpenAI (NASDAQ:OAI) and Meta Platforms Inc (NASDAQ:META), though AMD itself is not selling any shares and will receive no proceeds from the transactions.

The overwhelming majority of the registered stock stems from two major commercial arrangements, with OpenAI and Meta each eligible to acquire and resell up to 160 million shares at an exercise price of $0.01 per share. Neither warrant is currently exercisable, and the underlying shares will only vest in tranches tied to substantial hardware procurement milestones and stock-price appreciation.

For both OpenAI and Meta, initial share vesting requires the delivery or shipment of an initial one gigawatt equivalent of AMD Instinct GPU products, including AMD Instinct MI450 Series hardware for OpenAI. Full vesting of the 160 million shares for each partner is contingent upon cumulative purchases reaching six gigawatts, alongside the fulfillment of technical conditions and AMD share-price targets that escalate to $600 per share for the final tranche.

The selling stockholder roster features several prominent institutional investors, venture capital firms, and technology peers that held stakes in World Labs or Taalas prior to their acquisitions. Notable names listed in the prospectus include entities affiliated with Andreessen Horowitz, Fidelity funds, BlackRock, Inc., NVIDIA Corporation, Autodesk, Inc., and Cisco Investments LLC.

news.Title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 23: Micron Surges 19% as Nvidia CEO Change Calms AI Spending Fears
news.Content:
Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) surged 19.04% on Monday, November 23, closing at $707.70 as semiconductor stocks staged a remarkable recovery following last week's steep sell-off. Nvidia's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO helped restore confidence across the artificial intelligence (AI) industry, while commentary from Citi suggesting concerns over AI infrastructure spending may be overblown provided additional support for memory-chip stocks. Trading volume reached 49.1 million shares, approximately 72% above its three-month daily average of 28.6 million, highlighting strong investor participation in the rebound.

How the markets moved today

Led by semiconductor stocks, Wall Street staged a broad rebound following last week's steep sell-off. The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) surged 4.74% to close at 7,238, while the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) jumped 6.51% to 24,090, reflecting a sharp improvement in investor sentiment.

The rally extended across the semiconductor industry, particularly among companies exposed to growing demand for AI infrastructure. Western Digital (NASDAQ:WDC) climbed 13.84% to $297.25, while NXP Semiconductors (NASDAQ:NXPI) gained 8.93% to $256.14. The widespread gains suggest investors are reassessing the outlook for chipmakers following a period of intense selling pressure and concerns surrounding AI-related capital spending.

What this means for investors

Micron's sharp rebound highlights the market's continued sensitivity to developments surrounding artificial intelligence infrastructure spending. Although uncertainty around Nvidia's leadership has eased, the underlying demand for advanced memory remains the more important factor for Micron's long-term outlook. As AI models become increasingly complex and data centers require greater computing capacity, demand for high-performance memory could provide a substantial growth opportunity.

However, the memory semiconductor industry remains highly cyclical, with profitability heavily influenced by supply, demand, and pricing conditions. Following Monday's 19% rally, investors should be particularly mindful of whether Micron's earnings growth can justify its valuation, especially if major technology companies begin moderating their AI capital expenditures.

Looking ahead, Micron's appearance at the UBS Global Technology and AI Conference and its December 17 earnings report will provide important opportunities to assess these risks. Investors should focus on management's commentary regarding memory pricing, production capacity, and expected demand from AI customers. Sustained pricing strength and improving profitability would provide stronger evidence that Micron's recovery is supported by fundamentals rather than simply a rebound in semiconductor stocks.

Story Continues

news.Title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 23: Markets Rebound From Correction on AI Relief Rally
news.Content:
Up 4.74% to 7,238, the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) exited correction territory in an historic rebound, while the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) surged 6.51% to 24,090 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES:^DJI) gained 3.01% to 49,595 as buyers returned ahead of the holiday week.

Today's biggest moves

Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) skyrocketed 31.48% after the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO triggered a massive relief rally, while Micron Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MU) soared 19.04% following newly secured multi-year customer agreements for memory supply and broader support from the AI trade rebound.

Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA) climbed 11.60% on progress toward commercializing autonomous driving, whereas CrowdStrike (NASDAQ:CRWD) dropped 8.92% after the market digested news of the company's acquisition of Zscaler (NASDAQ:ZS) in an all-stock, $44 billion deal.

What this means for investors

After seven straight days of losses, the S&P 500 roared back on Monday, spurred by Jensen Huang being reinstated at Nvidia. Today's dramatic move helped the index exit correction territory, as it rose by its largest amount in over a year and a half.

Jensen's return spurs stock spikes: Most AI-related stocks tied to Nvidia soared today, with Nebius (NASDAQ:NBIS), CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV), Dell (NYSE:DELL), Bloom Energy (NYSE:BE), and Lumentum (NASDAQ:LITE) all rising more than 15%.

CrowdStrike buys Zscaler: CrowdStrike dropped 9%, while Zscaler jumped 18% after the former announced it was acquiring the latter in an all-stock deal. Trading at a lofty valuation, I like CrowdStrike's decision to use its premium-priced equity to build out its cybersecurity platform. Now we need to watch for a successful integration if and when the deal closes in the second half of 2027, given the sheer size of the purchase.

Rocket Lab ends sell-off, skyrockets 9%: In a recent interview, Rocket Lab's CFO said they expect a "strong uplift in pricing within six to nine months" for its Electron launches, as SpaceX's (NASDAQ:SPCX) Falcon 9 is largely booked through late 2028 or early 2029. I think the market is rightfully optimistic about this outlook.

All in all, it was a great day for the markets and for investors, and it serves as a timely reminder of why Foolish investors focus on " time in the market rather than timing the market."

news.Title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 23: Advanced Micro Devices Climbs on AI-Chip Rebound After Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
news.Content:
Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD), an AI and CPU chips provider, closed at $453.46, up 6.85%. Shares rose after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, and investors are watching AI-chip sentiment and conference commentary.

Trading volume reached 53.0M shares, coming in about 93% above its three-month average of 27.5M shares.

How the markets moved today

S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) closed at 7,237, up 4.73%, while Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX: ^IXIC) closed at 24,090, up 6.51%. Among semiconductors and semiconductor equipment peers, Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) closed at $165.05, up 31.48%, and Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) closed at $59.66, up 16.34%, highlighting a broad AI-chip rebound.

What this means for investors

AMD was one of the many stocks that benefited from the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO. This stands in contrast to what happened Friday when AMD stock plunged on a short-seller report . The report alleged that some AMD server firmware fell into the hands of a blacklisted Chinese company.

By today, that report appeared to be forgotten. Although AMD is a major competitor to Nvidia in the data center space, it benefits indirectly as Huang's return breathes new life into the AI trade and brings stability to the semiconductor sector.

Fortunately, AMD has made technical progress to the point that it may benefit directly as well. Many industry analysts believe that AMD's MI450 series GPU (along with the MI455X Helios rack) has, at least on paper, caught up to Nvidia's latest release, the Vera Rubin.

Admittedly, at a P/E ratio of 98, the tech stock remains far more expensive than Nvidia, which, even with its gains today, trades at just 18 times earnings. However, analysts forecast that AMD's revenue will grow at 51% annually this year, then rise to 84% in 2027.

Amid a reinvigorated AI trade, such growth gives investors all the more reason to take a closer look at AMD stock.

news.Title: Why Marvell Technology Stock Crushed it Today
news.Content:
If anything, Monday will go down in history as the day when a high-profile tech company CEO was reinstated at the company he helped found. It also marks the day when stocks associated with that company saw double-digit bounces -- case in point, Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL), whose stock closed that trading session more than 18% higher.

A high-profile return

That prodigal CEO is none other than Nvidia 's (NASDAQ:NVDA) Jensen Huang. In a significant development in the saga of the artificial intelligence (AI) chip company's leader, he was reinstated as CEO Monday after stepping down over a relationship scandal that may involve state-sponsored espionage.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Although Marvell and Nvidia were rivals for quite some time despite differing business profiles, they eventually became co-dependents to a degree.

They collaborate on various facets of Nvidia's technology, to the point where Nvidia felt compelled to invest $2 billion in an equity stake in Marvell earlier this year.

Still a major player in AI

Essentially, this makes Marvell's Monday pop a sympathy rally on the Nvidia/Huang news. While I continue to feel that it's unwise to invest in a company purely on the back of good news with a peer, Nvidia's turn in the spotlight that day illustrates Marvell's prominence and importance in crucial segments of the AI chip market. Even after Monday's increase, it looks like a good play on the AI revolution.

news.Title: From Resignation to Reinstatement: Huang's Market Impact
news.Content:
Jensen Huang: The World's Most Consequential CEO

Less than two weeks ago, Nvidia ( NVDA ) founder and CEO Jensen Huang was forced to resign after multiple alleged affairs came to light. Before Huang's departure, he was seen as the most important CEO in the world. Huang came up with the idea to start a chip company more than three decades ago while sitting in a "Denny's" booth. With intense competition and little in cash, Nvidia nearly went bankrupt. However, the company's chips found their niche serving the video game space. Later, Nvidia's GPUs kicked off the AI revolution thanks to their rare combination of massive parallel processing, specialized AI hardware, high-speed networking, and a dominant ecosystem.

Simply put, without Nvidia, the AI ecosystem as we know it would be completely different. OpenAI, which started the AI revolution with its groundbreaking "ChatGPT" large language model, leveraged Nvidia GPUs to train its model. Following Huang's departure, Nvidia dropped more than 40%, erasing more than $1 trillion in market value in a handful of weeks. On Monday, Huang was reinstated, and Nvidia recovered ~$1 trillion in a single session.

Image Source: TradingView

Who Benefits from Jensen Huang's Return?

As the market showed, Jensen Huang's status as the "godfather of the advanced AI chip" cannot be overstated. Below are some of the beneficiaries of Huang's return:

· U.S. Investors: Without the AI boom, the U.S. economy would likely be in a recession. As the main chip supplier of the AI boom and one of the largest companies on Wall Street, a healthy Nvidia is integral to a strong U.S. economy and stock market.

· The AI Ecosystem: Beyond its best-in-class chips, Nvidia is key to the health of the AI industry as a whole. Nvidia has become known as the "AI central bank" due its numerous AI investments, equity stakes, infrastructure commitments, and vendor financing commitments. AI infrastructure players like Micron ( MU ), Nebius Group ( NBIS ), Taiwan Semiconductor ( TSM ), and Dell Technologies ( DELL ) are clear winners.

· Nvidia Investors: Although new CEOs can have succeeded in running a public company, history shows that founder-led companies outperform dramatically in the long term. In the case of Nvidia, this phenomenon is likely even more pronounced due to the complexity and expertise needed to run it.

Who Loses from Jensen Huang's Return?

Although far more parties benefit from Huang's return, there are some clear losers, including:

· China/Huawei: The AI race between the U.S. and China will likely determine which country has the most power and influence over the next decade. With Huang's return China losses for two reasons: First, rules for sending Nvidia's sought-after chips will likely be tightened, making it more difficult for Chinese companies to train their AI models. Second,Huawei, one of China's largest tech companies, will have a much harder time catching up to Nvidia with Huang at the helm.

Story Continues

· Closed-Source Models: Before his forced resignation, Jensen Huangwas making a major push into open-source models with its "Nemotron" ecosystem. Huang has also made several investments into open-source AI companies. Low-cost or free open-source AI models threaten closed-source AI model operators such as OpenAI and Anthropic ( ANT ). While the Nasdaq gained nearly 7% today, Anthropic exhibited relative weakness and closed the session in the red.

· Late Short Sellers: Until Monday morning, the chances of a Jensen Huang return as CEO seemed slim. As such, short sellers piled into the stock. Nvidia short sellers suffered losses of more than $12 billion after Monday's rally.

Bottom Line

Jensen Huang's sudden exit and swift reinstatement underscore how closely the global AI trade, infrastructure supply chains, and major equity benchmarks are tied to his leadership at Nvidia.

news.Title: ASML Stock’s Sell-Off Looks Excessive Against Its Growth Outlook
news.Content: ASML Holding's (ASML) stock sell-off looks excessive against its growth outlook, in my view. The lithography equipment manufacturer reported record quarterly sales of €11.7 billion in Q3 2026. During the earnings call, CEO Christophe Fouquet said planned supply for 2027 and 2028 "will not fully meet the demand of our customers." That is a striking message during a semiconductor sell-off. While investors are questioning how long the artificial intelligence (AI) buildout can last, ASML's customers are already asking for more equipment years ahead. Given that disconnect, I think the decline offers an unusually attractive entry point. Thus, my rating on ASML stock is a Buy . The Sell-Off Overlooks ASML's Position The ongoing, brutal market sell-off likely overlooks ASML's position within semiconductor manufacturing. Investors worry that enormous AI spending could produce disappointing returns. Possible data-center overbuilding and tighter export controls have only added to the pressure. As a result, ASML has been caught squarely in the broader sector retreat, pushing the stock 32% below its 52-week high . Promotion BLACK FRIDAY SALE Get 75% Off TipRanks Premium and unlock powerful investing tools to make smarter, more confident investment decisions Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter , and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks Learn more about TipRanks Premium I believe these concerns deserve attention. However, what the market fails to see is that ASML has more protection than many individual chip companies. ASML is the only manufacturer of Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography systems, which print the finest features on advanced chips. That monopoly insulates the company from the fierce competition among chip designers. Nvidia (NVDA) could lose share to AMD (AMD) or a hyperscaler's custom processor. However, the manufacturers producing those competing chips would still need ASML's equipment. Increasing chip complexity also means more lithography work. The eventual winner among chip designers matters less than continued demand for advanced manufacturing. The most recent Q3 results supported that distinction. Net income reached €5 billion , even if that included a €500 million Mistral AI valuation gain. Gross margin exceeded guidance at 57.5%. Installed Base Management sales also beat expectations at €3.3 billion, helped by productivity upgrades. Looking further ahead, the demand picture is even stronger. Customer forecasts keep increasing, and planned supply remains insufficient for 2027 and 2028. Some customers are discussing orders for 2029 and 2030. I find those conversations more persuasive than the sector's current mood. Story Continues Growth Has Several Years to Run Importantly, growth appears to have several years to run if ASML delivers its capacity plans. Q4 guidance calls for €14.2–€15.2 billion of revenue and roughly 57% gross margins. That would be another large sequential increase. Looking ahead to 2027, Low-NA EUV capacity is almost fully covered by orders, despite a planned 30% expansion. ASML already holds substantial 2028 orders too. It is now investigating increasing 2028 capacity beyond the further 30% previously considered . Demand is rising faster than its earlier manufacturing plans allowed. Customers have also agreed to price increases for critical products. Management expects these to help revenue and margins from 2027, with the full effect starting in 2028. Underpinning that demand is the industry's move toward 2nm and smaller chips. AI processors need increasingly advanced logic, while High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) requires sophisticated DRAM manufacturing. More critical layers use EUV as chip designs become harder to produce. Deep Ultraviolet (DUV) immersion equipment remains important elsewhere in the manufacturing process. Beyond selling brand-new systems, ASML has additional levers for growth. Customers can buy upgrades that let existing machines produce more wafers. I believe that offers ASML additional revenue without waiting for an entirely new fab to open. Also, its advanced-packaging equipment creates another opportunity as manufacturers combine more components within individual products. Further out on the technology curve, High-NA EUV adds a longer-term reason for optimism. Intel (INTC) already uses it on selected layers of some 18A processors. Other customers are preparing to adopt it as their manufacturing processes advance. These transitions take time, but each adds to ASML's role in customers' roadmaps. Replacing its equipment becomes harder when production processes are developed around it. This is why I see a company helping enable the next generations of chips, with several ways to earn more as the industry advances. ASML's Valuation Looks Increasingly Attractive ASML's valuation looks increasingly attractive when I look beyond this year. Today, ASML trades at 27.32x 2026 consensus earnings per share (EPS) of $46.35 . The multiples fall to 20.05x for 2027, 14.76x for 2028, and 13.13x for 2029. Consensus expects EPS growth of roughly 36% in both 2027 and 2028, making roughly 20x next year's earnings look reasonable for that outlook. I believe ASML deserves a premium for its technological lead and long customer relationships. Its installed base also creates substantial service revenue. As a result, projected earnings growth could make today's price look inexpensive without any valuation rerating. Buybacks should help boost that per-share growth. ASML's €12 billion 2026–2028 program includes canceling shares beyond those reserved for employee plans. Management has been executing aggressively: it repurchased €4.1 billion in Q3 alone. The latest disclosed week, November 9–13, added about €443 million. That is roughly 40% above Q3's average weekly pace. Purchases were faster still during November 2–6, and I particularly like seeing substantial repurchases during the decline. Lower purchase prices allow the same spending to retire more shares. The risks still warrant our attention, though. Further China restrictions could reduce equipment sales, and customers might delay fabs. A sharper AI spending slowdown would eventually reach ASML. Increasing manufacturing capacity is costly and difficult, and a handful of major customers heavily influence demand. The current-year multiple still carries a premium. However, strong order coverage gives ASML time to grow into that valuation. I think the market is allowing too little value for its unusual visibility. Is ASML Stock a Buy? Wall Street rates ASML a Strong Buy, with six Buy ratings. The $2,504 average price target implies roughly 98% upside from its current price levels. Thus, analysts see significant upside from here despite the ongoing panic. Conclusion ASML's share price has fallen while customers continue asking for more equipment. Its moat remains intact, and capacity plans point to growth well beyond Q4. Meanwhile, with the stock trading at roughly 20x 2027 earnings and below 15x for 2028, I think the sell-off offers a compelling opportunity. Heavy buybacks only add to that appeal. news.Title: AMD’s Blockbuster Q3 Report Is Getting Lost in the Pullback
news.Content: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) delivered a blockbuster Q3 FY2026 report , but the broader pullback in semiconductor stocks is overshadowing its strong results. Revenue reached $13.4 billion, up 45% year-over-year. Growth was driven by record Data Center revenue of $8.5 billion, up 97% year-over-year on strong demand for EPYC processors and Instinct graphics processing units (GPUs). Looking ahead, management also guided Q4 2026 revenue to about $17 billion. Despite the recent sector-wide sell-off, I remain bullish on AMD stock and maintain a Buy rating, given its accelerating data center scale and management's positive outlook for Q4. For context, AMD designs and sells computer chip processors that power products like servers and personal computers (PCs). Promotion BLACK FRIDAY SALE Get 75% Off TipRanks Premium and unlock powerful investing tools to make smarter, more confident investment decisions Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter , and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks Learn more about TipRanks Premium AMD Data Center Revenue On the Q3 FY2026 earnings call, CEO Lisa Su stated the company forecasts Data Center segment revenue to be "more than 80% of our total revenue in 2027." Meanwhile, Q3 revenue was reported at $13.4 billion, up 45% year-over-year, and guidance was set at $17 billion for Q4 FY2026. Adding the first nine months' revenue of $35 billion to the $17 billion expected in Q4 puts the company on track for roughly $52 billion in FY2026. Looking ahead, the company expects total revenue to grow more than 80% in 2027, with Data Center revenue making up more than 80% of that. This implies revenue of at least $93.6 billion, including roughly $74.9 billion from data centers. To put that figure in perspective, Nvidia (NVDA) reported $107.6 billion in data center revenue in a single quarter, Q3 FY2027. AMD isn't in the same league as Nvidia, but it is trending upward and comes without all of the risks Nvidia faces going into 2027 . The company could capture market share if Nvidia loses momentum due to Jensen Huang 's departure. To support management guidance on total revenue, Su mentioned that customers such as Anthropic (ANT) and Meta (META) brought their first Helios racks online this quarter and are already running their latest models on them. The company also pointed to Meta's Muse , a consumer agentic artificial intelligence (AI) product, as an example of agentic AI growth lifting demand for its EPYC server central processing units (CPUs). This, in turn, supports the expectation that total revenue will grow as enterprise and consumer agentic AI usage increases. Data center and server refresh revenue are the underlying drivers for my bull case on AMD. Story Continues Semiconductor Sell-Off Leaves AMD Little Margin for Error According to Lisa Su, AMD's "third quarter was the largest and most profitable in our history," yet the semiconductor industry is seeing a major sell-off since its June 2026 highs. The company's stock price has fallen nearly 20% over the past five trading days , and the sentiment around semiconductors remains weak. AMD has strong fundamentals, but it has little margin for error in public markets right now. A consistent theme of risks surrounds the semiconductor and data center trade, and AMD carries them all. On cash flow, it reported free cash flow of $554 million , down from $1.5 billion in Q3 FY2025. CFO Jean Hu attributed this to working capital demands and capex, but I consider it a noteworthy risk if receivables and contracts start outgrowing sales. Equally important, the market is pricing in the political shift that occurred in the United States. Democrats won control of Congress in the midterm elections , so investors fear more regulation around data center development in the coming months. For example, Nebius (NBIS) cut its 2026 revenue outlook to the low end of the range due to third-party data center power and construction delays. If similar infrastructure bottlenecks slow customer deployments and leave AMD struggling to clear the inventory it has been building up, that could weigh on AMD's earnings per share (EPS) and revenue guidance for 2027. Lastly, Lisa Su specifically acknowledged the memory issue by stating PC sell-through "slowed late in the quarter" due to high memory and component costs. AMD is planning for PC market unit shipments to decline by a double-digit percentage in 2027. AMD Has a Proven Track Record for Hitting Expectations With the primary risks laid out, it's fair to have concerns. However, AMD has met or beaten TipRanks' earnings estimates for 16 consecutive quarters since November 1, 2022. Competition and concentration risks affect every major company in this space, but AMD has a proven track record of meeting and exceeding expectations. AMD trades at a trailing 12-month P/E of 90.73x compared to Nvidia's P/E of 13.48x . On the surface, that multiple is steep, but with management guiding revenue growth of more than 80% in 2027, I expect it to grow into it over the long term. AMD ended Q3 with $15.8 billion in cash and short-term investments, up from $10.6 billion at the end of FY2025, with its total principal debt at $7.1 billion. For further context, its debt-to-market cap is around 1% while the semiconductor sector average sits at 2.58%. Backed by a healthy net cash position and a clear path to revenue acceleration, AMD is well positioned to capitalize on its infrastructure investments and the next wave of consumer AI applications. AMD on Wall Street Turning to Wall Street, AMD has a Strong Buy consensus rating, based on 28 Buy ratings, three Hold ratings, and zero Sell ratings. AMD's average price target of $652.26 represents 53.69% upside potential over the current price of $424.39 for the next 12 months. The Bottom Line The recent sell-off has AMD down nearly 20% in five trading days, but this is the same company that just reported the largest quarter in its history. Although a trailing P/E of 90.73x leaves little room for error, its balance sheet gives it some room to ride out weaker cash flow and regulatory uncertainty. Based on management's guidance and the underlying fundamentals, I remain bullish on AMD over the long term, and I think the average analyst price target on Wall Street is within reach. news.Title: Nvidia soars 31% as board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, chip stocks jump
news.Content:
Chip giant Nvidia ( NVDA ) stock soared 31% on Monday after the board of the AI chip giant reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. Other AI infrastructure names also bounced following Huang's surprise return.

President Trump publicly called on the board of the AI chip heavyweight to reinstate Huang.

Follow live updates and reactions to Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO >

Shares of peers AMD ( AMD ) and Broadcom ( AVGO ) also rebounded 6% and 3%, respectively, following a brutal sell-off last week.

news.Title: Is AMD's Stock in Trouble After a Concerning Short-Seller Report?
news.Content:
A short-seller report can be devastating for a stock. Even if it's untrue or full of misinformation, it can strike fear into investors and send a stock reeling.

Last week, shares of Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) fell amid a short-seller report, which called into question its ties to a Chinese company, IEIT Systems. Ties to China are a sensitive issue in light of Nvidia's recent controversy involving CEO Jensen Huang and a possible spy. That led Huang to resign from the company, although he would end up being reinstated.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

AMD is up big this year, but does this short-seller report give investors reason to dump the stock before it's too late?

Image source: Getty Images.

Allegations are concerning, but unproven

Hunterbrook Media, which has a short position in AMD and thus stands to benefit from its decline in price, claims that the tech company "bills over 20% of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong." It also states that a blacklisted Chinese company, IEIT Systems, has been gaining access to newer AMD firmware, which is needed to run AMD's chips.

AMD has dismissed the allegations of any wrongdoing, stating that it is in compliance with U.S. export laws, which impose significant restrictions on the type of chips and technology that can be sent to China.

The key, however, is whether any products were sold to Chinese customers that violated U.S. export law, and as long as that hasn't been the case, and at this point there's no reason to believe it is, then there's no reason for investors to worry about references to Chinese customers.

AMD's revenue totaled $34.6 billion in its most recent fiscal year, and of that tally, more than 22% was related to customers in China (including Hong Kong). Sales to China aren't on their own a reason for investors to worry about AMD's stock.

Should investors buy the dip on AMD stock?

AMD's stock has been falling in recent weeks, and it's now down more than 30% from its 52-week high of over $658. The stock, however, isn't cheap, trading at close to 100 times its trailing earnings.

At a time when market conditions may not be ideal for the tech sector, with interest rates potentially rising higher next month, there could be more bearish activity ahead for AMD and the broader tech market.

Story Continues

For investors who are willing to hang on for the long haul (e.g., five-plus years), AMD may be worth buying given its strong position in the chip market. In the short run, however, this could be a risky stock to own, as there may be plenty of room for it to fall lower given its high price tag today.

news.Title: Apple vs. Broadcom: Comparing Revenue Trends Amid the Artificial Intelligence Boom
news.Content:
Apple: Seasonal Revenue Spikes

Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) makes mobile phones, computers, and tablets for consumers, businesses, and schools. It released the Apple HomeView smart display on Nov. 13.

The consumer electronics giant's top line exhibits sharp quarterly seasonality tied to consumer hardware cycles. Apple tends to release new products in the fall, timed to capture holiday shopping demand. That's why its revenue soars in the fourth quarter.

Broadcom: Consistent Quarterly Revenue Growth

Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) makes semiconductor components and infrastructure software for enterprise networking. It announced an agreement with NTT -owned DOCOMO on Oct. 20, and launched Arcot Scam Defense on Oct. 21.

Broadcom posted positive quarter-over-quarter revenue growth in every quarter over the past two years. That increase is accelerating in fiscal 2026, reflecting secular enterprise and hyperscaler AI infrastructure demand.

Why Revenue Matters for Investors

Revenue represents the total money brought in by sales before any expenses are deducted. Closely tracking this top-line financial figure helps investors understand the total scale and growth trajectory of a business.

Foolish Take

Apple and Broadcom's revenue trends over the past two years reveal a sharp contrast between the former's consumer-driven seasonal cycles and the latter's rapid, uninterrupted sequential compounding fueled by the rise of artificial intelligence .

In fact, AI has become a key factor in both companies, with Apple signing a multiyear commitment with Broadcom exceeding $30 billion through 2031 to secure custom AI server silicon, wireless and radio frequency components, and semiconductor chips manufactured domestically. Apple intends to use Broadcom's server chip to power Apple Intelligence cloud servers, the retailer's proprietary AI offering.

Story Continues

Apple's revenue trend shows a pronounced increase in 2026 over 2025, thanks to the release of popular new products such as its foldable iPhone Duo. This was further helped by the company's hardware-plus-services flywheel, where customers buy a product, then sign up for additional subscription services such as Apple's cloud storage.

Broadcom is displaying unbroken quarterly sales growth, illustrating the strong demand for its AI solutions. Its compounding top line is driven by custom AI accelerators, data center networking chips, and high-margin infrastructure software. However, investors face higher customer concentration risk. The company's top five customers account for about 40% of revenue, with Apple alone representing roughly 20% of Broadcom's annual sales.

news.Title: How to Play AMD Stock as Hunterbrook Slams the Company With a New Short Report
news.Content:
Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) is facing a fresh test of investor confidence after short seller Hunterbrook Media published a new report raising concerns about the chipmaker's China exposure and potential export-control risks. Hunterbrook alleges that newer versions of AMD's firmware continued to appear in updates from IEIT Systems, a Chinese server maker added to the U.S. Commerce Department's Entity List in 2025. Moreover, Hunterbrook Capital disclosed that it is short AMD, while AMD has pushed back, saying the claims misrepresent its business practices and relationships and that it complies with applicable U.S. export-control laws.

The report triggered a sharp selloff, with AMD shares falling 7.7% on Nov. 19 and another 13.3% on Nov. 20 amid a broader artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor rout. The timing is significant because AMD had just delivered a record third quarter, and now the question is whether Hunterbrook's allegations represent a material threat to AMD's AI growth story or create a potentially attractive entry point after the selloff.

More News from Barchart

Dear Dollar Tree Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 24

Leadership Risk vs. Record Numbers: Nvidia Posted $115 Billion in Revenue in Its First Report Without Jensen Huang. What It Means for NVDA Stock.

AMD vs. Nvidia Stock After Jensen Huang's Exit: 1 Trades at Nearly 4x the Other's Earnings Multiple. Here's the AI Chip Stock I'd Buy Now.

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

About Advanced Micro Devices Stock

Advanced Micro Devices is a Santa Clara, California, based fabless semiconductor firm, known for high-performance computing solutions, including its Ryzen, EPYC, Threadripper, Radeon, and Instinct product lines. Since its founding, AMD has evolved into a major player in CPUs, GPUs, adaptive SoCs, FPGAs, and AI accelerators. AMD's market cap currently stands at around $760.3 billion, placing it among the top semiconductor firms globally.

AMD stock has delivered extraordinary gains over the past year, but the momentum has taken a sharp turn in November. Shares are up 122% over the past 52 weeks and 112% year-to-date (YTD), underscoring how strongly investors had positioned the chipmaker as a major beneficiary of the AI infrastructure boom. However, AMD has plunged 12% over the past month, with the latest selloff pushing the stock to $424.39 on Nov. 20, well below its Oct. 6 52-week high of $658.52.

The recent weakness reflects a combination of company-specific and broader market pressures rather than a deterioration in AMD's underlying growth story alone. The selloff accelerated after the Hunterbrook Media report was published on Nov. 19.

Story Continues

The latest leg lower also came amid a broader technology selloff and concerns surrounding AI-related stocks, meaning the decline cannot be attributed entirely to the short report. However, it remains to be seen whether the pullback represents a temporary sentiment-driven correction or the beginning of a deeper reset in expectations. Even now, AMD stock has already started seeing green on the price chart as the broader market rebounds today.

AMD stock is currently priced at 70.62 times forward earnings, trading at a lofty valuation compared to the sector median.

Better-Than-Expected Financial Performance

AMD's third-quarter 2026 results, released Nov. 3, after the market close, showed that the company's AI-driven growth remained exceptionally strong despite growing concerns around valuation and the broader semiconductor market. AMD reported record quarterly revenue of $13.4 billion, up 45% year-over-year (YoY). The company also exceeded the high end of its prior revenue guidance.

Profitability improved even faster than revenue as non-GAAP gross profit increased 50% to $7.5 billion, while adjusted gross margin expanded to 56% from 54%. Non-GAAP operating income jumped 75% to $3.9 billion, with operating margin rising to 29% from 24%. Non-GAAP net income climbed 77% to $3.5 billion, and adjusted EPS increased 74% to $2.09 from $1.20 a year earlier and topped expectations. The faster growth in earnings than revenue highlights the operating leverage AMD is generating as its higher-margin AI and Data Center products scale.

The biggest driver was Data Center, where revenue nearly doubled. Data Center revenue surged 97% YoY to a record $8.5 billion, driven by strong demand for EPYC processors and AMD Instinct GPUs, including the launch of the MI450 series. Data Center operating income climbed to $2.9 billion from $1.1 billion, reflecting the substantial improvement in profitability accompanying the revenue growth.

Outside Data Center, the picture was more mixed. Client revenue increased 7% YoY to $2.9 billion, helped by Ryzen mobile processors, while Gaming revenue fell 40% to $773 million, reflecting lower semi-custom and graphics revenue, and the combined Client and Gaming segment declined 8% YoY to $3.7 billion. Embedded revenue was a brighter spot, rising 29% to $1.1 billion.

AMD also provided an aggressive fourth-quarter outlook. For Q4 2026, management expects revenue of $17 billion, plus or minus 3%, implying roughly 66% YoY growth at the midpoint and a 27% sequential increase from Q3. The company expects non-GAAP gross margin of approximately 55%. Management said accelerating Data Center demand, including the scaling of its Helios platform and Venice products, should support the stronger fourth-quarter performance.

Meanwhile, as per consensus, its EPS is expected to rise by 111.9% YoY to $6.93 in fiscal 2026, before improving by around 131.5% annually to reach $16.04 in fiscal 2027.

Analysts Are Optimistic About AMD Stock

Oppenheimer turned more bullish on AMD after the chipmaker's strong third-quarter performance, upgrading the stock to "Outperform" from "Perform" on Nov. 9 and assigning a $600 price target.

Moreover, William Blair upgraded AMD to "Outperform" from "Market Perform" this month, arguing that the factors that had previously weighed on its rating have improved materially.

AMD stock has a consensus "Strong Buy" rating overall. Out of 48 analysts covering the semiconductor stock, 39 recommend a "Strong Buy," two give a "Moderate Buy," and seven analysts stay cautious with a "Hold" rating.

Its average analyst price target of $661.82 suggests an upside of 47%. The Street-high target price of $1,250 indicates as much as 177% upside ahead.

news.Title: 抱著怕跌 賣了怕漲！輝達暴漲逾30% 揭美股投資人兩難
news.Content: 據《彭博》周一(23日)報導，黃仁勳回歸輝達(NVDA-US)，帶動股價暴漲逾30%，也凸顯美股投資人日益難解的兩難：減碼科技巨頭，可以在市場重挫時降低損失，卻可能在同一批股票反彈時，錯過漲勢、落後大盤。 十大成分股占六成權重 科技巨頭左右指數漲跌 截至紐約周一中午12時30分，光是輝達一檔股票，就貢獻羅素1000成長指數當日漲幅的逾四成，以及那斯達克100指數漲幅的約四分之一。然而，就在幾天前，輝達仍是長達六周拋售潮的焦點之一，那斯達克100指數也一度逼近熊市。 這種急跌急漲，放大了基金經理人長期面對的問題：持有較少科技巨頭股票，有助於在跌市中守住績效，但當巨頭重新領漲，較分散的投資組合又容易跟不上。 《彭博》彙整數據顯示，截至10月底，羅素1000成長指數前十大成分股合計權重高達60%，是過去30年中位數的兩倍，輝達單獨就占15%。 在該指數跌入修正區間的一段期間，近半數成分股其實仍然上漲，卻抵不過少數大型權值股下跌的拖累。 Bridgeway Capital Management共同投資長Jacob Pozharny指出，過度集中於單一產業或次產業，會讓個別股票遭遇的衝擊被放大，並擴散至其他公司，輝達就是一個例子。 分散持股能抗跌 反彈時卻容易落後大盤 主動型基金與指數之間的持股差距，也愈拉愈大。彭博行業研究分析師David Cohne指出，10月底大型成長型基金平均將40%的資金配置於羅素指數前十大成分股，較指數本身低約20個百分點，差距比去年再擴大約5個百分點。 Cohne認為，這未必代表經理人對科技巨頭缺乏信心，而是指數集中程度太高。主動型基金通常維持較分散的配置，即使已大量持有這些股票，相較於指數仍可能明顯減碼；部分基金也受到分散投資規範限制，難以完全跟隨巨頭權重。 今年大型股下跌，確實讓主動型經理人獲得展現選股能力的機會。高盛(GS-US)彙整數據顯示，今年以來超過80%的大型成長型基金擊敗基準指數，表現為十多年來最佳。但若拉長觀察期間，能夠勝出的基金僅約三分之一。 對主動型經理人而言，追上指數與控制集中風險之間的拉扯仍未解決。Vaughan Nelson副投資長Adam Rich形容，這是非常棘手的局面：「光是為了跟上表現，就得違背自己原本努力堅持的投資原則。」 科技新股接力上市 集中風險恐進一步升高 未來，這道難題還可能更加棘手。SpaceX(SPCX-US)與Anthropic(ANT-US)已相繼上市，OpenAI也可能接棒，讓成長型指數更加仰賴AI相關企業的表現。 關鍵在於可供市場交易的股份。多數主要股票指數依自由流通市值決定權重，Anthropic上市初期可交易股份有限，OpenAI未來也可能如此。隨著員工與上市前股東的閉鎖期屆滿、更多股份可以交易，這些公司的指數權重也可能提高。 依羅素投資一項情境推估，到2028年初，Anthropic、OpenAI與SpaceX合計可能占成長型指數的6%至8%。相較之下，目前該指數規模最小的255家成分股，合計權重也只有約6%。 羅素投資資深投資分析師Zoe Tan指出，指數表現可能愈來愈取決於少數AI企業及其共同驅動因素，其他公司與產業的相對影響力則被壓縮。因此，投資人需要重新檢視，基準指數所代表的配置，是否仍符合投資組合目標與可承擔風險。

news.Title: Is Micron Technology Stock a Buy at $700?
news.Content:
The stock market has been volatile in recent weeks, with many tech stocks putting shareholders on a roller-coaster ride. Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU), which once traded at over $1,200 at its peak, recently fell below $600. But with Nvidia announcing the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday, that has sparked a rally in the markets, and Micron has gone along for the ride.

Now back up to around $700, Micron's stock looks set to head higher again. Is it a buy right now?

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Micron.

The stock is likely to continue to move with the broader tech sector

Micron's business has been on fire; there's no doubt about that given its impressive results. In its most recent quarter, for the period ending Sept. 3, its revenue totaled $54.2 billion, up nearly five times from the $11.3 billion it reported a year ago. For this type of growth, investors would likely be paying far more than just the 10 times trailing earnings it's trading at right now.

But the reason the market is demanding a discount is the uncertainty relating to the memory shortage and how long it will last. This is why I expect Micron's stock will ultimately depend on the outlook for the memory market, which, in turn, will reflect the overall sentiment in the tech sector .

If demand is expected to remain robust across all things tech-related, the outlook for memory and storage products will be similar.

Micron is largely a speculative investment at this stage

What makes it difficult to invest in Micron is that its earnings multiples are not all that helpful to investors. Otherwise, the stock would be a no-brainer buy given its growth, to be trading at such a low earnings multiple. Instead, there's been apprehension around the stock due to concerns about its future growth and question marks about the memory shortage and whether prices will come down in the near future, impacting Micron's growth prospects.

It also doesn't help that historically, the market for memory and storage products has been cyclical. Bullish investors may be tempted to believe that this time things are different because of artificial intelligence, but bearish investors may have a much more cautious outlook and consider the industry's past volatility.

Due to the uncertainty around Micron's future, I wouldn't buy it even at its reduced valuation . There's still ample risk here. Investors who buy the stock should expect continued volatility, as its erratic price movements over the past few weeks highlight just how risky the stock can be, even though it may appear cheap.

news.Title: Billionaire Ray Dalio Is Going All-In on AI and Chip Stocks: Top 5 Holdings
news.Content:
Speaking at the Forbes Global CEO Conference in Singapore on October 7, Ray Dalio was of the opinion that the AI boom had entered a "classic bubble," and that there was a distinction between "how terrific a technology is and how terrific an investment is." Gain insight into the AI sector through our list of the AI Stocks Dominating List of Biggest Winners .

He further told the Forbes event that the changing circumstances and rising rates had not yet resulted in "a negative effect on other things", but that, at the same time, it does not elevate the pressure for interest rates to balloon even further. He said the AI bubble could begin to burst once higher borrowing costs started having an impact, adding that he believed markets were approaching that point.

READ ALSO: Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller's New AI Warning and Top 10 Stock Picks

Dalio has been developing this argument throughout 2026. In January, he warned that the AI boom was in the early stages of a bubble, after a prolonged rally in technology stocks. His broader concerns extended to the uncertainty surrounding Fed policy and productivity growth, adding that he believed the newly appointed Fed chair and FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) at the time were likely to be biased to push nominal and real interest rates down. This, according to him, could be supportive of prices and inflate bubbles. For more insight, read our recently published article on the top 10 stocks to buy according to billionaire Ken Fisher .

But Dalio is far from dismissing AI's economic promise. In a September discussion published by the World Economic Forum, he argued that both the optimists and pessimists could be right. He believes that AI is following the same path as other transformative technologies throughout history, ranging from railroads to the internet, as they all tend to produce bubbles. AI is no different from them, according to Ray, and how the technology is managed by societies would eventually help determine how the advantages and disadvantages are shared.

So, what are the best AI and chip stocks billionaire Ray Dalio is going all-in on? We provided the expanded list of the top 10 holdings here . The top 5 stocks are provided below.

Our Methodology

Why are we interested in the stocks that hedge funds pile into? NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) remains one of the most direct ways for investors to gain exposure to the expansion of AI computing infrastructure. Its accelerated computing platforms support the training and deployment of sophisticated AI models, while its networking technologies and software contribute to the broader systems used in data centers.

The company's November 17, 2026 earnings release revealed the extraordinary scale of demand. Third-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue reached $115.8 billion, up 103% year over year, while Data Center revenue rose 110% to $107.6 billion. The larger investment opportunity extends beyond supplying individual processors. NVIDIA's strategy encompasses integrated computing systems designed to address the demanding performance requirements of increasingly complex AI applications. For investors, NVIDIA's ability to maintain its technological advantage and generate attractive margins will matter just as much as the overall growth of the AI infrastructure market.

Analyst Upside: 69.65%

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 129

Applied Materials, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMAT) is positioned to benefit from the increasing sophistication of semiconductor manufacturing. Its equipment and technologies support the production of advanced chips, making it an important supplier as manufacturers invest in more capable processors and memory.

The company's fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 results demonstrated strong demand for its technologies. Revenue increased 53% year over year to $10.41 billion, while fiscal 2026 revenue reached a record $34.45 billion, up 21% year over year. Its quarterly GAAP gross margin stood at 50.4%. Applied Materials also generated $8.87 billion in operating cash flow during the fiscal year, giving investors another measure of the financial performance supporting its semiconductor equipment operations.

The company's strength lies in the range of manufacturing processes its products address. Rather than depending on a single chip architecture, Applied Materials supplies technologies used across different stages of semiconductor production, and this creates exposure to increasingly complex manufacturing requirements, although it does not eliminate the industry's cyclicality.

Capital investment by semiconductor manufacturers remains an important determinant of equipment demand. The central issue for shareholders is whether technology-driven spending can sustain profitable growth beyond periods of especially strong equipment investment.

Lam Research Corporation (NASDAQ:LRCX) supplies semiconductor manufacturing equipment used in processes such as deposition and etching. Its technologies are important to producing increasingly complex chips, including the advanced logic and memory devices used in AI computing systems.

Lam's September-quarter 2026 results demonstrated substantial operating momentum, with revenue increasing to $8.22 billion, up 22% from the preceding quarter. Lam's opportunity is not limited to an increase in the number of chips manufactured. As semiconductor technology becomes more complex, production can require increasingly demanding manufacturing processes, creating opportunities for specialized equipment suppliers.

Lam's exposure to memory manufacturing also connects its business to the investment required to produce more sophisticated memory devices. Nevertheless, semiconductor equipment spending remains cyclical, and changes in manufacturers' capacity plans can affect orders even when the long-term demand for computing continues to expand.

For investors, Lam's ability to support advanced manufacturing requirements while preserving operating profitability will be central to the company's longer-term investment case.

2. ASML Holding N.V. (NASDAQ: ASML )

Analyst Upside: 76.41%

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 125

ASML Holding N.V. (NASDAQ:ASML) occupies an important position in the semiconductor supply chain because its extreme ultraviolet lithography systems enable the production of advanced chips. As demand for increasingly powerful AI processors grows, the technical complexity of chip manufacturing makes ASML's equipment particularly significant.

The company's third-quarter 2026 results reflected strong demand. In its October 2026 earnings release, ASML said customer demand was exceeding its planned supply capacity for both 2027 and 2028. Management is consequently exploring additional capacity increases to meet demand. Total net sales for the quarter reached €11.7 billion, with a gross margin of 57.5%. The company now expects full-year 2026 total net sales to be in the €44 billion to €45 billion range, with a gross margin around 56%.

ASML's competitive advantage lies in the advanced technology and specialized expertise required to manufacture its lithography systems. Its business also benefits from servicing and upgrading equipment already installed at customer facilities, providing a revenue opportunity beyond new system sales.

However, ASML is exposed to semiconductor manufacturers' capital spending decisions. The important factor for investors to consider is whether the increasingly demanding manufacturing requirements of advanced semiconductors can sustain equipment demand through the industry's cyclical fluctuations.

1. Micron Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: MU )

Analyst Upside: 128.12%

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 169

Micron Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ:MU) offers exposure to an essential part of AI computing that receives less attention than processors: memory. High-performance computing systems require substantial memory capacity and bandwidth, making advanced memory technologies important to the operation of AI infrastructure.

The company's fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 results showed revenue increasing to $54.23 billion from $11.32 billion a year earlier, while operating cash flow reached $43.97 billion. Management highlighted AI-related demand and its plans to increase investment in technology, products, and manufacturing capacity. These investments are intended to support the evolving requirements of customers developing advanced computing platforms.

The company's advanced DRAM and high-bandwidth memory products place it within an important part of the AI supply chain. Reuters reported in September that Micron has increased commitments under its long-term supply agreements to $32 billion, which highlights the demand for AI memory chips. news.Title: Billionaire Ray Dalio Is Going All-In on These 10 AI and Chip Stocks: Should You Buy?
news.Content: Speaking at the Forbes Global CEO Conference in Singapore on October 7, Ray Dalio was of the opinion that the AI boom had entered a "classic bubble," and that there was a distinction between "how terrific a technology is and how terrific an investment is." Gain insight into the AI sector through our list of the AI Stocks Dominating List of Biggest Winners . He further told the Forbes event that the changing circumstances and rising rates had not yet resulted in "a negative effect on other things", but that, at the same time, it does not elevate the pressure for interest rates to balloon even further. He said the AI bubble could begin to burst once higher borrowing costs started having an impact, adding that he believed markets were approaching that point. READ ALSO: Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller's New AI Warning and Top 10 Stock Picks Dalio has been developing this argument throughout 2026. In January, he warned that the AI boom was in the early stages of a bubble, after a prolonged rally in technology stocks. His broader concerns extended to the uncertainty surrounding Fed policy and productivity growth, adding that he believed the newly appointed Fed chair and FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) at the time were likely to be biased toward pushing nominal and real interest rates down. This, according to him, could be supportive of prices and inflate bubbles. For more insight, read our recently published article on the top 10 stocks to buy according to billionaire Ken Fisher . But Dalio is far from dismissing AI's economic promise. In a September discussion published by the World Economic Forum, he argued that both the optimists and pessimists could be right. He believes that AI is following the same path as other transformative technologies throughout history, ranging from railroads to the internet, as they all tend to produce bubbles. AI is no different from them, according to Ray, and how the technology is managed by societies would eventually help determine how the advantages and disadvantages are shared. So, what are the best AI and chip stocks billionaire Ray Dalio is going all-in on? We provided the expanded list of the top 10 holdings here . Down below, we look at the stocks that rank 10th to 6th. Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ: MSFT ) Analyst Upside: 27.13% Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 300 Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) has positioned Azure at the center of its AI strategy, combining cloud infrastructure with enterprise applications and AI services. The company's ability to integrate AI across its existing products gives it multiple potential sources of demand, although the infrastructure required to deliver those services carries substantial costs. Microsoft reported fiscal first-quarter 2027 revenue of $92.3 billion, an increase of 19% year over year. Microsoft Cloud revenue grew 30% to $63.9 billion, while Azure revenue climbed 48%. Its commercial remaining performance obligation increased 73% to $677 billion. Microsoft also generated $18.6 billion in free cash flow despite substantial infrastructure investments, exceeding analyst expectations by around $10 billion, according to Reuters. Management also expects Azure revenue growth of 49%–50% in the following quarter, which exceeds analyst estimates ​of 47.6%, according to Reuters. 9. Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMZN ) Analyst Upside: 28.22% Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 366 Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) has an increasingly significant AI opportunity through Amazon Web Services. AWS provides computing infrastructure for enterprises and technology companies, allowing Amazon to participate in the growing demand for cloud-based AI workloads. Amazon's third-quarter 2026 results highlighted the strength of its cloud business. AWS net sales increased 39.3% year over year, marking its fastest growth rate in nearly five years, and reached an annualized revenue run rate of approximately $184 billion. READ ALSO: 10 Stocks With Easy 15-38% Gains The AWS segment also generated $17.8 billion in quarterly operating income, compared with $11.4 billion a year earlier. These figures show that AWS's expansion is contributing substantial operating profits alongside its revenue growth. Amazon has opportunities to serve customers developing AI applications while providing the storage, computing, and supporting services those applications require. However, the company must balance additional capacity investment against the revenue and operating profits generated by customers using that capacity. The performance of AWS remains a key factor in evaluating Amazon's long-term growth potential alongside its much larger retail operations. 8. Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) Analyst Upside: 42.42% Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 264 Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL) has several potential avenues for turning AI investment into revenue. Beyond its established advertising operations, the company is expanding Google Cloud, developing its Gemini models, and investing in specialized computing infrastructure. Google Cloud's operating income more than tripled to $11.12 billion in the September 2026 quarter, as revenue increased by a record 103% to $30.71 billion, supported by solid growth in Google Cloud Platform across enterprise AI solutions and enterprise AI infrastructure, along with core GCP services. These developments provide evidence of commercial demand alongside Alphabet's substantial infrastructure investment. The company is also developing its own tensor processing units, giving it additional flexibility in how it supplies and deploys computing capacity. ACCESS NOW: 10 Fastest-Growing AI Stocks to Buy Now However, management reported that third-quarter capital expenditure was $51.4 billion, and negative free cash flow reached $9.1 billion, which was driven by its investments in CapEx. The long-term investment case therefore depends on whether the company's expanding cloud and AI operations can deliver sufficient returns on the capital required to support their growth, while its core advertising businesses remain competitive. 7. Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ: AVGO ) Analyst Upside: 50.73% Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 166 Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ:AVGO) has become an important supplier of specialized AI semiconductors and networking products. Its custom accelerator business provides exposure to customers seeking computing architectures tailored to their particular requirements, while networking technology supports communication across increasingly large AI systems. The company's fiscal third-quarter 2026 results demonstrated the scale of this opportunity, with the company reporting revenue of $29.6 billion, up 86% from the previous year. AI semiconductor revenue surged 221% year over year to $16.7 billion, reflecting strong demand for custom accelerators and networking products. Broadcom also generated $13.7 billion in quarterly free cash flow, demonstrating its ability to convert substantial revenue into cash while continuing to serve expanding infrastructure markets. Custom silicon allows customers to optimize hardware for particular workloads, potentially creating long-term opportunities for suppliers with the necessary design expertise. Nevertheless, investors need to keep in mind that maintaining growth will require both sustained demand for custom AI computing and continued execution in an increasingly competitive semiconductor market. 6. The company's power generation and electrification businesses supply equipment and services used to produce electricity and expand power networks, capabilities that are increasingly relevant as data centers place greater demands on energy infrastructure. Its third-quarter 2026 results demonstrated strong underlying demand. GE Vernova reported orders of approximately $29 billion, revenue of $12.6 billion, and a backlog reaching $197 billion. The company also raised its 2026 financial guidance following the quarter's performance. A major attraction for investors is the breadth of the company's exposure to electricity infrastructure. Demand for new power generation capacity, grid equipment, and related services can support its operations across several different markets. READ ALSO: 10 Best Affordable Blue Chip Stocks to Buy Now However, it would be inaccurate to attribute all of GE Vernova's growth to artificial intelligence. Its customers serve a broad range of industrial and electricity needs. The company's longer-term performance will depend on its ability to execute large equipment orders, manage manufacturing capacity, and convert its growing backlog into profitable revenue. The AI opportunity adds to those existing business drivers rather than replacing them. news.Title: 《強勢美股特報》TLN,LFUS,TEX等3檔
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-24 02:04:16 數位內容中心 發佈

Talen Energy（TLN.US）： 成交價363.74美元，上漲9.26%，開盤360.61美元，盤中高點365.52美元，盤中低點353.95美元，均價361.02美元，成交量7.01萬股。

Talen Energy與一名具投資等級評級的PJM客戶簽下七年期容量合約，將在2029/2030至2035/2036各交付年度銷售750MW容量，預期每年帶來約1億美元收入，主要由Guernsey Power Station提供750MW認可容量。這筆新約的重要性，在於公司把原本受電力市場波動影響較大的獲利來源，進一步轉成可預測的長約現金流。加上先前與AWS的協議，Talen到2036年的已簽約毛利率已提高至40%，未來十年合計約有10億美元容量收入能見度。公司也另外鎖定Guernsey剩餘588MW於2029/2030年度，以及Waterford Energy Center自2029/2030至2031/2032三年共702MW容量，使2029/2030規劃年度總簽約容量超過2GW。

Littelfuse（LFUS.US）： 成交價388.07美元，上漲8.53%，開盤381.11美元，盤中高點392.22美元，盤中低點378.95美元，均價385.37美元，成交量1.72萬股。

Littelfuse最近連續推出兩條新產品線，方向都指向車用電子與空間受限的工業設備。較具代表性的是TP7.0SMD-XC車規級TVS二極體，採用Foldback技術，在小型表面貼裝封裝中提供最高7000W峰值脈衝功率，並維持24V低且平坦的箝位電壓，鎖定ADAS、區域控制單元等低耐壓敏感晶片保護需求，同時通過AEC-Q101認證並支援PPAP流程。另一項更新是C&K SDE系列薄型SMT DIP開關，主打可端對端並排擴充，最高提供12位配置，應用鎖定工業控制面板、保全消防與物聯網裝置。相較只看整體景氣，這兩項新品更直接顯示Littelfuse正把產品重心往高可靠度、車規化與小型化設計深化。

Terex（TEX.US）： 成交價54.33美元，上漲8.13%，開盤51.67美元，盤中高點54.8美元，盤中低點52.1美元，均價53.79美元，成交量9.14萬股。

Terex近期沒有新的財報、併購或重大接單公告，現有資料顯示市場判讀仍圍繞公司轉型是否能落實到獲利結構改善。較具體的觀察點，是Terex是否能達成2026年調整後EBITDA9.65億美元目標，以及把營收結構由波動較大的設備銷售，逐步轉向更穩定的業務來源。現階段外界主要檢視三件事，包括既有訂單能否持續轉成營收、併購後成本協同是否如期發揮，以及高毛利、低波動業務占比能否提高。也就是說，Terex當前最值得追蹤的變化，不是單一新消息，而是轉型進度能否把原本偏週期性的工業設備公司，推向獲利品質更穩的結構。

AI資料中心電力核准卡住，業者轉向提升場內效率並尋找昂貴過渡供電

《美股主題週報》散熱—VRT、CARR、AAON

news.Content:

Burlington Stores, Inc.（BURL.US）： 成交價238.15美元，下跌2.93%，開盤249.08美元，盤中高點249.08美元，盤中低點235.86美元，均價240.76美元，成交量42.21萬股。

Burlington正把門市與商品升級計畫推進到更仰賴後端執行的階段，近期主線集中在Store Experience2.0與Merchandising2.0兩項調整。公司不只改善門市體驗，也同步調整商品陳列與品類組合，目標是把折扣零售的流量優勢轉成更穩定的獲利結構。這套策略能否落地，關鍵不在促銷，而在供應鏈、補貨效率與跨區調度是否跟上。若配送中心效率或庫存配置失準，熱門品項缺貨與滯銷品堆積都可能侵蝕毛利率，也會削弱新門市體驗的效果。先前資料已反映公司營收年增11.3%與獲利體質改善的期待，後續更值得追蹤的是庫存品質、毛利率、同店銷售與物流效率能否同步改善，而不只是展店與營收擴張。

Pilgrim's Pride（PPC.US）： 成交價27.83美元，下跌2.69%，開盤28.1美元，盤中高點28.47美元，盤中低點27.74美元，均價28.05美元，成交量4.16萬股。

Pilgrim's Pride近期沒有公布足以改寫營運方向的新產品或重大財測，公開面較新的變化主要來自外部爭議與市場預期轉弱。美國眾議院民主黨首席議員拉斯金近期在信中點名，JBS的美國子公司Pilgrim's Pride在川普政府宣布允許最多30萬公噸、低於市場價格的牛絞肉原料進口後，曾向2024年就職基金捐贈500萬美元，相關關稅豁免程序因此遭要求徹查。另一項較直接的財務訊號是，FactSet彙整的7位分析師已把Pilgrim's Pride2026年每股盈餘預估中位數由2.48美元下修至2.36美元，2026年營收中位數為185.31億美元，顯示市場對公司後續獲利預期轉趨保守。

news.Title: Should You Buy Marvell Technology Stock Before Dec. 1?
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) reports its latest earnings numbers at the start of December, and they could be pivotal for a stock that's been volatile in recent weeks. While it's still sitting on some strong gains north of 60% this year, there has been a bit of a pullback of late as the market reacted negatively to news of its planned acquisition of Lumentum Holdings .

A good earnings report and outlook could, however, convince investors that the tech stock is on the right path forward. Should investors buy Marvell's stock before its earnings come out on Dec. 1?

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

The market may be expecting much more than just a strong quarter

Back in August, when Marvell reported its most recent numbers, its growth rate was 37%, with the company posting record revenue of more than $2.7 billion. For the current quarter, which ended on Oct. 31, Marvell forecasted around $3.2 billion in net revenue, which would translate into a year-over-year growth rate of over 50%.

Effectively, this means that type of growth is already priced into the tech stock . Unless Marvell does better than that, which may not be easy to achieve, the stock may not necessarily get much, if any, boost. Crucially, investors may be looking ahead to the guidance and how strong demand is expected to be for the next quarter.

The challenge these days is that with interest rates on the rise, there may be a bit more of a pullback in tech-related spending in the future, which, in turn, may hurt Marvell's near-term growth prospects. Investors may be looking for confidence that won't be the case. Plus, they may be looking for reasons for management to justify its all-stock deal for Lumentum, which places a massive $115 billion enterprise value on the business.

Thus far, Marvell's management hasn't appeared to have done enough to convince investors that the deal will pay off. There will likely be questions relating to the deal on the earnings call, which may have a big impact on the stock afterward.

Is Marvell's stock worth buying today?

For investors looking to buy Marvell's stock, it may be a good idea to wait until after earnings. As well as what the company does in the upcoming quarter and as rosy as its guidance may be, there's also the Fed meeting that happens a week later. An interest rate hike is widely expected, and it may be even 50 basis points. That could trigger a sharp sell-off in the tech sector, at which point Marvell may be an even more attractive buy.

Story Continues

Currently, it's trading at around 50 times its trailing earnings, which may be justifiable under ideal growth conditions. However, given the state of the economy and the possibility of a pullback in tech spending, investors may want to demand a lower price for Marvell stock before buying it. And the stock's valuation could indeed fall lower in the coming weeks; there's no rush to buy right now.

news.Title: Advanced Micro Devices vs. Dell Technologies: Comparing Revenue Trends Amid the Artificial Intelligence Boom
news.Content:
Advanced Micro Devices: Rapidly Rising Revenue in 2026

Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) makes computer processors and graphics chips. It closed the World Labs acquisition on Nov. 16, and announced a partnership with Meta Platforms on Oct. 27.

AMD's year-over-year quarterly revenue growth rate has stepped up from the low-to-mid 30% range throughout 2025 to an average of 44% across the first three quarters of 2026, with management projecting further acceleration in Q4.

Dell Technologies: Greater Absolute Revenue Totals

Dell Technologies (NYSE:DELL) makes personal computers, servers, and storage solutions. It partnered with Rackspace on Nov. 17, and collaborated with Mistral AI on Oct. 21.

Dell has seen an even sharper inflection in top-line growth across calendar 2026 as its massive AI server backlog converts into shipments. Its higher absolute revenue total is due to the company selling complete, high-ticket systems -- such as servers, data center hardware, and PCs -- whereas AMD sells individual semiconductor components that go into those systems.

Why Revenue Matters for Investors

Tracking revenue helps investors measure a company's ability to generate baseline sales before accounting for expenses. This metric reveals whether an organization is successfully attracting customers and growing its overall business volume over time.

Foolish Take

A look at the revenue trends for AMD and Dell reveal both are enjoying massive revenue boosts as the artificial intelligence boom accelerates in 2026. With the rise of AI, these companies quickly pivoted away from relying on cyclical PC markets to being anchored by enterprise and hyperscale AI infrastructure expansion.

Story Continues

Thanks to a record $95 billion server backlog, Dell raised its full-year fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $192 billion, implying approximately 69% annual growth over fiscal 2026. AMD demonstrated a steady, compounding staircase, climbing 74.7% from $7.7 billion in Q4 2024 to $13.4 billion in Q3 2026, with management guiding for roughly $17 billion in Q4 2026.

While Dell generates more than triple AMD's trailing twelve-month revenue (about $151.2 billion vs. $45.4 billion), the revenue trends highlight the difference between a systems integrator, such as Dell, and AMD's fabless chip design approach. Dell converts massive AI server backlog into high-volume revenue at roughly 21% gross margins, exposing it to component cost inflation. Conversely, AMD captures upstream silicon pricing power with 54% gross margins, meaning each incremental dollar of data center revenue flows through to operating income at a much higher rate.
