Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The Federal Open Market Committee will announce its next rate decision.

Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) reports earnings after the market closes.

Micron (NASDAQ:MU) is legally allowed to execute its expanded share repurchase plan.

Here's how each event could move the market.

Image source: Getty Images.

The Fed's big decision

The next FOMC meeting concludes on Dec. 9 and chair Kevin Warsh is expected to hold a press conference discussing its target fed funds rate decision. Futures traders currently expect the committee to raise the target rate by 25 basis points, with an outside chance of a 50-basis-point increase. Expectations for a rate increase were significantly lower before the most recent inflation report, which showed prices rising faster than expected.

Higher interest rates tend to keep stock prices lower, as investors are pushed to discount earnings at a higher rate. Higher interest rates are especially relevant in today's market, where many of the largest companies in the S&P 500 have become extremely capital-intensive, relying on outside funding to fuel their growth.

While the rate decision is important, it's unlikely the Fed will do anything that surprises the market and causes a significant move in prices in and of itself. What may be more telling is Warsh's comments at the press conference. While he's aimed to reduce how much telegraphing he does about the Fed's future rate plans, his comments could provide some indication of what he and the committee are watching ahead of the next meeting.

Broadcom's earnings

Broadcom is one of the most important chipmakers in the artificial intelligence space. It's the leading developer of custom AI accelerators used by hyperscalers and leading AI labs. Investors will be paying close attention to its earnings report, in particular, its AI semiconductor revenue.

Story Continues

Management said it expects AI semiconductor revenue to accelerate to $21.7 billion, up 236% year over year for the quarter. A shortfall could indicate the shift to custom silicon isn't moving as quickly as expected or that hyperscalers simply can't build as quickly as anticipated. The former would be bad news for several other companies that make custom AI chips, while the latter would be bad news for the entire semiconductor industry.

On the flip side, a good report and better-than-expected outlook could provide a boost to Broadcom stock and the rest of the industry. It could particularly benefit Alphabet and Anthropic , its two largest partners.

Micron's buybacks begin

Micron boosted its share repurchase authorization from $2.16 billion to $35.16 billion in October, but there's a big catch. The company is not legally allowed to repurchase more shares than it issues for stock-based compensation until Dec. 9. That's due to receiving Chip Act funding from the U.S. government in 2024.

Micron will likely do its best not to move the market for its stock, but it could be a huge buyer for the shares at depressed levels. The stock is down about 40% from its peak this summer and 29.5% since the board authorized the repurchase in October.

The confidence of a big buyer in Micron stock could support the stock price of one of the largest semiconductor stocks in the S&P 500. And if Micron's management is buying the stock around the current level, it could encourage other investors to buy its competitors and other AI stocks that have come down in price. Management may provide an update on its buyback program again with its quarterly earnings report in December, giving investors a better idea of how big a buyer of its own stock it will be.

Semiconductor stocks suffered the steepest losses, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropping approximately 12%.

The selloff followed a difficult October for technology stocks, as the S&P 500 technology sector lost 6.8%. Concerns over massive AI infrastructure investments, uncertain returns, and potential regulatory changes have weighed on investor sentiment. Growth stocks have been particularly vulnerable because their elevated valuations depend heavily on future earnings expectations and are sensitive to higher interest rates. Following the report, traders raised the probability of a quarter-point December rate hike to 84%, according to Yahoo Finance.

Markets have continued to swing as investors weigh the implications of higher borrowing costs against economic resilience. news.Title: Why Broadcom Stock Could Double by 2030
news.Content:
Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) stock traded at $304.41 as of market close on Nov. 20, 2026 -- down 12% for the year and more than a third below its 52-week high, while the Nasdaq-100 has been just about flat. Wall Street is focused on the financing risks in AI spending, prompting a Rothschild & Co Redburn downgrade on Nov. 13, as well as concerns over data center delays and tighter U.S. chip export rules.

Nonetheless, insatiable demand for AI chips has driven strong growth for Broadcom this year. In the quarter ended Aug. 2, Broadcom's revenue rose 86% year over year to $29.6 billion, and AI semiconductor revenue more than tripled to $16.7 billion. With earnings still expected to grow far faster than the stock price, there's a path for Broadcom shares to double by 2030.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

AI revenue expected to double

A March 2026 report from Morgan Stanley estimated nearly $3 trillion of AI infrastructure investment will be needed through 2028, with more than 80% still ahead. On the Sept. 2 earnings call, Broadcom CEO Hock Tan said AI revenue should double to about $115 billion in fiscal 2027 and double again to $230 billion in fiscal 2028, with supply already secured.

Image source: Getty Images.

Broadcom co-designs custom AI chips, called XPUs, with frontier model developers such as OpenAI and Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT). Tan says they can outperform graphics processing units (GPUs) at about half the cost. It also has a long-term agreement with Alphabet 's Google that runs through 2031.

There are concerns around potential delays in data center construction. Power, land, and construction decide when data centers come online, and Morgan Stanley expects about 20% of U.S. projects planned for 2028 to slip to 2029. But that only shifts revenue by a year and shouldn't be a reason to sell the stock.

Anthropic's IPO eases the financing risk

Tan expects Anthropic to become Broadcom's largest XPU customer in 2027. Anthropic's filing shows five-year equipment leases with Broadcom totaling about $161 billion, and Anthropic can issue up to $42 billion of convertible notes to cover it.

That's the financing risk that analysts are worried about. If Anthropic ultimately can't fund its commitments, it could be a problem for Broadcom.

However, Anthropic's initial public offering (IPO) netted nearly $120 billion in proceeds, including a $26 billion private placement in which Broadcom buys about $1 billion of stock. That's on top of $95.6 billion of cash Anthropic held as of Sept. 30, which gives it a sizable cushion to cover its rent payments to Broadcom.

Story Continues

Earnings growth can double the stock

Broadcom earned $7.83 per share over the past 12 months, a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of about 39. The fiscal 2028 consensus is $30.53 per share, consistent with Tan's outlook for earnings to exceed $30.

A 20 P/E on fiscal 2028 estimates implies a price near $611, more than double yesterday's closing price. The multiple would fall by more than half, around the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) average, and the stock would still nearly double. Even the lowest analyst estimate of $25.22 implies about $504 at that multiple.

At half today's P/E, Broadcom's earnings growth could carry the stock to roughly double by 2028, and even if data center projects get delayed by a year, it could still see enough growth through 2030 to double the share price.

news.Title: Broadcom Stock Is 27% Below Its June Record. Here's Where I Think It Will Be in 2030.
news.Content:
Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) shares trade around $353 as I write this, about 27% below the record $481.57 they closed at on June 2. But in the quarter Broadcom reported in September, the chip designer's non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share surged 96% from a year earlier.

Where could Broadcom stock be by the end of 2030?

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

I think it could hit around $600. That'd be a rise of about 70% from today's price, or about 14% a year.

This estimate hinges on one earnings path, based mainly on Broadcom's artificial intelligence (AI) chips, and one ending valuation . It also comes before the company's fiscal fourth-quarter report on Dec. 9, which might change both.

And it relies most on one assumption: that a really short list of customers keeps buying.

Image source: Getty Images.

A $30 starting point

Showing how fast the AI business is scaling, Broadcom's AI semiconductor revenue climbed 221% year over year to $16.7 billion in the fiscal third quarter of 2026 (the period ended Aug. 2, 2026). Management sees fiscal Q4 AI revenue of $21.7 billion, an acceleration to 236% growth, which would take the fiscal 2026 total to about $58 billion. Custom AI chips, which Broadcom designs for specific customers, made up 73% of the third-quarter total. And AI networking revenue, from the chips that tie those processors together, climbed over 2.5-fold from a year earlier.

Management also said on its September earnings call that it's locked in the supply to double AI revenue again in fiscal 2027, to about $115 billion. It sees a path to $230 billion in fiscal 2028, and it expects networking to grow just as fast as the custom chips.

"As a result, I got to say we are very much on target to exceed $30 in earnings per share in fiscal 2028," CEO Hock Tan said on the call.

I use that $30 as my base for fiscal 2028. Then, I assume earnings growth slows to around 10% a year as the largest data center build-outs mature. This would put earnings per share at about $40 in fiscal 2031.

What will investors pay in 2030?

Today, the stock price is around 18 times the fiscal 2027 earnings per share analysts expect on average. The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) traded at about 18 times forward earnings in mid-November, according to FactSet.

Sure, Broadcom is growing far faster than the index now. By the end of 2030, though, investors will probably be pricing the stock on fiscal 2031 earnings, and growth should be much slower. So I assume a lower price-to-earnings ratio of around 15.

Story Continues

At 15 times forward earnings of about $40, the stock would be worth about $600.

That means all the gain in my estimate comes from earnings growth, with investors paying less for every dollar of Broadcom's profit than they do now.

Profitability looks like a smaller risk. Management expects adjusted gross margin to ease to around 73% in fiscal Q4, from 78% a year earlier, as memory-heavy custom chips grow. But it sees the adjusted operating margin staying at about 66%, flat year over year.

Five customers carry the estimate

The bigger risk is who buys those chips. Broadcom estimates that its top five end customers made up around 55% of its fiscal third-quarter revenue, versus about 40% a year earlier. In the first three quarters of fiscal 2026, that share was about 50%.

Broadcom makes custom AI chips for six customers. Management expects Anthropic to become the largest of them in 2027, and OpenAI the second largest in 2028.

The company's latest quarterly filing warns that losing any top-five customer, or a big fall in demand from one, could have a material adverse effect on its business.

What if the big deployments are around two years late? Then earnings per share might hit $30 in fiscal 2030 and about $33 in fiscal 2031. At the same 15 times forward earnings, the stock would land near $500 instead, for yearly gains of about 9%.

That's still a decent return. But a customer that stops buying entirely could do much more harm.

All in all, I think around $600 is a fair estimate for Broadcom stock at the end of 2030. If those customers keep building, today's price looks reasonable to me for a company with that path ahead of it. But that's just a guess, and much of it rests on spending decisions Broadcom doesn't control.

news.Title: Billionaire David Tepper Just Made a Massive AI Chip Rotation — Will It Pay Off?
news.Content:
David Tepper of Appaloosa Management is considered one of the world's top hedge fund managers, and through his investment prowess, he's amassed an estimated net worth of $28.5 billion. The Carolina Panthers' owner was reshuffling his artificial intelligence (AI) semiconductor positions in Q3, exiting positions in Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) and Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO), while buying shares of Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Micron (NASDAQ:MU). He also cut his stake in Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) (NASDAQ:GOOG) nearly in half.

While Tepper's track record speaks for itself, I think he got it wrong in this case. Here's why.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The great rotation

While Tepper was buying Nvidia shares before Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO, the company is facing potential issues beyond the loss of its CEO. Competitors have started to catch up, with Semianalysis recently reporting that Alphabet's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), which it co-developed with Broadcom, are delivering better performance per dollar. Meanwhile, all of Nvidia's largest customers, outside of Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ:SPCX) are working on developing their own custom chips.

The AI application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) market is growing much more quickly than the GPU market, with Counterpoint Research projecting that custom AI chip unit shipments will surpass data center GPU shipments in 2028. Two of the biggest winners from this trend are Alphabet and Broadcom.

Alphabet developed its TPUs more than a decade ago, and its comprehensive ecosystem is starting to rival Nvidia's. Not only is TPU growth supported by Alphabet's internal use and its cloud offering, but it is also beginning to sell its solutions to external data center operators, such as Anthropic and OpenAI.

Bloomberg Intelligence believes that TPU sales outside of Google Cloud could grow from just $12 billion this year to over $135 billion in 2028. This is a huge revenue driver for both Alphabet and Broadcom, which appear to be two of the biggest winners in this rotation.

Even bigger news for Nvidia competitors, though, is that Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) revealed that its Claude Mythos model demonstrated that it can get models up to speed running on AMD GPUs in just two to three days without any human involvement, dramatically cutting down the six to 12 months it used to take a dozen engineers to get models running on different chips. This greatly narrows Nvidia's CUDA moat and opens the door for both AMD and ASICs to take market share.

Story Continues

The timing is great for AMD, as it recently started shipping its complete Helios systems, which combine its GPUs, CPUs, and networking into one package, to large hyperscaler customers. It's significantly cheaper than Nvidia's end-to-end server racks, opening the door to take more market share if it can show strong performance. The company's CPUs will also play a key role in Alphabet's new TPU 8tx AI system .

Image source: Getty Images.

With CUDA's moat weakening, Alphabet, Broadcom, and AMD, all of which have cheaper offerings, should benefit greatly in the coming years. Meanwhile, Nvidia could face not just a loss of share but also margin compression. This could lead to lower profitability even if it can grow its revenue. That's one of the big reasons I prefer the three stocks Tepper was selling over Nvidia.

Memory collapse

As for the other semiconductor stock that Tepper was buying, Micron, I'd be careful. Memory has historically experienced very big boom-and-bust cycles, and, while this supercycle is certainly different, memory still tends to be a commodity.

Micron is also the most exposed of the big dynamic random access memory (DRAM) makers to any changes in prices of conventional memory, with it having the smallest share of the high bandwidth memory (HBM) market, which has been the driving force of the industry.

Another area of worry is with NAND, or flash memory. While Micron derives the bulk of its memory from DRAM, NAND has grown to about a quarter of its revenue. Hong Kong-based GF Securities recently issued a note saying it expects this market to become oversupplied as soon as next year. While primarily a DRAM maker, Micron would not be immune to a big price pullback in the NAND market.

news.Title: ULA Vulcan Launch Ends in Disaster for Amazon's Satellite Internet Ambitions
news.Content: A crisis was forming in the space industry. For months, Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ:SPCX) CEO Elon Musk had been making noises about ending commercial launches of its Falcon 9 rocket -- the rocket that, in 2025, launched more than 80% of all payloads to orbit worldwide. At the time, rockets from rival companies Arianespace, Blue Origin, and United Launch Alliance were all grounded for a variety of technical glitches. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. ...
news.AI_Summary:
• United Launch Alliance's (ULA) Vulcan rocket experienced a total mission failure, resulting in the loss of all 40 Amazon Leo communication satellites.
• The failure is attributed to a problem with the Vulcan first stage, specifically the fuel supply to the BE-4 engines, impacting Amazon's satellite internet ambitions.
• Amazon has reserved numerous launches on ULA's Vulcan Centaur rockets to build its satellite communications system and compete with SpaceX's Starlink.
• This failure exacerbates Amazon's reliance on ULA's Vulcan, as Atlas V rockets are nearing retirement and SpaceX Falcon 9 launches are booked through 2028.
• The issue with the BE-4 engines could also affect Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket, further complicating Amazon's launch schedule.

news.Title: Why It’s Time to Buy the Pullback in Broadcom Stock
news.Content:
Broadcom (AVGO) shares have pulled back sharply, giving up most of their gains for the year. The decline comes amid a broader selloff in artificial intelligence (AI) stocks, margin pressure, and growing concerns that competition in the custom AI chip market is heating up.

Marvell Technology's (MRVL) partnership with Alphabet's (GOOG) (GOOGL) Google to develop custom AI chips has added to these concerns. However, the competitive threat to Broadcom may be getting more attention than it deserves. The bigger picture is that Broadcom is witnessing growing adoption of its custom AI accelerators, or XPUs, among its customers. Moreover, Broadcom is projecting solid growth for XPUs.

More News from Barchart

A $150 Billion Reason to Buy the Nvidia Stock Dip

Leadership Risk vs. Record Numbers: Nvidia Posted $115 Billion in Revenue in Its First Report Without Jensen Huang. What It Means for NVDA Stock.

AMD vs. Nvidia Stock After Jensen Huang's Exit: 1 Trades at Nearly 4x the Other's Earnings Multiple. Here's the AI Chip Stock I'd Buy Now.

Our exclusive Barchart Brief newsletter is your FREE midday guide to what's moving stocks, sectors, and investor sentiment - delivered right when you need the info most. Subscribe today!

While its gross margins are expected to remain under pressure from the growing share of AI revenue in overall sales, solid operating leverage will continue to drive its earnings.

With its long-term growth outlook still intact, the recent pullback presents a buying opportunity for investors. The lower share price has also made Broadcom's valuation more appealing, strengthening its investment appeal.

Broadcom's Growth Trajectory Remains Exceptionally Strong

Broadcom continues to deliver impressive growth, and its momentum is expected to strengthen further in Q4 and beyond. Strong demand for custom AI accelerators, AI networking solutions, and enterprise AI infrastructure is positioning the company for significant growth.

Broadcom reported Q3 revenue of $29.6 billion, up 86% year-over-year (YoY). This represents a sharp acceleration from 29% growth in Q1 and 48% in Q2. The biggest contributor to its accelerating growth is its AI semiconductor business, which grew 221% YoY and 54% sequentially in Q3.

Within AI semiconductors, its custom AI silicon business is growing rapidly. Its six XPU customers are rapidly expanding the deployment of their own AI accelerators, driving a substantial increase in demand.

AI semiconductor revenue exceeded $16.7 billion in Q3, more than tripling from the previous year. XPU shipments increased more than 3.5 times, accounting for approximately 73% of AI semiconductor revenue. Meanwhile, AI networking revenue grew more than 2.5 times, highlighting strong demand across the broader AI infrastructure ecosystem.

Story Continues

The outlook is even stronger. Broadcom expects Q4 AI revenue to reach $21.7 billion, up 236% YoY, driven by higher accelerator shipments for Anthropic (ANT), Google, OpenAI, and Meta (META). Both XPU and AI networking revenue are expected to triple YoY.

As a result, management has raised its FY26 AI revenue expectations to approximately $58 billion, representing 186% growth and exceeding its earlier outlook.

More importantly, management's longer-term projections suggest that Broadcom's AI opportunity is still in its early stages. The company expects AI revenue to double to $115 billion in FY27 and reach $230 billion in FY28. Broadcom has secured the supply needed to support these targets.

Alongside solid top-line growth, Broadcom's profitability is also expanding. In Q3, operating income increased 92% YoY, outpacing revenue growth despite some pressure from changes in business mix. The earnings opportunity is equally significant. Management expects Broadcom to generate more than $30 in EPS by FY28, reflecting significant growth ahead.

Non-AI Businesses Continue to Provide Support

Beyond AI, non-AI semiconductor revenue is expected to support Broadcom's overall growth, led by demand in broadband and server storage. Its Infrastructure software revenue reached $8.8 billion in Q3, up 29% YoY, while annual recurring revenue (ARR) grew 15%.

VMware is also expanding Broadcom's opportunity in enterprise AI, which will likely support its growth.

Q4 Outlook Points to Further Acceleration

Broadcom expects Q4 FY26 revenue to reach $34.8 billion, up 93% YoY, with an operating margin of approximately 66%.

This guidance suggests growth is not slowing. Instead, accelerating demand for custom AI accelerators and networking solutions is expected to drive another significant step up in revenue.

Broadcom Stock Appears Attractive on Valuation

Broadcom's current valuation appears compelling relative to its robust earnings growth outlook. AVGO stock trades at 19.3 times forward earnings, which is low considering the company's strong earnings growth potential.

Analysts project Broadcom's EPS to increase by 70% in FY27 to $17.31. Furthermore, management's revenue outlook for FY28 points to EPS exceeding $30, implying roughly 73% YoY growth compared with analyst estimates for FY27.

Overall, AVGO's strong projected earnings growth and a relatively low forward valuation suggest investors should consider buying the pullback.

AVGO Stock Is a Buy on Pullback

AVGO stock's recent pullback offers an attractive entry point, given its accelerating AI revenue, led by expanding XPU business. It is also expected to deliver solid earnings growth over the next couple of years.

Wall Street is bullish on AVGO's prospects, as reflected in its "Strong Buy" consensus rating and $519.11 average price target.

news.Title: ASML vs. Broadcom: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
news.Content:
The semiconductor world is currently split between the machines that build chips and the designs that power them. Is ASML (NASDAQ:ASML) or Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) the better play for your portfolio?

ASML holds a virtual monopoly on the advanced lithography machinery required to print the world's most sophisticated microchips. Meanwhile, Broadcom has evolved into a powerhouse of networking components and enterprise software. Both companies are critical to the tech supply chain, but they offer distinct paths for investors seeking exposure to high-end silicon.

The case for ASML

ASML manufactures lithography systems, which are massive machines that use light to print intricate patterns onto silicon wafers. It provides the essential hardware for every major chipmaker to produce smaller, faster, and more efficient processors. Because its technology is unique, it serves as a critical gatekeeper for the entire high-end semiconductor market.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $43.4 billion, an increase of roughly 22.5%. The company generated approximately $14.8 billion in net income. This growth highlights the sustained demand for extreme ultraviolet lithography systems used in advanced chip production for artificial intelligence and high-performance computing.

As of ASML's December 2025 balance sheet, the current ratio, which measures a company's ability to cover its short-term debts with short-term assets, is approximately 1.3. The debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.2, showing that the company uses relatively little debt compared to its total equity. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was close to $12.2 billion.

The case for Broadcom

Broadcom is a dominant player among semiconductor stocks, providing infrastructure software and hardware solutions to global enterprises. The company has significant customer concentration, with its top five end customers accounting for roughly 40% of revenue in its latest annual report. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business, as evidenced by a $30 billion commitment from Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL).

In the 12 months ended Aug. 2, 2026, revenue reached close to $89.1 billion, representing significant growth of nearly 48.7%. The company reported net income of approximately $38.3 billion during this time frame. This surge was partly driven by the integration of large acquisitions and booming demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure across data centers.

As of Broadcom's November 2025 balance sheet, the current ratio is roughly 1.7. The debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.8, indicating a higher level of total debt relative to shareholder equity than ASML. In the fiscal year ended Nov. 2, 2025, free cash flow was close to $26.9 billion, though stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 27.5% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Story Continues

Risk profile comparison

ASML faces risks from its position at the center of global trade tensions, particularly concerning international export restrictions. The company also operates in the cyclical semiconductor equipment market, where spending by chipmakers can fluctuate based on broader economic conditions and interest rates. Furthermore, the rapid pace of innovation requires constant, heavy investment in research and development to maintain its technological lead over any potential competitors.

Broadcom operates in a highly cyclical industry that faces rapid price erosion and evolving technological requirements driven by artificial intelligence. It relies heavily on a limited number of contract manufacturers, such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (NYSE:TSM), which produced approximately 95% of its wafers according to its latest annual report. Broadcom also faces intense regulatory scrutiny and risks associated with its strategy of integrating large acquisitions into its software portfolio.

Valuation comparison

Broadcom looks potentially cheaper based on its forward P/E, which compares the stock price to future earnings estimates, whereas ASML has a lower P/S ratio.

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

Which stock would I buy for 2027?

The current market environment is, shall we say, hostile to tech stocks, and shares of ASML and Broadcom reflect that:

ASML data by YCharts

That said, zooming out over the past decade, both stocks have put in decent performances, handily outpacing the S&P 500 's (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) return:

In the past, I have picked ASML over many other stocks for several reasons. For one, it has a monopoly in the extreme ultraviolet lithography niche it operates in. That gives it strong pricing power and a solid moat. ASML also consistently reports a net margin in excess of 30%, and it pays a modest dividend.

However, it's hard to argue with Broadcom's long-term performance. A company of that size reporting nearly 50% revenue growth is pretty wild. ASML and Broadcom are both exposed to the inherent cyclicality of the semiconductor industry, so I think that risk factor offsets itself. And the tech sector (and the market in general) may be melting down right now, but long-term investors shouldn't get especially concerned over what happens in the course of a week, or a month, or even a year.

I'm breaking with my pattern here. I don't think ASML is a bad choice, to be clear, but Broadcom has strong margins and even better revenue growth. Broadcom gets my vote for 2027 and beyond.

news.Title: The 1 Thing I'll Be Watching When Broadcom Reports on Dec. 9
news.Content:
Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) shares have dropped about $135 apiece since their record close on June 2, putting the stock roughly 28% under that peak at about $347 as of this writing. The chip designer reports results for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 (the period ended Nov. 1, 2026) after the market closes on Wednesday, Dec. 9.

There'll be lots of numbers in that release. But one line matters more to me than the rest: artificial intelligence (AI) semiconductor revenue. I'll be checking it twice -- once for the quarter Broadcom just wrapped up, against the $21.7 billion management forecast in September, and once for what the company expects in the first quarter of fiscal 2027.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

After all, AI chips made up 56% of Broadcom's revenue in its latest quarter, and they accounted for over 80% of its year-over-year revenue growth.

Image source: Getty Images.

AI revenue keeps landing above forecast

Broadcom has made a habit of landing a bit above its own AI forecasts this year. In the first quarter of fiscal 2026 (the period ended Feb. 1, 2026), AI semiconductor revenue was $8.4 billion, against the $8.2 billion management had forecast. The fiscal second quarter brought $10.8 billion, against a $10.7 billion forecast. And the fiscal third quarter (the period ended Aug. 2) delivered $16.7 billion, over the $16.0 billion management had guided for.

Growth has accelerated the whole way, too. Year-over-year AI revenue growth rose from 106% in fiscal Q1 to 143% in fiscal Q2 and 221% in fiscal Q3. For fiscal Q4, management expects 236%.

In other words, Broadcom's guidance has leaned a little conservative. But the beats have been small -- between around 1% and 4% above the forecast. I'm not expecting a blowout in fiscal Q4, then. AI revenue at or a bit above $21.7 billion would show me the company is still on the schedule management laid out.

A result under $21.7 billion would break that streak for the first time this fiscal year.

Why does the next forecast matter more?

Management's goal for next year is about $115 billion of AI revenue in fiscal 2027 -- almost double the $58 billion or so it expects for fiscal 2026. And on its September earnings call, Broadcom said it doesn't plan to update that figure every quarter. That arguably makes each quarterly forecast the best checkpoint investors have.

Story Continues

Do the math, and $115 billion comes to almost $29 billion a quarter on average. That's about a third higher than the fiscal fourth-quarter forecast. If AI revenue rose at an even pace from $21.7 billion, the first quarter of fiscal 2027 would likely need to land somewhere near $24 billion to keep the year on track.

A first-quarter forecast in the mid-$20 billion range, then, should be a sign the doubling is on schedule. A forecast closer to $22 billion might mean more of next year's growth is being shifted into the second half of fiscal 2027.

Management sounded confident in September.

"Our demand actually exceeds this outlook, and we will work to improve supply," said CEO Hock Tan.

If that holds, the first-quarter forecast might land above my rough math. Either way, Dec. 9 is the first chance to check.

What the stock needs now

After a 28% fall, I don't think Broadcom needs a big upside surprise to work from here. Of course, the company has kept growing through the slide. Fiscal third-quarter revenue rose 86% year over year to $29.6 billion, and non-GAAP (adjusted) operating income climbed 92%.

That growth hasn't made the stock cheap, though. At around $347, each share costs about 44 times Broadcom's earnings per share over the past four quarters. This price-to-earnings ratio only makes sense if AI revenue continues to rise as management expects.

What the stock needs is evidence that next year's doubling is still on track. And the AI revenue line, along with the forecast behind it, is where that evidence should first appear.

Granted, one good report won't settle everything. Much of next year's AI revenue hinges on deployment plans from a few big AI customers, and those plans can change. But the first-quarter forecast is the closest look investors will get at whether these plans are holding.

In the end, if fiscal Q4 AI revenue comes in at or above $21.7 billion and the first-quarter forecast calls for the mid-$20 billion range, I think today's price looks fair for a growth stock with sales climbing this fast. A forecast well below that would make me more cautious, even at a lower stock price.

Broadcom expects Anthropic to become its largest custom AI chip customer in 2027, making the developer's access to capital an important factor in its growth outlook.

Strong demand for Anthropic's shares suggests investors remain willing to finance large technology companies, although higher borrowing costs and long-term infrastructure obligations remain risks.

After a long wait, Claude developer Anthropic PBC (NASDAQ: ANT) is finally a publicly traded company. The news is a positive for many firms across the AI and semiconductor industry, including chip giant Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO). Not only does the move bolster Anthropic's ability to make good on its large-scale commitments to Broadcom, but it also pushes back on one of the key concerns Broadcom's CEO outlined earlier this year.

Anthropic Fortifies Balance Sheet With IPO and Private Placement Proceeds

Anthropic's total chip leasing commitments to Broadcom are $161.2 billion over the next five years, excluding interest. With these commitments, Broadcom expects Anthropic to become its largest XPU customer in 2027, and to sustain that position in 2028. This makes Anthropic's ability to pay Broadcom critical to the chip giant achieving its forecast for $350 billion in AI semiconductor sales from its fiscal year 2027 to fiscal year 2028.

→ 3 Dividend ETFs Offering Steadier Footing in a Shaky Market

Anthropic's total commitments to AI hyperscalers and neoclouds are also several times larger than its commitment to Broadcom. To satisfy all these payments, getting its hands on as much cash as possible is key. Luckily for Anthropic and its suppliers, the company's latest share offerings will significantly bolster its balance sheet.

Anthropic set its IPO price at $83 and initially offered 980 million shares. After removing the 23.6 million shares sold by certain stockholders, Anthropic listed proceeds from the original offering, after underwriting discounts but before other expenses, at around $78.8 billion. Underwriters subsequently exercised their option to buy 147 million additional shares, bringing the total offering to 1.127 billion shares and Anthropic's gross IPO proceeds to approximately $91.6 billion.

→ Cracks in the Crockery? Williams-Sonoma Insiders Sell Shares

Separately, the company closed a private share placement worth around $26 billion, with Broadcom among the investors. Including this, Anthropic raised approximately $117.6 billion in gross proceeds from newly issued shares across both offerings, before fees and expenses.

Story Continues

The company's amended S-1 filing shows that it was already in a very strong cash position, with cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments of around $131.8 billion. Its final prospectus estimates that these holdings would have totaled approximately $244.6 billion on a pro forma adjusted basis as of Sept. 30, assuming the completed offerings and full exercise of the underwriters' option, after estimated expenses and related tax withholding obligations.

→ If NVIDIA Tightens Its Wallet, These 3 Stocks Could Feel It

This massive piggy bank should go a long way toward helping Anthropic fund its lease and compute commitments over the coming years as it looks to increase its profitability. Although the company's sales are growing rapidly and margins are improving, its commitments still dwarf the size of its profits. In the first nine months of 2026, Anthropic's adjusted operating profit was $4.08 billion, and its operating cash flow was $6.57 billion.

Anthropic's IPO Demand Signals Willingness to Commit Capital to AI Firms

When discussing constraints on the AI buildout going forward, Broadcom's CEO Hock Tan recently said, "What I think might be the biggest constraint is capital." In this context, the strong demand for Anthropic's IPO is a positive sign, indicating that investors are still willing to commit capital to AI companies.

Around a week before going public, Anthropic said the expected price for its IPO was between $70 and $78 per share. The company also said it expected to offer 825 million shares. Based on these numbers, the high end of Anthropic's gross proceeds from the offering was around $64.35 billion, including shares sold by existing stockholders.

However, reports soon emerged that the company's IPO was around six times oversubscribed, indicating very strong investor demand. In turn, the company increased both the price per share and the number of shares offered, putting its IPO proceeds well above this previous figure.

Something similar has played out with the recent equity and bond offerings at Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META). These offerings were all several times oversubscribed according to reports, again signaling strong demand to provide capital to AI companies. This is another positive sign for Broadcom, as Meta is also one of its top chip customers, with the companies partnering to design Meta's custom AI accelerators.

Still, just because Anthropic and Meta are able to attract capital today doesn't mean the entire AI ecosystem can, or that this will continue indefinitely. Pressure is already building on debt issuance in the form of higher interest rates and credit spreads, as shown by Meta's recent offerings.

Wall Street Continues to Eye Strong Upside in Broadcom Shares

Anthropic's IPO is another strong development for Broadcom's outlook as the company targets immense AI chip sales growth over the coming years. Notably, Broadcom shares had recovered significantly since plummeting below $300 after markets reacted to the midterm election results. However, the stock took another big hit on Nov. 12, falling below $310.

Wall Street analysts have generally maintained a bullish outlook on Broadcom. The MarketBeat consensus price target near $525 implies over 70% upside. However, Rothschild & Co Redburn significantly decreased their target in November from $595 to $398.

news.Title: Here’s My Top AI Stock to Buy With Nvidia in Uncertain Territory
news.Content:
Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) has been a rough stock to own over the past few weeks. It has lost its co-founder and CEO, Jensen Huang, and some investors worry it may never recover. While the board searches for a new leader to fill his shoes, investors are waiting to see what happens next.

In the meantime, I think there are several great companies available to invest in, with Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) being one of the best options. Broadcom is a direct competitor of Nvidia and has some advantages over Nvidia. That could lead to it stealing more market share during the current turmoil, making it a top stock to consider buying now.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Broadcom's custom AI chips challenge Nvidia's GPUs

Nvidia's primary products are graphics processing units (GPUs), which are incredible computing units that can process multiple calculations in parallel. While these units are great at nearly any task, they don't specialize in any one task. Some of this potential is wasted when a GPU is used for one workload throughout its lifespan. A specific and purpose-built computing unit would do a better job in these scenarios, and that's where Broadcom steps in.

Broadcom has emerged as a great partner for designing custom AI chips, and many companies have already partnered with it and launched their own custom AI chips. However, there has been no larger partner than Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL). Alphabet and Broadcom collaborated to design and build its Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), which can outperform GPUs in many scenarios from a cost perspective. These units are fantastic, and companies like Anthropic have designed much of their computing infrastructure around them.

With Nvidia GPUs expensive and not purpose-built, many AI companies are turning to custom AI chips like the TPU to deliver the computing power they need at a lower price point. This is translating into huge growth for Broadcom, and it's growing even faster than Nvidia is.

Broadcom's growth over the next few years should be impressive

Broadcom hasn't been shy about telling investors of the impressive growth that's coming down the pipeline. During its most recent conference call, management revealed guidance that AI semiconductor revenue will double in 2027 to $115 billion. Furthermore, Broadcom announced that that figure is expected to double again to $230 billion in 2028. It doesn't get much better than that, and investors are bound to be happy with returns if Broadcom can follow through on that projection.

Story Continues

Despite that projection, Broadcom's stock isn't valued at all that high. Broadcom is already in fiscal year 2027, and trades at just 17 times next year's earnings.

AVGO PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts

That's a very cheap price tag to pay for a stalwart like Broadcom.

Broadcom also doesn't carry the same risks as a company like Nvidia, where a questionable portion of sales is being diverted to China. Broadcom's customers are well-known, and there isn't much risk of its products falling into the wrong hands. This is a key factor that many investors ignore, along with the fact that Broadcom's products are starting to steal data center market share.

I think all of this adds up to Broadcom being one of the best investment options right now. It's cheap, growing quickly, doesn't have export risk, and has a stable leadership team. That is a recipe for success in the AI world, and I think Broadcom shareholders will be well rewarded over the long term.

Now is a perfect time to buy amid the turmoil in the market surrounding AI stocks. By this time next year, Broadcom's stock will likely be much higher.

news.Content:

GF Securities says reports of server processor order cuts at Meta Platforms ( NASDAQ:META ) and Microsoft ( NASDAQ:MSFT ) overstate the weakness in demand. He put the shift at more than 500,000 chips and linked it to Meta's rollout of servers for AI agents. Pu said Microsoft's overall order volume was steady, with changes in how capacity was allocated among server manufacturers.

AMD is gaining ground in the x86 market, according to Pu. He pegged its third-quarter share of x86 server CPU shipments at 35.5%, up from 27.8% a year earlier. He forecasts shipments of AMD's next-generation Venice processors will rise to 5.4 million in 2027 from 400,000 in 2026.

AI agents can make repeated model calls, retrieve data and use other software to finish a task. That creates work for general-purpose CPUs alongside the accelerators that run AI models. GF Securities expects total server CPU shipments to rise 29% in 2027, with AI inference driving demand.

The question is whether that demand shows up in customer orders and shipments, and how much Nvidia and AMD capture as buyers rethink which processors they deploy.

news.Title: Congress files detail AMD requests to export AI chips to China, says Hunterbrook
news.Content:
The House Foreign Affairs Committee publicly released confidential export-license records showing that AMD (AMD) applied to export 600,000 advanced AI chips to Chinese companies, with applications covering 300,000 chips approved as of May 11, Hunterbrook says. AMD characterized the proposed transfers as posing a "low" diversion risk, while the committee said some companies listed on Nvidia's ( NVDA ) applications also appeared as end recipients on AMD applications, potentially including Maginfra and Aivres, firms previously linked to blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT. Hunterbrook disclosed that its fund is short AMD.

news.Title: Nvidia’s (NVDA) AI Demand Visibility into 2029 Keeps Me Bullish
news.Content:
Nvidia's (NVDA) visibility into artificial intelligence (AI) demand through 2029 keeps me bullish after its latest results. The AI infrastructure chipmaker faces an uncomfortable leadership transition following Jensen Huang's departure. Its customers still need more compute, however, and supply plans stretch years ahead. Nvidia's supply commitments rose to $390 billion from $279 billion last quarter, with visibility extending into the next few years.

Interim CEO Colette Kress said, "Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track, and our ambition has never been greater." With shares near 9x Fiscal 2028 earnings, I think investors are overlooking the growth those plans support. Thus, I rate NVDA stock a Buy .

Nvidia's Q3 Delivered More Than a Beat

Nvidia's Q3 results delivered more than a beat, in my view. The company reported revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% year-over-year. That exceeded consensus by nearly $7 billion. Adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $2.68 also comfortably beat expectations. Data Center revenue climbed 110% to $107.6 billion, while adjusted gross margin reached 74.9%.

Rubin began volume shipments and delivered Nvidia's fastest product ramp. It contributed nearly $20 billion in its first shipment quarter. Customers are adopting the next generation while demand for existing systems remains strong.

Q4 guidance calls for $130 billion of revenue, against $124.9 billion expected . Note that this excludes all China Data Center compute revenue. Gross margins should bottom at 71%–72%, then recover toward 72%–73% in Fiscal 2028. Price increases should help offset higher memory costs.

Management also raised its Fiscal 2028 revenue-growth expectation to 75% from 70%. That gives me considerably more confidence than another small quarterly beat would.

Cash generation makes the growth more valuable. Q3 free cash flow reached $43.8 billion, and shareholder distributions totaled $28.1 billion. Nvidia has $227.3 billion of buyback authorization remaining. Management intends to use it by Fiscal 2028, while returning excess free cash flow after strategic investments. That should support per-share earnings as the business expands.

Nvidia Can Keep Growing Without Huang

Story Continues

Importantly, I believe Nvidia can keep growing without Huang. Surely, he deserves enormous credit for building the company, and replacing him carries cultural risk. Yet Kress has been CFO since 2013. Annual revenue grew from roughly $4 billion to over $200 billion during her tenure.

Moreover, technical leaders such as Ian Buck , creator of Compute Unified Device Architecture (CUDA), remain deeply involved. CUDA's developer ecosystem and Nvidia's networking capabilities are established advantages. Its rack-scale systems draw on supplier relationships built over many years. Notably, the first earnings call after Huang's departure brought higher guidance.

That execution carries directly into a multi-year product lineup that is already locked in. Rubin Ultra remains scheduled for 2027 . Feynman, Nvidia's next-generation graphics processing unit (GPU) architecture, will follow in 2028 alongside the upcoming Rosa central processing unit (CPU). With that roadmap clear, customers can plan their data center builds years ahead.

The supply commitments explain why that continuity matters. Purchasing obligations have increased from $279 billion to $390 billion, including $203 billion for Fiscal 2028 and $92 billion for Fiscal 2029. While these are Nvidia's own commitments to suppliers rather than guaranteed customer backlog, I see their scale as evidence of management's visibility into demand.

Component partners are making matching multi-year bets. New chip-substrate capacity from Kinsus ( TW:3189 ) targets 2028, while Siliconware Precision Industries' (SPIL) advanced chip-packaging expansion extends into mid-2029. Suppliers are clearly preparing to serve multiple product generations, which looks very different from an industry expecting orders to dry up shortly.

Customer agreements point in the same direction. Nvidia's $32 billion in conditional neocloud commitments extend into 2032 and beyond. Financing must be secured and capacity operational before those commitments take effect. Meanwhile, OpenAI's existing and planned deployments extend through 2030. Management has said supply should remain a bottleneck through Fiscal 2028. Rubin is only beginning its ramp.

Additionally, let's not forget that frontier labs still need more computing capacity, while inference and agentic AI broaden demand beyond training. Physical AI and sovereign projects create further opportunities. Nvidia can capture more spending through CPUs and NVLink alongside GPUs. Spectrum networking and complete systems add to that opportunity. Huang's departure doesn't remove those customer requirements.

NVDA's Valuation Looks Surprisingly Modest

NVDA's valuation looks surprisingly modest against that growth outlook. Today, Nvidia trades at around 9x Fiscal 2028 consensus EPS of $16.61. Fiscal 2029's $21.75 estimate brings it to 7x. Consensus expects EPS growth of 72% next year and then another 31% afterward. Wall Street already allows for deceleration while still forecasting substantial earnings gains.

A single-digit multiple would make more sense if profits faced an imminent collapse. Today's customer deployments and supply planning point toward continued expansion. Nvidia doesn't need today's growth rate forever for the valuation to work. Even EPS 25% below Fiscal 2028 consensus would leave earnings near $12.46. Today's price would imply roughly 11.7x that figure.

Buybacks provide further support. The remaining authorization represents roughly 6% of Nvidia's current market value. Buying shares at lower earnings multiples gives each dollar more earnings power.

The risks, of course, deserve attention. AMD (AMD) and hyperscaler custom chips could take share. Customers may moderate spending if AI returns disappoint. China restrictions limit access to a major market, while memory costs pressure margins. Nvidia's growing financial commitments also expose it to partners' execution and funding problems.

Leadership continuity also still needs proving over time. Those risks keep the opportunity uncertain, but I think today's valuation offers substantial compensation.

Is NVDA Stock a Buy?

Wall Street rates NVDA a Moderate Buy, based on 30 Buys, 13 Holds, and one Sell. The $232.59 average price target implies about 59% upside from the latest premarket quote.

Conclusion

Nvidia's leadership transition deserves scrutiny, but the demand outlook remains exceptional. Q3 doubled revenue, and management raised its expectations for next year. Supply-chain investments extending into 2029 support a much longer growth story. At roughly 9x Fiscal 2028 earnings, with enormous buybacks planned, I remain firmly bullish. That price leaves room for growth to slow considerably.

news.Title: AMD Is Down 26% and Intel Is Down 42%. Which AI Stock Is Worth Buying on the Dip?
news.Content:
The recent semiconductor sell-off has presented investors with potentially attractive buying opportunities as concerns surrounding artificial intelligence (AI) valuations weigh on the sector. Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) and Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) have fallen approximately 26% and 42% from their respective recent highs.

AMD has established itself as a major supplier of high-performance computing products, capitalizing on growing demand for AI infrastructure. Intel, meanwhile, is pursuing an ambitious turnaround centered on restoring its competitive position in processor design and semiconductor manufacturing.

While both companies stand to benefit from continued investment in AI, their contrasting financial performance, capital requirements, and competitive positions present two distinct investment opportunities.

The case for Advanced Micro Devices

AMD designs high-performance processors and accelerators for data centers, personal computers, and gaming systems. Its expanding portfolio of AI accelerators and multiyear strategic partnership with OpenAI position the company to capture a greater share of AI infrastructure spending. Meanwhile, established relationships with companies such as Sony and Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) provide additional revenue streams through its gaming business.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 26, 2026, revenue reached approximately $45.4 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 41.9%. AMD generated $7.6 billion in net income over the same period, translating to a profit margin of roughly 16.8%. Its ability to deliver substantial revenue growth while maintaining profitability is particularly attractive as investors increasingly scrutinize the financial performance of AI-related companies.

As of December 2025, AMD maintained a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.1 and a current ratio of 2.9, reflecting a relatively strong balance sheet. The company also generated approximately $6.7 billion in free cash flow during fiscal 2025, although stock-based compensation accounted for 21.2% of operating cash flow.

The case for Intel

Intel designs and manufactures processors for personal computers, data centers, and networking applications. While its established processor business remains a significant source of revenue, much of Intel's long-term investment thesis centers on its foundry strategy. By expanding its semiconductor manufacturing capabilities, Intel aims to compete for manufacturing contracts from other chip designers while reducing its reliance on traditional processor sales.

Story Continues

In the 12 months ended Sept. 26, 2026, revenue reached approximately $59.9 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 12.1%. However, Intel recorded a net loss of roughly $12 billion, translating to a negative profit margin of 20.1%. Despite improving revenue, Intel continues to face substantial financial challenges as it works to regain market share and establish a competitive semiconductor manufacturing business.

As of December 2025, Intel maintained a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.4 and a current ratio of approximately 2.0. However, the company recorded negative free cash flow of $4.9 billion in fiscal 2025, while stock-based compensation accounted for 25.1% of operating cash flow.

Risk profile comparison

One of AMD's primary risks is intense competition from Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), which maintains an established lead in the AI accelerator market. However, geopolitical and regulatory risks are becoming increasingly significant. On Nov. 19, AMD shares fell nearly 8% following a report alleging ties to blacklisted Chinese companies, claims AMD has disputed. New U.S. export restrictions targeting remote access to advanced AI chips through overseas data centers could also limit international growth opportunities.

Intel faces considerably greater financial and operational risks. Unlike AMD, Intel must absorb the substantial costs of developing and operating its own semiconductor manufacturing facilities. Its foundry strategy requires significant capital investment, with profitability largely dependent on securing external manufacturing customers and achieving sufficient production volumes. Intel must accomplish this while attempting to regain market share in its traditional processor business. Customer concentration adds another layer of risk, with its three largest customers accounting for approximately 43% of net revenue in 2025.

Valuation comparison

Intel appears to be the cheaper option based on both the Forward P/E , which compares stock price to future earnings estimates, and the P/S ratio, which measures market cap divided by sales over the past twelve months.

Which stock would I buy the dip for 2027?

From a valuation standpoint, Intel appears to be the more affordable option, trading at 37.2 times forward earnings compared to AMD's 60.6. Intel also trades at 4.9 times sales, considerably below AMD's multiple of 17.7. Although neither stock looks particularly cheap, I believe AMD's stronger financial position and growth prospects make it the more compelling investment following the recent semiconductor sell-off.

With interest rates remaining elevated and investors increasingly scrutinizing AI-related capital expenditures, the financial composition of each company deserves particular consideration. AMD's limited debt burden, positive free cash flow, and established profitability provide the financial flexibility to invest in product development without relying heavily on external financing. In contrast, Intel must fund an expensive manufacturing turnaround while contending with substantial losses and negative free cash flow.

Although AMD's elevated valuation leaves it vulnerable to further selling pressure, I believe its stronger balance sheet, superior revenue growth, and considerably lower capital requirements justify a valuation premium. Given the current macroeconomic environment, I would rather invest in a semiconductor company with proven financial performance than one whose investment thesis depends heavily on a successful turnaround.

news.Title: Nvidia drops 12%, Broadcom and AMD extend declines as the AI trade melts down
news.Content:
Chip giant Nvidia ( NVDA ) extended its declines on Friday, dropping 12%. The stock headed for seven straight days of losses amid a reported SEC probe into the chip maker's accounting practices.

Shares of peers AMD ( AMD ) and Broadcom ( AVGO ) also tanked double-digit percentages as a broader AI trade sell-off intensified. Broadcom has significant financial ties to Anthropic ( ANT ), which made its public debut on Thursday. Under an arrangement disclosed in Anthropic's prospectus, the chipmaker agreed to lend the AI developer up to $42 billion to help finance its infrastructure build-out and purchase about $1 billion of Anthropic shares as part of its IPO-related private placement.

On Friday, Anthropic's stock fell as much as 12% amid a broader tech sell-off.

Memory chipmaker Micron Technology ( MU ) and peer SK Hynix ( SKHY ) dropped more than 10%. Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company ( TSM ) and equipment maker ASML ( ASML ) also declined.

Yorkville Ives' Dan Ives said the AI trade weakness "is a panic-driven sell-off" in tech "rather than a red flag moment indicating darker times ahead for tech and the market."

"Big Tech will be spending capex next year in the $1.5 trillion range, and that is not changing because of the panic in the market the last few months," he wrote on Friday.

The broader chip sector fell on Thursday following the public debut of AI model maker Anthropic. The sector was already on shaky ground following the exit of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and concerns over AI financing.

Nvidia is down more than 22% year to date, putting it on pace for its first annual decline since 2022, when the Federal Reserve began a rate-hiking cycle, according to Yahoo Finance's AlphaSpace data.

Other areas of the AI trade were under pressure Friday, with optical equipment maker Coherent ( COHR ) and Bloom Energy ( BE ) stocks sinking 6% and 7%, respectively.

Neocloud providers CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Nebius ( NBIS ) both extended losses from the prior session, declining roughly 9%.

Broadcom anticipates fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 gross margin of approximately 73%, down from 78% reported in the year-ago quarter.

Broadcom's reliance on six major custom accelerator customers also creates concentration risks. Moreover, shortages of advanced wafers, memory and substrates, alongside delays in data center construction and power availability, could affect the timing of AI infrastructure deployments. Financing arrangements supporting customers such as OpenAI and Anthropic introduce additional contingent liabilities. These concerns, combined with the stock's elevated valuation, warrant a cautious investment stance.

AVGO's Strong AI Growth Boosts Competitive Prowess

Broadcom is benefiting from surging demand for custom AI accelerators and networking solutions as hyperscalers expand their AI infrastructure investments. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, AI semiconductor revenues surged 221% year over year and 54% sequentially to $16.7 billion. The company expects AI semiconductor revenues to reach $21.7 billion in the fourth quarter, representing 236% year-over-year growth. More importantly, Broadcom expects AI semiconductor revenues to reach approximately $115 billion in fiscal 2027 and $230 billion in fiscal 2028, supported by accelerating custom accelerator adoption.

Broadcom's relationships with Google, Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta provide substantial visibility into future AI semiconductor demand. The company has strengthened its long-standing partnership with Google through an agreement to develop and supply future generations of Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) and AI networking products. Anthropic is expected to deploy an additional 5 gigawatts of TPU capacity in 2027, followed by an incremental 10 gigawatts in 2028. OpenAI is targeting 1.3 gigawatts of Jalapeno accelerator deployments in 2027 and more than 5 gigawatts in 2028, while Broadcom is also developing multiple generations of Meta's MTIA accelerators.

Broadcom's AI opportunity extends beyond custom accelerators into Ethernet switching, optical interconnects and high-speed connectivity solutions. The company's Tomahawk 6 Ethernet switch offers 100-terabit-per-second capacity, while its next-generation Tomahawk 7 targets 200 terabits per second. Broadcom is also expanding its presence in optical digital signal processors, electro-absorption modulated lasers, vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers and continuous-wave lasers. The company expects AI networking revenues to grow as rapidly as its custom accelerator business over the next few years. This diversified AI portfolio enables Broadcom to benefit from rising networking complexity and bandwidth requirements across AI data centers, supporting its long-term growth outlook.

Story Continues

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings is pegged at $3.82 per share, unchanged over the past 60 days, indicating 96% growth from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

Conclusion

Broadcom's modest 1.9% share price appreciation over the past year and premium valuation may discourage investors seeking immediate upside. Nevertheless, AVGO's rapidly expanding AI semiconductor business, strong hyperscaler relationships, networking leadership and growing software portfolio provide compelling long-term growth opportunities. Robust free cash flow generation and operating leverage further strengthen Broadcom's fundamentals. news.Title: Prediction: This Is What Will Happen to Micron’s Stock Price in December
news.Content:
Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) has made investors significantly richer in 2026, with shares of the memory specialist up 123% as of this writing. However, the stock has run into rough weather in the second half of the year.

Micron stock has lost 32% of its value since the beginning of July. Micron has been affected by concerns about rising competition from China and a pullback in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure spending due to higher interest rates, which could constrain funding. That's why Micron investors will now be eagerly awaiting Micron's fiscal 2027 first-quarter report, which is expected in the second half of December.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

I will take a closer look at the state of the memory market to determine whether this high-flying AI stock can regain its mojo.

Image source: Micron.

The memory market experienced an incredible jump last quarter

Market research firm Counterpoint Research notes that the memory supercycle continued in the third quarter of 2026. The dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) market's revenue increased by an incredible 5x over the prior-year period to $200 billion. A massive price increase drove this phenomenal jump, while bit shipments increased by only 4% year over year.

Counterpoint points out that Micron controlled 21% of the DRAM market last quarter. So, Micron's DRAM revenue in calendar Q3 should be $42 billion, based on Counterpoint's analysis. It is worth noting that Micron's fiscal Q1 ends in early December, so calendar Q3 overlaps with two months of its fiscal Q1.

But even if that's the case, Micron's DRAM business is on track to surge by a significant margin over the $10.8 billion in revenue it generated from this segment in the first quarter of fiscal 2026. Micron has called for $61.5 billion in revenue for the current quarter, implying a 4.5x increase over last year. The company derives nearly three-fourths of its revenue from the DRAM segment, suggesting it is on track to exceed $40 billion in DRAM revenue.

Also, the company is forecasting an increase of almost 8x in earnings per share from the year-ago period. Memory prices are still growing exponentially, as the limited supply of these chips forces buyers to compete for available capacity, thereby putting Micron in a position to command higher prices. As a result, the company should be able to achieve the phenomenal increase in earnings per share (EPS) that it expects.

Story Continues

However, a lot will depend on the company's guidance for the stock to accelerate again. There is good news for investors on this front as well.

Micron's guidance should be a strong one, and that could give its stock price a nice boost

Counterpoint Research expects memory prices to remain strong in 2027 as well. In fact, it isn't the only source that's expecting a bump in memory prices next year. TrendForce, for instance, is forecasting a 70%-140% increase in the price of AI-specific high-bandwidth memory (HBM) next year. The firm estimates that spending on memory and storage chips will account for 68% of the capital expenditure of the top nine cloud service providers (CSPs) globally, up from 47% this year.

Specifically, TrendForce expects a 50% increase in the capex of the top nine CSPs in 2027 to $1.38 trillion. That means memory and NAND flash storage revenue could hit $940 billion next year, up from an estimated $433 billion in 2026. As Micron is among the major manufacturers of DRAM and NAND flash, it seems well-placed to sustain healthy revenue and earnings growth next year.

In fact, as the memory market is poised to more than double in 2027, there is a chance of the company exceeding the 133% EPS increase to $176.50 that analysts are expecting for fiscal 2027. However, even that is a sizable jump, warranting a premium valuation for this semiconductor stock, which is trading at just 10 times earnings.

So, there are several signs suggesting that Micron stock could surge in December. The stock is extremely cheap, on track to deliver exponential growth, and could outpace Wall Street's expectations. All these factors could boost investor confidence in the stock and send it flying next month.

news.Title: Stock Market Midday, Nov. 20: Nasdaq Plunges Nearly 3% as AMD and Micron Lead a Brutal Semiconductor Sell-Off
news.Content:
As of 11:31 a.m. ET, the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) had plunged 2.80% to 23,210, while the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) fell 1.54% to 7,065, approaching the psychologically important 7,000 level. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES:^DJI) fared considerably better, edging 0.10% lower to 49,048.

Selling pressure extended beyond equities, with gold tumbling 3.73% to $3,547.90, while the 10-year Treasury yield eased three basis points to 5.04%. Consumer staples led sector performance as investors gravitated toward more defensive areas of the market, while technology suffered the heaviest losses.

Today's biggest moves

Semiconductor stocks were among the hardest hit on Friday, with Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) tumbling 11.03% as concerns surrounding firmware security and alleged ties to blacklisted Chinese companies continued to weigh on shares. Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) plunged 12.03% amid the intensifying semiconductor sell-off, reflecting growing investor concerns surrounding chip valuations and the outlook for memory demand.

Meanwhile, Humana (NYSE:HUM) gained 4.63%, recovering some of its losses from earlier this week following proposed changes to Medicare Advantage regulations. Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT) also bucked the broader market trend, climbing 3.18% as investors evaluated the retailer's performance and outlook heading into the holiday shopping season.

What this means for investors

For much of the past two years, investors have rewarded companies for their exposure to AI and ability to grow revenue. However, with financing costs remaining elevated, the market is increasingly likely to favor companies generating tangible returns from AI over those committing billions of dollars to infrastructure with uncertain payback periods. Profit margins, free cash flow, and capital efficiency could become more influential in determining which technology stocks outperform.

Beyond technology, the next several weeks of holiday shopping will provide an important indication of whether consumer spending can withstand persistently restrictive financial conditions. Any meaningful deterioration in consumer demand could prompt analysts to lower corporate earnings expectations for 2027, leaving stocks vulnerable to further valuation compression.

Another development worth monitoring is the simultaneous weakness in stocks, gold, and cryptocurrencies, which suggests investors may be reducing their overall risk exposure. With the S&P 500 trading below its 200-day moving average, the next meaningful recovery will ideally be accompanied by broader sector participation, easing borrowing costs, and stabilizing earnings expectations. Without improvement in these conditions, even a substantial market rebound could prove short-lived.

news.Title: Google reportedly cuts Broadcom-designed TPU plans, eyes more MediaTek chips
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Google has reduced its planned 2027 shipments of Broadcom-designed AI chips while preparing to increase shipments of a MediaTek-designed alternative, according to technology supply-chain analyst Ming-Chi Kuo.

Our AI stock portfolio is beating the S&P 500 by 118%. Discover the stocks we're buying and the opportunities we're watching next. Exclusive for Yahoo! Finance readers: 55% off for Black Friday, plus an extra 15% at checkout. Subscribe today! »

The reported changes suggest Google is adjusting the mix of its custom AI processors as it navigates supply-chain constraints and limited data-center power—not necessarily pulling back on its broader AI ambitions.

In a recent post, Kuo said his latest industry survey indicated that Google had cut planned 2027 shipments of its Broadcom-designed TPU 8i series by approximately 1 million units. That represents roughly 20% of the series' previously expected shipment volume.

Those figures imply a reduction from approximately 5 million chips to 4 million, although both totals are estimates derived from Kuo's reported numbers.

Most of the cuts affect the higher-priced 8i Max, also known as Whalefish, according to Kuo. That concentration could make the potential revenue impact more significant than the unit reduction alone suggests. However, his post did not provide pricing, contract terms or an estimate of the financial effect on Broadcom.

TPUs, or Tensor Processing Units, are Google's custom processors for AI workloads.

Kuo also reported that Google plans to increase 2027 shipments of the MediaTek-designed TPU 8t series, though the details remain unsettled.

The post did not specify the size of that increase, leaving it unclear whether additional 8t shipments would fully offset the reduction in the 8i family.

For investors, the report is directionally unfavorable for expectations surrounding Broadcom's Google TPU business and potentially favorable for MediaTek's role in Google's chip plans. It does not, however, establish the eventual revenue impact for either company.

Stop chasing stocks after they've already rallied. Find your next investment opportunity with AI stock picks, earnings insights, and market-moving news. Yahoo! Finance readers get an extra 15% off on top of the 55% off Black Friday price. Join today! »

Kuo linked the change to Google's prioritization of frontier model development—the work involved in building its most advanced AI models.

According to his post, Google has repeatedly emphasized in recent months that frontier development receives first call on available computing resources. He characterized the changing TPU shipment mix as an adjustment to that priority amid tight supply chains and data-center power constraints.

Story Continues

The distinction matters: a reduction in one chip family does not automatically mean Google expects less overall demand for AI computing. It could instead reflect a decision to allocate scarce manufacturing capacity, infrastructure and electricity differently.

Kuo's post did not provide enough technical or economic detail to establish exactly why Google would favor additional 8t shipments over the affected 8i models.

Kuo, an analyst at TF International Securities best known for his technology supply-chain research, based the report on an industry survey rather than an official Google announcement.

With the shipment changes concerning 2027, the outlook remains subject to revisions. The key questions are how much Google ultimately increases its MediaTek-designed chip orders, whether those gains offset the Broadcom-designed reductions, and what the final mix means for supplier revenue.

Broadcom shares were down 8.9% on the day amid broad-based selling across the semiconductor sector. Alongside that wider weakness, Kuo's report raised concerns about lower expected Google TPU volumes, particularly for higher-priced models, and a potential shift toward MediaTek-designed chips.

The decline should not be attributed solely to the reported shipment changes. Still, the report adds uncertainty around Broadcom's future Google-related revenue as investors reassess expectations for AI-chip suppliers.

For now, Kuo's findings point to a potential reshuffling within Google's AI-chip supply chain—not clear evidence of a retreat from AI investment.

news.Title: Why Micron Stock Crashed Today
news.Content:
Micron (NASDAQ:MU) stock tumbled 10.6% through 11:20 a.m. ET Friday morning, and I know what you're thinking:

Anthropic IPO'd yesterday at $83 a share , opened at $111.50 -- a 34% gain -- and then closed at $97.17 -- a 13% loss for anyone who bought in at the open. It's not quite a broken IPO, but for many investors it probably feels like one, and it may be making investors in other artificial intelligence-related stocks nervous. It doesn't help that Anthropic is down another 10.4% today.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

But I think there's another reason why Micron stock is down today.

I blame TrendForce.

Image source: Getty Images.

TrendForce sounds the alarm on NAND

As StreetInsider.com reports today, memory-market research firm TrendForce just published a negative forecast for NAND flash memory demand in 2027.

Major Chinese cloud providers are likely to cut orders for enterprise SSDs next year, TrendForce warns. Indeed, they're already cutting orders, and NAND spot prices are already down 20% "as distributors clear inventory." This decrease in demand may eliminate pricing pressure on NAND chips, forcing NAND prices lower in Q1 2027, in Q2 2027, and "onward."

What this means for Micron

Now, the good news for Micron is that it doesn't just sell NAND. Actually, only about 26% of the company's revenue comes from NAND, with the balance coming from sales of DRAM. This means that Micron won't be as sensitive to NAND price declines as Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK), for example.

But it's still going to pinch.

Investors also have to be alert to the risk that the same dynamics that depress demand for NAND may also affect DRAM demand. If we see demand and prices decline there as well, then Micron may fail to dodge this bullet.

Caveat Micron investor.
