news.Title: 3 Dividend ETFs Offering Steadier Footing in a Shaky Market
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Schwab US Dividend Equity ETF? Here are five stocks we like better.

Dividend-focused ETFs have held up better than the broader market during the recent sell-off, offering investors a way to maintain equity exposure.

SCHD and LVHI offer lower volatility and dividend income, although LVHI carries higher expenses.

VYM provides broad diversification and low fees, but its substantial Broadcom holding leaves some exposure to the technology sector.

Over the past month, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA: SPY) has fallen nearly 5%, while the tech-heavy Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ: QQQ) has dropped about 8%, as the sell-off in AI and semiconductor stocks spilled over into the broader market.

For more conservative investors, the instinct in moments like this can be to step aside entirely. But exiting the market altogether risks missing the rebound when sentiment eventually turns. A middle ground might be to rotate a portion of capital into funds built to absorb less market turbulence, staying invested while dialing down overall volatility.

→ 3 Dividend ETFs Offering Steadier Footing in a Shaky Market

With the 10-year Treasury yield sitting just above 5%, investors purely chasing income can currently earn more, with less credit risk, in government bonds than in any of the funds below. So the case for these three ETFs is stability first, with stock market exposure maintained and dividends serving as a supporting benefit rather than the main attraction.

Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF: Quality Screens and a Defensive Tilt

The Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (NYSEARCA: SCHD) tracks the Dow Jones U.S. Dividend 100 Index, which filters companies on measures such as cash flow, return on equity, and dividend growth history.

→ Cracks in the Crockery? Williams-Sonoma Insiders Sell Shares

The result is a portfolio of about 100 mature, cash-generative businesses, with names such as Procter & Gamble (NYSE: PG), Coca-Cola (NYSE: KO), and Chevron (NYSE: CVX) among its largest positions.

That makeup has translated into steadier price action. SCHD carries a beta of 0.68 and has held roughly flat over the past month, even as the S&P 500 slid.

→ If NVIDIA Tightens Its Wallet, These 3 Stocks Could Feel It

It remains up more than 26% year to date and sits less than 5% below its 52-week high.

At just 0.06% in annual expenses, it is one of the cheapest funds in its category and yields about 3%.

Its top 10 holdings, however, make up roughly 41% of assets, so it is more concentrated than its holding count might suggest.

Story Continues

Franklin International Low Volatility High Dividend Index ETF: The Lowest Volatility of the Group

The Franklin International Low Volatility High Dividend Index ETF (BATS: LVHI) offers a different angle by looking outside the U.S. altogether.

The fund selects dividend-paying stocks across developed international markets, then weights them toward those with lower volatility.

Canada, Japan, and the United Kingdom are its largest country exposures, with Shell (NYSE: SHEL) and Unilever (NYSE: UL) among its top holdings.

The fund hedges its currency exposure back to the U.S. dollar, helping to reduce the foreign exchange swings that can add volatility to international funds. It also carries a beta of just 0.34, the lowest of the three.

That steadiness has shown up recently, with the fund essentially flat over the past month and about 3.5% below its 52-week high.

LVHI offers the highest dividend yield of the group at nearly 5%. The trade-off is cost: a 0.40% expense ratio and a portfolio weighted heavily toward financials and energy, which together make up more than 40% of assets.

Vanguard High Dividend Yield ETF: Broad Diversification at a Low Cost

The Vanguard High Dividend Yield ETF (NYSEARCA: VYM) takes the broadest approach of the three.

It tracks the FTSE High Dividend Yield Index, holding roughly 600 U.S. companies that pay above-average dividends, with its top 10 positions accounting for only about a quarter of assets.

VYM has also held up well, remaining roughly flat over the past month compared with the S&P 500's nearly 5% decline, and it trades less than 5% below its 52-week high.

Its 0.04% expense ratio is the lowest of the group, and its beta of 0.73 points to noticeably less volatility than the broader market.

VYM is not entirely insulated from the AI trade.

Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO) is its largest holding at nearly 7% of assets, alongside JPMorgan Chase (NYSE: JPM) and Exxon Mobil (NYSE: XOM). Its 2.3% yield is also the lowest of the three.

Staying in the Market Without the Full Ride

None of these funds will escape a broad market decline, and they are likely to lag in tech-led rallies. With Treasuries paying more, they are also not the answer for investors focused solely on income.

They can help investors stay invested while softening the impact of the market's swings. Each has held up considerably better than the S&P 500 during the recent turbulence and sits within 5% of its 52-week high. For investors weighing whether to sit on the sidelines or ride out the uncertainty, rotating a portion of capital into funds like these offers a measured alternative to an all-or-nothing decision.

Management expects data center revenues to increase approximately 10% in the fourth quarter, supported by higher demand for 800G and 1.6T connectivity, as well as increasing adoption of advanced power management solutions.

Strength in ADI's industrial business is also expected to support fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results. Management expects industrial revenues to grow at a high-single-digit rate in the fourth quarter. Increasing AI infrastructure investments are also driving demand for ATE solutions, while continued defense spending and higher analog content across industrial applications provide additional growth opportunities.

ADI's automotive and consumer businesses are expected to have contributed to the company's growth in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. In automotive, the company is benefiting from higher content and market-share gains across next-generation advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS), infotainment and electric powertrains. Management expects automotive revenues to increase at a low-single-digit rate in the fourth quarter. Its consumer business is also expected to grow at a high-single-digit rate, supported by demand across smartphones, hearables, wearables and its B2B-like prosumer business.

Higher revenue and favorable product mix are expected to have supported further gross margin expansion. The company is also expected to have benefited from higher factory utilization as demand improves across its end markets.

news.Title: 《台股盤後》重摔2393點、險守36K；本週跌逾17%
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-20 16:14:02 新聞中心 發佈

台股今(20)日受制費半指數週四再跌逾2%與INTEL 18A製程傳出重大進展、台幣盤中又貶破33元大關下，台積電開盤就重挫，加上創意跌停鎖死、台達電/南亞/南亞科/奇鋐/欣興/台光電皆無力打開跌停，拖累前20大權值股如聯發科/日月光投控皆跌逾9%、金控重量級權值股亦跌逾6%，導致市場對國安基金強力護盤說法存疑下，29大類股皆全數收黑、跌幅皆逾3%，加權指數開低走低、收在36033.29點，重摔2393.60點或6.23%、史上第三大收盤跌點，僅能險守36K，成交量則再縮至8773.50億元；週K翻黑，本週共計下跌7641.83點或17.50%。

Anthropic超大規模IPO案未能重振投資人對逐漸消褪AI的熱情，再加上AMD的中國曝險引發疑慮下，美國四大指數週四全面下殺，並以費半指數下跌2.41%表現最差。亞洲股市方面，受制NASDAQ電子盤持續下跌，日股AI、半導體相關股慘跌，拖累日經225指數開低走低，終場收在最低點、重摔5.06%；韓國KOSPI指數亦收跌5.21%。

台股今日續遭賣壓襲擊，電子權值股淪為重災區，台積電開低走低，險守2000元關卡、下跌4.76%，台達電、創意、鴻勁、健策、聯發科、台光電、川湖、欣興、南亞科、奇鋐慘遭跌停，日月光投控重挫逾9%，聯電、智邦、國巨*跌幅也都超過8%。

觀察29大類股表現，台玻、中釉打入跌停拖累玻璃陶瓷類股大跌9.69%、跌幅最重。電子零組件類股也跌9.51%、跌幅居第二，其中金像電、聯茂、禾伸堂、南電、臻鼎-KY、華新科等多檔個股都收在跌停板價位。塑膠類股跌勢亦深、下跌9.09%，跌幅居第三；今日表現相對較好的前三名類股為資訊服務類股跌3.16%、貿易百貨類股跌3.47%、居家生活類股收跌3.86%，亦即所有類股皆慘跌收黑。

三大法人動向方面，今日三大法人合計賣超522.46億元；其中，自營商賣超340.84億元，投信賣超87.49億元，外資及陸資賣超94.13億元。

news.Title: Anthropic上市難救行情　日股暴跌逾3000點
news.Content:
（中央社記者戴雅真東京2026年11月20日專電）日本東京股市今天重挫，日經平均指數終場大跌3007.56點，收在56436.65點。儘管備受全球投資人期待的Claude聊天機器人開發商Anthropic上市首日表現亮眼，但其他美國主要股價指數幾乎全軍覆沒，賣壓也蔓延至日本市場，AI及半導體相關股票首當其衝。

日本經濟新聞報導，Anthropic上市首日開盤價達111.5美元，較每股83美元的首次公開發行（IPO）定價高出34%，但未能帶動整體市場回升。美國道瓊工業指數及那斯達克指數雙雙下跌超過2%，市場認為，投資人為了籌措認購Anthropic股票的資金，賣出其他持股變現，導致市場供需進一步惡化。

日本股市方面，軟銀集團今天盤中一度暴跌超過16%，跌破3000日圓，創下約1年3個月以來新低。半導體相關的鎧俠、藤倉跌幅也超過10%，東京證交所Growth 250指數一度下跌近5%。

東京股市除了整體市場氣氛低迷之外，個別企業的利空消息也接踵而至。

日本菸草公司（JT）19日宣布，將遭俄羅斯政府暫時接管的當地業務排除在合併財務報表範圍之外。受此影響，JT本會計年度的業績預測將由盈轉虧，年底股息也將較原先計畫減半，導致股價大幅下挫。

知名投資人上利武嗣警告，最近無論走到哪裡，都能感受到散戶投資人普遍缺乏活力，令他相當擔憂。

他指出，「隨著股市大幅下跌，部分高股息股票的相對殖利率吸引力可能逐漸提高。除了JT之外，投資人可以從長期角度考慮其他高股息標的，但在年底之前，恐怕只能先採取防守姿態。」

news.Title: 【Follow法人】外資重砍台積電破萬張...失血237億元！同步砍0050逾11萬張居冠
news.Content:
（下午4點29分更新買賣超個股）

AI利空頻傳，市場信心潰堤，台股加權指數今（20）日終場重挫2,393.60點，創下史上第三大收盤跌點。三大法人合計賣超522.46億元，其中外資續砍94.13億元，調節元大台灣50（0050）逾11萬張居冠，同步賣超權王台積電（2330）1萬1,862張、估約提款逾237億元。分析師表示，外資操作多參考前一晚美股走勢，昨晚美股跌勢相對和緩，外資調節力道也較小，台股這幾天卻在補跌，連日下殺又讓買盤縮手，賣單一出就容易壓低成交價，放大指數跌幅。

外資今日賣超前三大：0050、00403A、00991A

觀察外資賣超前十大，ETF占5檔、金融股2檔、電子股2檔、傳產股1檔。其中，元大台灣50（0050）遭外資賣超11萬454張，高居賣超冠軍；主動統一升級50（00403A）遭調節3萬4,858張，排名第二；主動復華未來50（00991A）被賣超2萬9,987張，位居第三。

值得注意的是，台積電今日收盤下跌100元、險守2,000元大關，外資同步賣超1萬1,862張，排名第九，若以收盤價估算，提款金額高達237.24億元；電子代工大廠仁寶（2324）也遭賣超1萬543張，排名第十。

外資今日買超前三大：聯電、群創、00712

反觀外資買超前十大，電子股占4檔、ETF占4檔，金融股與傳產股各1檔。晶圓代工二哥聯電（2303）獲外資大舉買超8萬321張，奪下今日買超冠軍；面板大廠群創（3481）獲加碼4萬6,944張，排名第二；復華富時不動產（00712）獲買超3萬5,773張，排名第三。

台股狂瀉2393點 外資賣超94億元

根據證交所公布籌碼動向，三大法人今日合計賣超522.46億元。其中，外資賣超94.13億元，連續5個交易日賣超2,185.72億元，累計今年來提款台股高達3兆2,090.92億元。

投信賣超87.49億元，呈由買轉賣，累計今年來買超台股1兆2,022.41億元。

自營商賣超340.84億元，其中自行買賣賣超50.68億元，避險操作賣超290.16億元。累計今年來提款台股達1兆6,935.41億元。

美國收緊先進AI晶片及運算設備出口管制，市場對AI資本支出回報與融資風險的疑慮升溫，台股今日盤中最低下探35,738.68點，一度重挫2,688.21點，寫下史上第四大盤中跌點，上市櫃逾300檔個股盤中觸及跌停。

台股終場加權指數收在36,033.29點，下跌2,393.60點、跌幅6.23%，險守36,000點，創下史上第三大收盤跌點，成交金額9,323.21億元。

分析師示警：外資賣超幅度收斂 不一定是止跌訊號

資深證券分析師蔡明翰表示，今年上半年AI需求強勁，帶動台股、韓股及美國費城半導體指數同步走高。進入下半年，AI需求訂單尚未出現明顯變化，但股價先因漲多而修正，10月以來又碰上輝達創辦人黃仁勳下台，以及市場對2028年美國大選可能帶來政策變數的疑慮。由於韓股與費半先前修正較快，台股相對位階仍高，近兩三天跌勢因而更重。他指出，連續下跌讓市場承接意願降到低點，賣方得把價格壓得更低才容易成交，即使當天外資賣超不到百億元，指數仍可能急跌。

蔡明翰也提醒，外資接下來的賣壓仍取決於美股表現，尤其要看費半能否止跌回升。他觀察，費半跌勢已有放緩跡象，若沒有新的利空，台股跌幅有機會逐步收斂。但單日外資賣超低於百億元，還不足以判斷台股已見底或出現進場訊號。一旦美股再度走弱，外資賣壓仍可能擴大。

馮萱榕／財經特派記者，主跑財政部、電腦通路、觀光餐飲等

news.Title: 台股跌2393點！台積電尾盤爆量急拉 36K失而復得
news.Content:
台股今（20）日賣壓全面失控，指數開低走低，盤中跌勢持續擴大，終場重挫2393點，跌幅6.23%，收36033點，成交量8773億元；櫃買指數遭遇猛烈賣壓，大跌7.72%，收263.31點。權值股、AI概念股幾乎全面倒地，台達電、聯發科雙雙亮燈跌停，台達電更跌破千元大關，股王信驊也連續第2天跌停。

從個股表現來看，今日市場賣壓相當沉重，上市櫃股票幾乎全面遭到拋售，上市下跌1325家，其中179家跌停；櫃買市場下跌1075家，跌停家數也高達189家，顯示資金撤出並不只集中在大型權值股，中小型股同樣面臨沉重修正壓力。

權值股方面，台積電（2330）盤中一度失守2000元整數關卡，最低下探1970元，尾盤卻突然出現10745張大單敲進，帶動股價急拉，重新站回2000元之上。不過，台達電（2308）今日遭遇重擊，股價直接亮燈跌停，下跌100元，收在900元，正式摔出千金股行列。

聯發科（2454）同樣難逃賣壓，股價重挫370元，跌幅達9.94%，以3350元跌停價作收。股王信驊（5274）更是慘烈，股價連續第2個交易日亮燈跌停，終場收在7860元，AI相關高價股成為這波修正的重災區。

對於台股近期劇烈震盪，統一投顧董事長黎方國分析，從黃仁勳離開輝達之後，市場開始關注AI產業的融資循環，以及信用擔保機制能否持續運作，這也是目前投資人最擔心的焦點之一。由於相關發展仍存在不確定性，市場短期內恐怕難以迅速恢復信心。

黎方國指出，目前股市只能採取「以跌止跌」的方式尋求支撐，投資人操作上應該「多看少做」，不需要急著進場摸底，因為整起事件後續發展仍沒有明確答案。儘管政府已經祭出「限空令2.0」，但從盤面表現來看，市場賣壓依舊相當沉重，政策效果仍有待觀察。

至於後續投資策略，黎方國認為，這波下跌過程中，主動式ETF跌幅相對慘重，投資人現階段可以先採取防禦性布局，將目光轉向被動式ETF，以及配息、配股相對穩定的高股息ETF，降低市場劇烈波動帶來的衝擊。

黎方國也提醒，在市場尚未釐清AI產業融資循環與信用擔保問題之前，投資人不宜貿然進場搶反彈，現階段應優先控制風險，等待市場賣壓逐步消化，再觀察後續布局機會。

news.Title: 台股流動性危機！收跌2393點史上第三慘 聯發科、台達電跌停
news.Content:
台股今（20日）出現史詩級崩盤，盤中最低下殺2688點觸及35738.68點，終場狂瀉2393.60點寫下史上第三大跌點，收在36033.29點，成交量僅8774億元，流動性不足被視為當前最大危機，最大權值股台積電暴跌100元收在2000元，聯發科跌停鎖在3350元，台達電跌停收在900元，廣達與鴻海也下跌超過4%，股王信驊跌停7860元。

全球半導體與人工智慧族群加速去槓桿，加上輝達黃仁勳去職引爆恐慌，美國12月升息壓力，以及民主黨上任後可能對人工智慧產業發展設下限制，且盤面上幾乎無利多支撐，引爆多殺多融資斷頭的沉重賣壓。

上市櫃家369家跌停，若從10月6日創下的49968點歷史新高算起，台股在一個半月下跌14230點，跌幅高達28.4%，落入技術性熊市。千金股與高價股成為殺盤重心，去槓桿情緒蔓延至金融與傳產族群，幾乎無一倖免，向來被視為避險標的電信族群也撐不住，中華電信下跌將近2%，遠傳與台灣大跌逾4%。

台股傳奇交易員「巨人傑」於臉書直言，比起黃仁勳與民主黨的衝擊，台股面臨流動性危機，成交量不足的問題需要爆量才能解決，否則硬撐著台積電及金融族群也沒用，最終也會一起下跌。

第一金證投顧指出，接下來隨著輝達國安與出口管制問題逐步釐清，以及12月9日聯準會利率決策出爐，台股在12月中以後仍有反攻機會，但不宜過早預設波段低點。

建議投資人目前操作策略維持低槓桿、提高現金比重，不急於全面抄底，優先選擇大型權值股及各產業龍頭。國安基金護盤核心標的，包括台積電、鴻海、台達電、廣達、富邦金及台塑，可視為反彈優先觀察指標。

news.Title: AI概念股倒一片！逾10檔亮燈跌停 廣達緯創挫逾5% 分析師：老AI已相對抗跌
news.Content:
美國晶片出口管制新規19日生效，將收緊16、14奈米及更先進製程的邏輯晶片出貨查核，影響恐延伸至消費性電子市場，拖累亞洲股市AI與半導體股遭集中拋售。台股今（20）日盤中重挫逾2,400點， AI概念股 成為賣壓重心，台積電（2330）盤中失守2,000元，最低下探1,990元，聯發科（2454）、聯電（2303）及台達電（2308）等超過10檔一度亮燈跌停，「老AI」鴻海（2317）、廣達（2382）、緯創（3231）同步大跌逾5%，廣達更跌破250元，創2025年5月以來、近19個月新低。分析師坦言，今日老AI反而相對抗跌。

台股繼昨日失守年線後，今日以37,646.13點跳空開低，下跌780.76點，隨後摜破11月6日前低37,837.05點，並接連失守37,000點及36,000點，截至上午11時40分，最低探至35,959.03點、重挫2,467.86點，改寫史上盤中第五大跌點。

AI概念股掀跌停潮！電子代工、散熱、PCB、光通訊齊殺

今日AI供應鏈賣壓從ASIC、先進封裝與測試，延伸至散熱、PCB及光通訊。股王信驊（5274）、ASIC指標股創意（3443）、伺服器滑軌廠川湖（2059）、散熱零件廠健策（3653）、奇鋐（3017）及銅箔基板大廠台光電（2383）等千金股相繼亮出跌停燈。半導體設備與測試族群中，旺矽（6223）、穎崴（6515）、精測（6510）、漢測（7856）、鴻勁（7769）、弘塑（3131）及印能科技（7734）也都觸及跌停。

權王台積電（2330）以2,035元開出，盤中跌破2,000元大關，市值一度降至約51.6兆元。AI伺服器及電子代工股同步走弱，鴻海（2317）、廣達（2382）、緯創（3231）、緯穎（6669）、英業達（2356）、神達（3706）、和碩（4938）、仁寶（2324）及技嘉（2376）盤中跌幅均逾5%。

PCB族群從上游材料到載板全面承壓，銅箔基板三雄台光電、聯茂（6213）、台燿（6274），以及ABF載板三雄南電（8046）、欣興（3037）、景碩（3189），盤中全數觸及跌停。玻纖布廠台玻（1802）、富喬（1815）、建榮（5340）及德宏（5475）同步亮燈，金像電（2368）、臻鼎-KY（4958）與金居（8358）也一度跌停。

光通訊族群同樣遭遇賣壓，聯亞（3081）、光聖（6442）、聯鈞（3450）、華星光（4979）及上詮（3363）盤中均觸及跌停。記憶體相關個股也普遍走低，南亞科（2408）、華邦電（2344）、旺宏（2337）、力積電（6770）、宜鼎（5289）及晶豪科（3006）盤中跌幅約7%至9%。

分析師：老AI抗跌 點名ASIC反彈機會

運達投顧分析師陳石輝指出，廣達在這波AI股殺盤前就已走弱，第三季毛利率從第二季的5.02%降至4.75%，財報公布後股價持續修正。不過，廣達前三季每股盈餘（EPS）已約20元，股價跌至247元附近後，評價已偏低。相較聯發科、日月光盤中一度跌停，老AI跌幅約5%，在這波賣壓中相對抗跌。

技術面上，陳石輝表示，廣達跌破年線後，先前反彈到年線附近就遇壓回落，如今再破前低，仍要等股價打底。緯創今日也跌破年線，但7月低點139元仍守得住，兩檔相比，他認為緯創線型較強，下周重點是能否站回年線，若反彈仍受年線壓制，宜先觀望。至於鴻海，他認為股價修正後投資價值已浮現，若與廣達相比，他會優先留意鴻海，並從EPS及電動車等業務的後續發展評估。

展望AI股反彈方向，陳石輝指出，這波賣壓已從伺服器供應鏈擴大至晶片股，輝達人事變動的影響仍需時間消化。他認為，業者可能加快自研晶片，逐步降低對輝達GPU的依賴，客製化晶片（ASIC）族群較有機會率先反彈，點名聯發科、世芯-KY（3661）、創意及近期走勢相對強勁的智原（3035）。他也預期，資金可能逐步從AI股分流至電動車、太空等題材。

美國19日生效的出口管制新規，收緊16奈米、14奈米及更先進製程邏輯晶片的出貨查核。外媒引述知情人士報導，台積電與三星電子已通知部分中國客戶，等待美方核發出口許可期間，將暫停部分處理器出貨。市場也持續關注AI業者的營收與獲利能否跟上資本支出，以及舉債擴張對現金流的影響。

news.Title: 外資撤離1152億美元創紀錄！AI晶片雙雄獲利創紀錄　韓股卻深陷「賣出韓國」風暴
news.Content:
南韓股市正面臨近年來最嚴峻的反常困局，儘管兩大權值股三星電子與SK海力士受惠於AI晶片需求爆發，交出創紀錄的財報成績單，但外資卻不為所動，持續大舉撤離，導致南韓綜合股指(KOSPI)經歷罕見的大幅修正。

截至週四(19日)，KOSPI從6月歷史高點累計暴跌44%，約3300兆韓元(約合2.4兆美元)市值灰飛煙滅，今(20)日早盤再挫4%，市場籠罩在恐慌氛圍中。

這波拋售潮規模堪稱空前，外資已連7月淨賣超韓股，累計資金淨流出高達1152億美元，創倫敦證券交易所集團(LSEG)自2008年開始統計以來的歷史新高。

首爾Kiwoom證券分析師韓志英直言，韓股正面臨全面性的「賣出韓國」趨勢，當務之急是設法重新吸引外資回流。

令人費解的是，韓股大跌與科技巨頭的強勁基本面形成強烈反差。作為全球HBM核心供應商，三星今年第三季營業利潤年增近九倍至107.4兆韓元，SK海力士同期利潤亦暴增逾七倍至83.3兆韓元。兩大巨頭更對後市樂觀，三星估晶片供應緊張恐延續至2028年，SK海力士也認為供需缺口將持續更久。

然而，三星與SK海力士合計佔KOSPI總市值近半，令韓股與全球AI投資週期深度綁定。

新加坡安本亞洲收益基金投資經理Isaac Thong指出，市場正進行明顯的資產輪動，投資人從AI相關資產撤出，轉向防禦性與高品質標的。

Thong強調，不同於過往產業下行週期，目前AI企業基本面依然強勁，這波下跌更多反映的是風險偏好降溫與資金配置的調整。

資金供需失衡更是本輪崩跌的關鍵推手。過去數月，上市公司大規模的庫藏股買回暫時吸收外資賣壓，但隨著回購計畫接近尾聲，市場憂心後續買盤斷炊。三星與SK海力士原規劃2026年股東回報合計上看210兆韓元，三星週四重申仍打算返還最多110兆韓元，SK海力士也堅持約100兆韓元的回購與股利計畫。

不過，南韓散戶歷經多輪重創，短期內恐無力填補資金缺口。此外，此前放大漲勢的SK海力士槓桿ETF，在跌勢中亦加速價格下修。

此外，華爾街對韓股長期價值仍有分歧。高盛本週再度下修KOSPI目標價，從12000點大砍至7500點，理由正是市場不願按基本面給予合理估值，但數據顯示，MSCI南韓指數預期本益比僅約3.27倍，遠低於全球指數的15.35倍，折價幅度顯著。

政治與監管變數亦添亂流。美國期中選舉後民主黨掌握國會，加上華府收緊先進晶片對亞太及拉美夥伴的出口限制，引發AI資料中心監管趨嚴的疑慮。

里昂證券(CLSA)半導體研究主管Sanjeev Rana認為，監管雖可能推高成本、拖慢基建步調，但基於AI對美國經濟與就業的重要性，算力產能仍會逐步到位，2027年企業獲利確定性依然偏高，政治風浪尚未撼動產業中長期前景。

news.Title: AI半導體股遭大舉拋售！日經早盤崩逾2700點失守57000點 韓股跌逾4%摔落5000點之下
news.Content:
日韓股市周五(20日)延續美股昨日大跌走勢，AI族群與半導體股遭猛烈拋售。日經225指數盤中重挫4.5%或2700點，跌破57000點關口，創兩週新低；南韓綜合股指(KOSPI)亦跌超4%。

受美股走勢拖累，東京市場的愛德萬測試、軟銀集團、鎧俠等AI及半導體個股率先遭拋售；首爾方面的SK海力士與三星電子分別跌近7%及5.3%，兩大記憶體巨頭成為重災區。

Anthropic周四(19日)以創紀錄融資規模在那斯達克上市，但未能提振科技股情緒。那指盤中一度上漲逾2%，隨後急轉直下、收跌逾2%。

專家認為，投資人為籌集資金認購Anthropic股票而拋售其他資產，進一步加劇科技股動盪。

此外，東京股市隨後將迎來連續三天假期，假期前的避險情緒明顯升溫，投資者傾向提前減倉以規避海外市場不確定性，令拋售壓力進一步放大。

市場人士指出，在AI族群估值偏高、假期避險與美股波動三重因素交織下，短線日股恐仍將承壓走跌。

news.Title: Anthropic掛牌未解AI疑慮，韓股早盤一度重挫4.1%、日經急跌3%
news.Content:
【財訊快報／陳孟朔】日、韓股市週五(20日)早盤再掀賣壓，韓國KOSPI指數一度重挫4.1%，日本日經225指數下跌3%，東證股價指數(TOPIX)跌2%至3,745.73點。人工智慧(AI)業者Anthropic創紀錄掛牌，未能緩解投資人對AI投資增速及科技股估值的疑慮。韓國大型半導體股領跌，SK海力士盤中一度重挫6.5%，三星電子下跌4.8%，兩檔跌幅均超過KOSPI指數。日本股市同步走弱，日經225指數跌幅大於涵蓋範圍較廣的東證股價指數。

Anthropic週四在美國掛牌，首日收在97.17美元，較83美元發行價上漲17.07%，但低於111.50美元的開盤價。同日那指下跌2.25%，創逾七個月收盤新低，科技股賣壓延續至週五亞洲早盤。

news.Title: 逾7年來首見 外資、日本散戶同步連3週減碼日股
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-20 07:08:47 蔡承啟 發佈

避險情緒升溫，外資連3週、日本散戶連4週減碼日股，而外資、日本散戶同步「連3週減碼日股」為逾7年來首見。

日經新聞報導，根據東京證券交易所19日公布的資料顯示，上週(11月第2週、11月9-13日)外資在日本股市(包含東京/名古屋市場)賣超3,124億日圓，連續第3週減碼日股，週賣超額較前一週(11月2-6日、賣超714億日圓)呈現大幅擴大。

上週日經225指數大漲3,707點(大漲6%)。而日本散戶上週在日本股市賣超3,614億日圓，連續第4週減碼日股，週賣超額較前一週(賣超4,802億日圓)呈現縮小。

據報導，外資、日本散戶同步「連3週減碼日股」，為逾7年來(2019年6月以來)首見。松井證券首席市場分析師窪田朋一郎表示，「外資和日本散戶同步賣超，是非常罕見的現象。因黃仁勳辭去CEO職務，以及美國期中選舉結果導致資料中心投資前景具不確定性，投資人避險情緒升溫」。

上週用來反映年金基金買賣狀況的信託銀行在日本股市買超3,933億日圓(前一週為買超2,306億日圓)，連續第2週加碼日股，週買超額創約6年7個月來(2020年3月第4週以來)新高水準。

news.Title: Qualcomm lays off 100s amid global restructuring, raises $4 billion
news.Content:
Qualcomm, the U.S. semiconductor giant whose chips power smartphones from Samsung, Xiaomi and OnePlus, as well as laptops from Microsoft, Dell and HP, is preparing another round of layoffs as it expands into artificial intelligence and data centers.

The San Diego-based company plans to permanently eliminate approximately 520 positions across its California offices, according to two newly filed Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) letters reviewed by TheStreet.

The layoffs, affecting engineers, senior executives, and other corporate employees, come just weeks after CEO Cristiano Amon delivered a blunt warning about employee performance and amid reports of approximately 1,500 additional job cuts in India.

Qualcomm files WARN notices detailing 520 layoffs

The WARN letters from Qualcomm reveal the following reductions:

San Diego: Approximately 442 employees across multiple offices, including locations at Qualcomm's Morehouse Drive headquarters complex.

Santa Clara and San Jose: Approximately 78 employees across several engineering and corporate offices.

The affected positions extend well beyond entry-level and administrative roles.

The notices identify senior and principal engineers, engineering directors, business development executives, product managers, financial analysts, attorneys and human resources personnel among the affected employees.

More Layoffs:

Canva CEO apologizes to workers, makes unusual promise amid layoffs

Disney eyes thousands more layoffs as major cost-cutting push widens

Popular website builder cuts 19% of jobs as CEO signals major shift

Some of the positions being eliminated include vice presidents of engineering, business development, and legal operations, as well as senior directors responsible for technology and product management.

Qualcomm confirmed in the filings that the reductions are permanent and do not involve closing its offices.

Employees received individual notices on Nov. 10 and Nov. 11 informing them that their employment would end on Jan. 12.

The company also disclosed that affected employees will receive severance pay and benefits, with details to be provided separately. Qualcomm did not specify the value of the packages in the WARN letters.

Workers will be eligible to apply for future positions at the company and receive outplacement assistance through LHH, a career-transition services provider.

Qualcomm CEO's blunt warning precedes global job cuts

The California layoffs come weeks after Amon informed employees of a global workforce reduction following the company's annual performance reviews.

Story Continues

In an internal memorandum dated Oct. 19, obtained by Reuters , Amon described the upcoming layoffs as a "performance-focused reduction" aimed at building a stronger performance culture.

He said the company needed to address areas where performance had consistently fallen short of expectations. The memo did not disclose how many employees would be affected, although notifications were expected to begin in November.

Qualcomm's restructuring has also extended to India, one of its largest engineering centers outside the United States.

On Nov. 12, The Times of India reported that approximately 1,500 employees were laid off across the country.

A separate Moneycontrol report estimated that more than 1,000 workers could be impacted.

Several affected employees told Moneycontrol they had received strong performance ratings and maintained good employment records before being laid off, raising questions about the performance-focused explanation.

Qualcomm has not publicly confirmed the total number of layoffs in India.

The Times of India also reported that some affected workers were offered two months' notice pay, an additional month's salary for each year of service, and continued insurance coverage for a year.

Qualcomm records $332 million in expenses amid restructuring

The latest job cuts come as Qualcomm faces declining smartphone-chip sales while investing heavily in newer businesses.

According to its fiscal 2026 annual report filed with the SEC , Qualcomm recorded $332 million in other expenses, substantially all of which were related to restructuring and severance costs.

That compares with just $39 million in fiscal 2025. The charges predate the newly disclosed November layoffs.

Qualcomm has also tapped debt markets as it reshapes its business.

In a separate SEC filing dated Nov. 13 , the chipmaker disclosed a $4 billion bond offering across five series of notes, with maturities ranging from 2028 to 2036.

The company said it would use approximately $2 billion to repay debt maturing in May 2027, with the remaining proceeds available for general corporate purposes, including potential acquisitions and working capital.

The financing disclosure came on the same day as Qualcomm's California WARN filings, highlighting the company's simultaneous efforts to manage its finances and restructure operations.

Qualcomm's Nov. 4 earnings report also revealed mounting pressure on its traditional business.

Total revenue declined 3% to $43.1 billion during fiscal 2026, while fourth-quarter revenue fell 8% to $10.32 billion. More significantly, quarterly handset-chip revenue plunged 26% to $5.14 billion.

However, its automotive business recorded 89% quarterly growth to $1.99 billion, highlighting the company's push into new markets.

Qualcomm is also making a major bet on AI data centers.

During its November earnings announcement, Amon projected that revenue from businesses outside smartphones would increase by more than 60% in fiscal 2027, with data center revenue expected to reach $5 billion.

The strategy was also outlined by CFO and Chief Operating Officer Akash Palkhiwala in an exclusive interview with TheStreet's Silin Chen , in which he discussed the company's expansion beyond smartphones into AI, automotive technology, and robotics.

Despite its restructuring, Qualcomm's global workforce actually expanded during fiscal 2026.

The company reported approximately 57,000 workers at the end of September, up from roughly 52,000 a year earlier.

The newly disclosed California layoffs illustrate how Qualcomm continues to eliminate selected positions, including senior engineering and leadership roles, even as its overall workforce and investments in emerging technologies expand.

Qualcomm faces competition as major customers develop their own chips

Qualcomm's restructuring comes as competing semiconductor companies report stronger growth and some of its biggest customers reduce their reliance on outside chip suppliers.

Taiwan's MediaTek, a direct competitor in smartphone processors, reported an 18.3% year-over-year revenue increase in the third quarter of 2026, reaching NT$168.1 billion, according to its latest earnings report .

Meanwhile, Nvidia, which competes in the broader AI semiconductor market Qualcomm is targeting, reported a 103% year-over-year revenue increase to $115.8 billion in its Nov. 17 earnings release .

Qualcomm is also facing a shift among longtime customers.

Apple, historically one of its largest modem-chip customers, is increasingly replacing Qualcomm components with its own internally developed chips. Samsung is also using its Exynos 2600 processors in certain Galaxy S26 models while retaining Qualcomm's Snapdragon chips in others.

In its latest annual report , Qualcomm acknowledged that Apple's transition to its own modems would significantly affect its chip business.

The company is betting that expansion into AI data centers, automotive technology, and other markets will help offset those losses, even as it continues restructuring its workforce.

news.Title: ROK to Boost Intelligent Devices Segment With AGILOX Buyout
news.Content:
Rockwell Automation, Inc. ROK announced that it has inked a definitive agreement to acquire AGILOX. This move supports ROK's goal of delivering production logistics capability to help customers transition from automation to autonomy by addressing material movement across the entire plant floor.

ROK's Benefits From the Deal

Based in Austria, AGILOX is a manufacturer of high-end autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) using self-developed artificial intelligence and swarm networking technology. The acquisition will bring together AGILOX's proven forklift AMR portfolio and Rockwell's existing OTTO flatbed AMR platform. This move will create a broader autonomous material-movement portfolio across manufacturing and warehouse operations.

The deal will gain from OTTO's strong North America presence and AGILOX's established European footprint. The companies expect the deal to create a stronger partner ecosystem.

AGILOX will become a part of Rockwell Automation's Intelligent Devices operating segment and gain access to ROK's deep customer relationships in strategic verticals. Rockwell Automation expects the deal to more than double its AMR business.

The deal is expected to close in the second quarter of Rockwell's fiscal year 2027, subject to closing and regulatory conditions.

Rockwell Automation Q4 Performance

Rockwell Automation reported adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $3.88 in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.72 by 4.3%. The bottom line increased 16.2% from $3.34 in the year-ago quarter, benefiting from higher sales volume, favorable currency and an improved operating margin.

Revenues increased 0.7% year over year to $2.33 billion but missed the consensus estimate of $2.39 billion by 2.3%. Organic sales increased 3%, while organic annual recurring revenue (ARR) grew 5%. We expected organic sales to increase 3.5% in the fourth quarter.

Net revenues of the Intelligent Devices segment amounted to $1.14 billion, up 5% year over year from $1.09 billion. The segment's operating earnings increased 14.9% year over year to $247 million from $215 million. Its operating margin increased to 21.6% from 19.8%, driven by higher sales volume, favorable currency, positive price-cost dynamics and a favorable mix. This was partially offset by higher compensation expenses.

ROK Stock's Price Performance

In the past year, ROK shares have gained 6.3% compared with the industry's 6.6% growth.

news.Title: Qualcomm vs. Taiwan Semiconductor: Diverging Revenue Trends for Major Chipmakers
news.Content:
Qualcomm: A Pattern of Gradual Revenue Declines

Qualcomm (NASDAQ:QCOM) primarily generates its revenue by designing, manufacturing, and supplying advanced integrated circuits and software solutions for global wireless communications, while concurrently licensing an extensive foundational intellectual property portfolio directly to major mobile device manufacturers worldwide.

It recently entered a collaborative agreement with Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) to integrate customized hardware into cloud facilities for complex data center infrastructure, while separately initiating a global workforce reduction and introducing new mobile processors at an annual technology summit.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing: A Steadily Rising Revenue Trend

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (NYSE:TSM) primarily generates its core revenue by operating globally as a dedicated independent foundry that manufactures, packages, and rigorously tests complex integrated circuits for a broad international client base of prominent advanced hardware designers.

It recently finished initial construction on an advanced fabrication plant located in Arizona to prepare for future volume production, and it simultaneously announced an expansive strategic plan to double specialized manufacturing capacity over the coming years.

Why Revenue Matters for Investors

Revenue here refers to the data provider's standardized income statement revenue line item, and observing how this metric behaves over consecutive periods provides valuable context to help individual investors evaluate whether a business is successfully capturing rising customer demand.

Foolish Take

The first thing to check for when examining a company's revenue trend is seasonality: some times of the year have stronger buying patterns than others. There usually is some seasonality for every business. To adjust for seasonality, investors often should compare one quarter to its comparable prior-year quarter to see if sales are rising or falling in that period, since reading a chart left to right could make business seem more volatile than it really is.

Qualcomm sees seasonality in its revenue, with sales peaking in December, which falls within its fiscal first quarter, but it is shown in the calendar fourth quarter in the chart. That comes from traditional holiday demand for its core smartphone customers.

TMSC also traditionally has had seasonality in its business, linked to seasonal demand for electronics. But in the chart, there is no evidence of that seasonality, as booming AI demand erases any perceived impact of consumer buying cycles.

Revenue trends like this are the most obvious metric for investors to examine when considering a stock. For Qualcomm, we see a trend of weaker sales sequentially and year-over-year. This reflects weakness in the company's mobile phone business, mainly due to steep consumer spending cuts in China.

TSMC's chart, however, is one that an investor would ideally want to see: strong sequential sales growth, indicating that demand is rising thanks to AI and data center trends.

news.Title: Why It’s Time to Buy the Pullback in Qualcomm Stock
news.Content:
Qualcomm (QCOM) stock has been under pressure, declining more than 38% from its 52-week high. The loss of Apple (AAPL) revenue and the adverse impact of rising memory costs on its handset business have weighed on its revenue and profitability.

The impact is evident in the company's fiscal 2026 results. Qualcomm reported revenue of $43.1 billion, down 3% from $44.3 billion in fiscal 2025. The company's core Qualcomm CDMA Technologies (QCT) business also saw revenue decline 3% year-over-year (YOY), largely due to weaker handset sales. However, strength in the automotive and Internet of Things (IoT) businesses supported its top line, while revenue from its Qualcomm Technology Licensing (QTL) segment remained broadly flat.

More News from Barchart

Our exclusive Barchart Brief newsletter is your FREE midday guide to what's moving stocks, sectors, and investor sentiment - delivered right when you need the info most. Subscribe today!

Profitability also took a hit. Adjusted EPS fell 12% YOY to $12.03 in fiscal 2026, reflecting weaker handset performance and continued margin pressure.

Despite these near-term challenges, there are reasons to remain optimistic about Qualcomm's prospects. Much of the negative news is already reflected in the price of QCOM stock. At the same time, its growing pipeline of opportunities across automotive, IoT, data center, and other markets provides a solid base for growth.

Qualcomm Is Set for Stronger Growth

Qualcomm entered fiscal 2027 strong, supported by its strategic shift toward revenue diversification, a solid data-center revenue opportunity, and ongoing strength in automotive.

Qualcomm expects non-handset revenues within its QCT segment — which is comprised of automotive, IoT, and data center — to increase by more than 60% YOY. These businesses are also projected to contribute more than 50% of total QCT revenues during the fiscal year, highlighting Qualcomm's gradual transition away from its traditional dependence on the smartphone market.

The data-center business is expected to become a significant growth contributor as Qualcomm moves from customer engagements to commercial shipments. Management has reaffirmed its revenue targets of $5 billion for fiscal 2027 and $15 billion for fiscal 2029, with the business expected to exit fiscal 2027 at an annualized revenue run rate (ARR) of approximately $7 billion. Initial shipments to two hyperscaler customers are expected to help generate more than $650 million in data-center revenue in the December quarter.

Story Continues

Furthermore, Qualcomm's strategic agreement with Amazon's (AMZN) Amazon Web Services presents a revenue opportunity of up to $60 billion over the next decade, while additional engagements with hyperscalers could further strengthen its long-term growth pipeline.

Qualcomm's automotive business is also demonstrating strong momentum, achieving an $8 billion ARR by the end of fiscal 2026. At the same time, investments in agentic artificial intelligence (AI), AI accelerators, and CPU platforms are positioning the company to capitalize on emerging computing requirements and create new product opportunities.

In QTL, Qualcomm has completed long-term agreements with major customers, including Apple, Huawei, and Transsion. These renewals provide greater revenue visibility and reduce near-term licensing uncertainty, while management expects the long-term QTL revenue outlook to remain unchanged. Additionally, planned product price increases to offset higher semiconductor input costs are expected to support QCT gross margins, with the full benefits likely to materialize in the second half of fiscal 2027.

Overall, Qualcomm's prospects remain solid, driven by a structural shift toward a more diversified revenue base. Expanding data-center operations, resilient automotive demand, AI-related investments, and stable licensing revenues provide multiple growth drivers.

Qualcomm's Diversified Growth Story Makes the Pullback Worth Buying

Wall Street analysts have a consensus "Moderate Buy" rating for QCOM stock. However, the pullback presents an attractive opportunity for long-term investors, as Qualcomm's growth prospects extend well beyond the challenged smartphone market. Although the loss of Apple-related revenue, weaker handset demand, and rising memory costs have weighed on its recent financial performance, the company's expanding automotive, IoT, and data-center businesses offer meaningful growth opportunities.

Moreover, renewed licensing agreements and planned product price increases should provide additional support to revenue visibility and margins. While near-term volatility may persist, Qualcomm's expanding growth pipeline and strategic positioning in AI infrastructure strengthen its investment case.

news.Title: TSMC tightens China AI chip curbs as new US rules close manufacturing loophole, sources say
news.Content: By Che Pan and Wen-Yee Lee Nov 19 (Reuters) - Taiwan's TSMC is tightening restrictions on Chinese chip designers, suspending some previously permitted advanced manufacturing orders and generally limiting affected customers to older chipmaking ‌technology, according to two people familiar with the matter. The move ...
news.AI_Summary:
• TSMC is implementing stricter restrictions on Chinese chip designers, halting advanced manufacturing orders below 16nm unless US export licenses are obtained.
• This move aims to close loopholes for Chinese companies seeking to produce advanced AI processors, potentially hindering their development of domestic alternatives to Nvidia chips.
• Chinese designers will generally be limited to older 28nm and 40nm processes, excluding those requiring high-bandwidth memory (HBM) or advanced packaging.
• The restrictions follow new US Commerce Department rules that eliminate a previous verification process for Chinese chip designs.
• These measures could significantly impact Chinese AI chip developers, including those creating alternatives to Nvidia's processors.

news.Title: Analysts Turned Bearish on These 5 Stocks on Monday
news.Content: US stocks reached mid-November under pressure from the same trade that carried them to records. On November 5, the Nasdaq Composite posted its deepest one-day drop in 19 months and confirmed a correction, as chipmakers sank on fears that tougher AI regulation could follow the Democratic win in Congress, Reuters reported. That day the Dow fell 3.4%, the S&P 500 slid 4.4%, and the Nasdaq dropped 5.5%. The weakness carried into the following week. Early on November 16, Nasdaq 100 futures were down 0.97% as AI-linked stocks came under pressure, and Reuters noted that markets were fully pricing a December rate increase after hotter-than-expected inflation data. Rate Hike Bets Weigh on the AI Trade By November 17, traders priced a 97.4% likelihood of a 25-basis-point Fed rate increase in December, according to CME FedWatch figures cited by Reuters. Higher borrowing costs matter most for the companies that have spent heavily on AI buildouts, and the spending itself is now under question from investors and strategists alike. Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB, said investors want to know how long the "hyperscaler capex super cycle" will keep supporting chip sales growth. Treasury yields have been moving sharply too: the 2-year yield fell more than 2 basis points on November 16, after its largest weekly rise in over two years the previous Friday. By the close on November 17, the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq had notched their first four-day streak of declines since September, Reuters reported. Fed speakers Christopher Waller, Beth Hammack, and John Williams were scheduled to talk that day, and the minutes of the October policy meeting were due the next day. For more on how analysts have treated the group during the slide, see our list of oversold AI stocks with more than 50% analyst upside . A Big AI Listing Tests Investor Appetite A large AI company's public debut is expected later this week, and Reuters described it as a test of demand for AI investments. Ipek Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote, said a successful debut won't necessarily lift every AI stock, because investors buying the new shares may sell existing tech holdings to make room. Bank of America economists expect the October minutes to show a deeper policy divide than the 10-2 vote suggested, which leaves rate expectations as unsettled as sentiment toward AI. Investors who would rather look at cheaper names can start with our ranking of affordable stocks that Wall Street analysts like . We shared the expanded list of Analysts Turned Bearish on These 10 Stocks on Monday here. You can find the top 5 stocks below. We have ranked these stocks in ascending order of their average upside potential, as of November 16. At Insider Monkey, we are obsessed with what hedge funds do. The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. Insider Monkey's quarterly newsletter strategy selects 14 small-cap and large-cap stocks every quarter and has returned 612% since May 2014, beating its benchmark by 375 percentage points ( see more details here ). Analysts Turned Bearish on These 5 Stocks on Monday 5. Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) Average Upside Potential: 64% Freedom Broker cut its price target on Applied Materials to $490 from $530 on November 16 and kept a Buy rating, citing multiple compression. The firm said the company's results beat its estimates for both revenue and earnings per share, by a small margin on revenue and a larger one on earnings. Lower-than-expected operating expenses offset a gross margin that fell short of Freedom Broker's forecast. Growth was led by DRAM, which rose to a third of Semiconductor Systems revenue, and the company expects wafer fab equipment spending to grow more than 30% in 2027. Applied Materials makes the equipment chipmakers use to build semiconductors. For the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, which ended October 25, it reported record revenue of $10.41 billion, up 53% from a year earlier, and record non-GAAP earnings per share of $4.16. Over the full fiscal year, the company distributed $4.75 billion to shareholders through share repurchases and dividends, and it guided first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue to $11.1 billion. It also unveiled the EPIC Center in Silicon Valley and added four new R&D partnerships. Our earlier analysis of Applied Materials asks whether its AI growth is already priced in. 4. Sea (NYSE:SE) Average Upside Potential: 90% Phillip Securities cut its price target on Sea to $130 from $170 on November 16 and kept a Buy rating. The firm said Sea's results for the third quarter of 2026 beat revenue expectations on growth at Shopee and Monee, but profit after tax and minority interests underperformed because of rising credit costs. Phillip raised its provision for credit losses by 3% to account for elevated credit expansion and lowered its terminal growth assumption, which pulled the target down even as it nudged up its 2026 revenue forecast. Sea runs Shopee, an e-commerce platform, Monee, its digital financial services arm, and Garena, its digital entertainment business. Phillip noted that Monee's loan book expanded 60% in the third quarter of 2026, while Garena's bookings rose 6%. The company's own results were strong at the top line. GAAP revenue rose 43.4% to $8.6 billion in the third quarter of 2026, and net income was $502.5 million. The board also approved an additional $1.0 billion share repurchase authorization. We also looked at whether Sea's 15% rally could last in an earlier piece on the stock. 3. Bilibili (NASDAQ:BILI) Average Upside Potential: 112% Macquarie downgraded Bilibili to Neutral from Outperform on November 16 and cut its U.S. price target to $13.90 from $24.20. Macquarie said consumer attention and ad budgets are shifting, which pressures platforms that depend on traffic. It lowered its advertising revenue estimates for 2026 through 2028 by 3% to 20% and its earnings estimates by 4% to 20%. It also cut its target multiple to 12 times 2027 earnings from 18 times, citing competition from short dramas. Bilibili runs a video community in China aimed at young people. Advertising has been its strongest line of business, growing faster than games. In the second quarter of 2026, advertising revenue rose 28% to RMB3.13 billion, while mobile game revenue fell 14% to RMB1.39 billion. Net profit rose 55% to RMB339.1 million. Net profit rose 55% to RMB339.1 million, and gross margin was 37.2%. Bilibili is expected to report its next quarterly results on November 24, and analysts expect earnings of $0.27 per share. Our earlier piece on how Bilibili's ad engine and margins outrun its slumping game unit covers the same split. 2. Applied Aerospace & Defense (NYSE:AADX) Average Upside Potential: 157% Jefferies downgraded Applied Aerospace & Defense to Hold from Buy on November 16 and cut the price target to $10.00 from $20.00 after the company reduced its 2026 guidance despite a third-quarter beat. Jefferies pointed to delays in rotorcraft additive manufacturing and to material supply constraints. It said $15 million to $20 million of rotorcraft revenue is slipping into the first half of 2027. The firm also flagged cost growth: headcount is up 17% since the IPO, and selling, general and administrative expenses excluding IPO costs rose 76% against sales growth of 39%. The new target equals 10.5 times 2028 EBITDA. Applied Aerospace & Defense provides design, engineering, and vertically integrated manufacturing for space and defense customers, across Space and Launch, Defense Aviation and Airborne, and Advanced Sensing and Precision Strike. In the third quarter of 2026, revenue hit a record $182.1 million, up 48.6%, and adjusted EBITDA reached $39.7 million. Backlog stood at $1.26 billion. The company now expects 2026 revenue of $660 million to $670 million. We asked whether record backlog can turn into real profit in an earlier analysis. 1. USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ:USAR) Average Upside Potential: 280% William Blair downgraded USA Rare Earth to Market Perform from Outperform on November 16, citing feedstock shortages at Less Common Metals and the Stillwater magnet plant. Because of the shortages, the firm pushed its sales and margin estimates out to 2028 and set a fair value of $9 per share. William Blair said the Serra Verde phase 1 output is committed to US SIIE under a 15-year take-or-pay agreement, so it cannot help ease the shortages. Feedstock help from the Round Top deposit is years away, and the firm said it prefers companies with a longer record of processing material. USA Rare Earth is building an integrated rare-earth and magnet supply chain. It owns Less Common Metals, the Stillwater magnet plant, the Pela Ema mine, and Round Top. In the third quarter of 2026, it reported revenue of $3.0 million and cash of about $1.2 billion. The Serra Verde combination closed on September 3, and shipments to US SIIE began in October. Management expects fourth-quarter sales of at least 325 tonnes of rare earth oxide. We looked at how it will manage the debt and production ramp after buying Serra Verde in a separate piece. news.Title: 美、日、韓全漲！ 台股獨崩1768點 法人揪背後真凶
news.Content:
美、日、韓股市同步走揚，唯獨台股重挫1,768點失守4萬點與年線！國泰期貨證券分析師郭經緯點出「AI硬體修正」疊加「內資多殺多」兩大元凶，並揭露限空令後的止跌4訊號。

美日韓股走穩台股獨自暴跌

國際股市今日走勢穩健，日股上漲0.71%、韓股勁揚1.39%，美股標普與納斯達克期指也都有1%以上的漲幅，唯獨台股背離重挫。台股今（19）日暴跌1,768點下跌4.4%，收在38,426點，成交量放大至8,953億元，一口氣摜破4萬點大關與年線（39,368點）。針對台股與國際盤脫鉤的現象，國泰期貨證券分析師郭經緯表示，主因是「AI硬體修正」，疊加「內資多殺多」。

斷頭隱憂引爆內資多殺多

分析今日籌碼面與盤面結構，郭經緯指出，今日外資賣超金額已縮小至243億元，顯見這波殺盤的賣壓核心其實來自內資。目前大盤融資餘額仍高達5,080億元，加上市場傳出9檔AI概念股爆發4.27億元違約交割，股價破線直接引爆融資斷頭潮，並連帶觸發自營商高達214億元的避險賣壓，重創中小型股表現，拖累櫃買指數大跌7.22%。

雙重利空壓抑買盤

除了內資籌碼鬆動，基本面與資金面也面臨逆風。郭經緯分析，近期美股主要反應AI模型題材上漲，但台股產業結構高度綁定輝達硬體供應鏈，目前市場正處於消化接班變數，以及SEMI（國際半導體產業協會）下修資本支出的雙重利空。與此同時，外資在期貨市場仍握有近10萬口空單，加上新台幣匯率貶破32.9元關卡，多重壓力導致市場買盤全面縮手。

止跌先看4大訊號

為穩定市場信心，金管會在今日盤後緊急祭出第二波限空令，宣布跌幅逾3.5%的個股明日平盤下禁空，並將借券賣出上限降至1%。展望明日盤勢，郭經緯認為，考量台股本週累計跌幅已逾10%，加上公股行庫進場護盤，預期明日盤勢將持續消化融資斷頭賣壓，但原本的年線支撐已轉為上檔反壓。至於大盤何時能真正落底，必須觀察4大關鍵止跌訊號，包含融資餘額連日大減、外資現貨轉買且期貨空單大減、新台幣匯率止貶回穩，以及股王信驊、創意、川湖等指標性高價股不再破底。

news.Title: 《韓股》尾盤買盤回流，KOSPI震盪收漲1.39%
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-19 16:55:18 數位內容中心 發佈

韓股今(19)日震盪收高，韓國KOSPI指數收於5,137.89點，上漲70.45點或1.39%，韓國KOSDAQ指數收於684.81點，上漲22點或3.32%。受到美股走勢分歧、科技股賣壓影響，早盤一度陷入震盪，但隨後在買盤回流帶動下，大盤逐步回升並守住漲勢，整體走勢仍偏強。

外部因素方面，市場仍關注AI投資回報疑慮，以及美國聯準會(Fed)偏鷹預期。Anthropic即將掛牌所引發的資金流向與估值壓力，讓投資人對AI題材的可持續性保持謹慎；在此背景下，韓國科技股早盤承壓，KOPSI指數一度失守5,000點整數關卡，加劇盤中波動。

權值股方面，Samsung Electronics(005930.KS)與SK hynix(000660.KS)早盤走弱，拖累KOSPI指數表現，半導體類股賣壓為指數早盤震盪的主因。不過，隨著尾盤買盤回流，大型科技股跌勢收斂，帶動KOSPI指數回升，終場重新站上5,100點。

相較之下，KOSDAQ指數走勢更為強勁，顯示市場資金仍在不同個股題材間輪動。市場對新掛牌與中小型成長股的風險偏好仍偏審慎，個股表現明顯分化，反映資金尚未完全回到單一投資主軸。

news.Title: 〈陸股盤後〉習近平發表APEC講話 三大指數走低
news.Content:
中國股市A股三大指數19日（周四）走低，中國國家主席習近平當天在深圳主持亞太經合組織（APEC）第三十三次領導人非正式會議，並發表題為《建設亞太共同體 續寫「亞太奇蹟」新篇章》講話。

上證指數19日收報3,577.62點，跌0.28%。深證成指收報10,583.20點，跌0.71%。創業板指收報2,293.34點，跌0.79%。

據《新華社》報導，習近平表示，世界百年變局加速演進，科技創新和產業創新方興未艾。面對新的機遇和挑戰，亞太合作必須適應新形勢、邁出新步伐、開創新局面，推動建設和衷共濟、開放融通、開拓創新、包容發展的亞太共同體。

習近平就此提出四個建議：  ——建設亞太共同體，要堅持和衷共濟。浩瀚的太平洋承載千帆、滋養萬物，造就了亞太地區兼收並蓄、和合共生的磅礴氣象。亞太大家庭的成員同在一條船上，要經受住太平洋的風浪，就應當勠力同心、守望相助，拉緊共同利益紐帶，攜手應對困難和挑戰，持續培育共同體意識。

——建設亞太共同體，要堅持開放融通。開放合作是亞太發展振興的必由之路。要秉持開放的區域主義，穩步推進經濟一體化進程，建構開放而不排他、融合而不分割的合作格局。倡導自由開放的貿易和投資，打通要素流動堵點，暢通經濟循環經脈，為亞太經濟增長開拓更廣闊空間。

——建設亞太共同體，要堅持開拓創新。創新是引領發展的第一動力。要鼓勵科技交流合作，促進創新成果轉化，營造開放、公平、公正、非歧視的合作環境。發揚進取精神，放大亞太經合組織孵化器作用，推動機制理念創新和結構性改革，不斷釋放亞太經濟的活力和潛力。

——建設亞太共同體，要堅持包容發展。亞太經濟體多樣性突出，發展訴求各異。要因勢利導推進合作，讓發展成果普惠共享，增加民眾獲得感，照顧各方舒適度，為實現亞太共同體目標積累有利條件。

news.Title: Stock Market Correction: 1 Investing Move I'm Avoiding Right Now
news.Content:
The number one thing I don't want to do, at any time and for any reason, is change my long-term investment approach to fit the current market zeitgeist. It is hard to stick to a long-term plan, especially when you believe there's a material risk of a stock market correction. But history shows that while corrections come and go, the market has always resumed its upward march.

This is why, despite my concerns about an artificial intelligence (AI) bubble, I'm not selling either of my two technology stocks: International Business Machines (NYSE: IBM) and Texas Instruments (NASDAQ: TXN). Here's a deeper dive into why sticking to my dividend-centric investment approach trumps the risk of the AI bubble bursting.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

There will be a bear market

I don't know when it will arrive, but I know with 100% certainty that there will be another bear market. And if history is any guide, a bull market will follow, eventually pushing the market to new all-time highs. That's what history shows, and you just have to look at a graph of the S&P 500 index (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) to prove to yourself that buying and holding is a pretty good investment plan.

That said, I am a dividend investor with a value focus. My preference is to buy companies with long histories of dividend growth when they have historically high yields. I believe those two facts indicate a good business and an attractive valuation. That's how I came across IBM and Texas Instruments. At this point, IBM's dividend streak is up to 31 years, while Texas Instruments' is at 23 years.

^SPX data by YCharts

I bought both stocks before the artificial intelligence trade took off, so my decision to jump aboard had nothing to do with that technology. I like IBM because it has an over 100-year history of adapting to the world around it, with a focus on serving business customers. I'm fond of Texas Instruments because it makes boring computer chips that go into just about every electronic device. I would fully expect the two companies to be involved in AI and, in fact, I would be upset if they didn't attempt to benefit from this still-emerging technology in some way.

I'm not getting rid of a good business

To be honest, I'd expect most of the companies I own to find a way to benefit from AI, even if that just meant using it to better serve customers or lower operating costs. But I lived through the dot-com bubble and see similarities to what is going on today with AI, which I believe is in its own bubble. If history rhymes, the bursting of the AI bubble could take the broader market down with it. The truth is, I don't just expect a stock market correction; I expect a prolonged and painful bear market led by the technology sector.

Story Continues

IBM and Texas Instruments are both likely to be caught up in the downdraft to a material extent. I'm not planning on selling either stock. The reason is that I want to stick to my long-term investment approach and avoid shifting it in response to Wall Street's often mercurial mood swings. AI is likely to change the world, just like the internet did at the turn of the century. And IBM and Texas Instruments will likely benefit for years to come from the changes that accompany broad AI adoption.

Unless either of these technology icons cuts their dividends or dramatically changes their business approach, my thesis for owning them isn't altered. Thus, my plan is to stick out the next bear market with companies I believe are worth holding over the long term. IBM and Texas Instruments are exactly those kinds of businesses.

The long-term history is clear, but that doesn't make buy and hold easy

As the above S&P 500 index graph highlights, buying and holding has been a winning long-term strategy. I lean into that with dividend stocks. I know that there's a bear market coming, because that's just how the market works. I expect the next correction to include AI-related stocks, including my only two tech holdings: IBM and Texas Instruments. I'm still not going to abandon my long-term investment approach because it has nothing to do with AI and everything to do with owning good businesses for the long term. IBM and Texas Instruments are still good businesses.

news.Title: Rockwell Automation Enhances Emulate3D With NVIDIA Technologies
news.Content:
Rockwell Automation, Inc. ROK announced that it is integrating NVIDIA Corporation 's NVDA NVIDIA Omniverse, NVIDIA RTX and OpenUSD technologies with its Emulate3D software. This move will expand the scale and performance of industrial simulation for manufacturers.

Rockwell Automation's Emulate3D software is a digital twin and industrial simulation software that helps manufacturers build 3D physics-based models to provide realistic feedback in place of the real automated system. The Emulate3D™ digital twin software enables users to identify potential control issues preemptively.

The addition of NVIDIA Omniverse, NVIDIA RTX and OpenUSD technologies to Emulate3D enables companies to move beyond single-machine testing and simulate operations across the entire factory floor. The expanded capabilities create a solid digital foundation for testing designs, operational strategies and AI-enabled workflows before physical commissioning.

This will help minimize commissioning risk by identifying issues earlier in the design process. The integration further supports the development of AI-enabled workflows across engineering and factory operations.

Rockwell Automation Q4 Performance

Rockwell Automation reported adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $3.88 in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 (ended Sept. 30, 2026), beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.72 by 4.3%. Revenues increased 0.7% year over year to $2.33 billion but missed the consensus estimate of $2.39 billion by 2.3%. Organic sales increased 3%, while organic annual recurring revenue (ARR) grew 5%. We expected organic sales to increase 3.5% in the fourth quarter.

news.Content: Wall Street closed a choppy week with the S&P 500 down 0.4% at 7,561.67 and the Nasdaq Composite off 0.91% at 25,136.27 on November 13. The slide did not erase the week's gains: the S&P 500 rose 2.5% over five sessions, its first winning week since October and its best since August, while the Nasdaq booked its first weekly gain in five weeks. Producer prices rose 0.3% from the prior month, a touch below the 0.4% economists expected, but the annual rate of 6.5% was the largest since November 2022. news.Title: The Deal Behind Needham’s Call on Lumentum (LITE)
news.Content:
We just published a list of the Forget Nvidia: 10 Stocks Wall Street is Betting on Right Now and Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) ranked 6th on this list.

Stocks ended a jumpy week with gains on paper and a sour finish. Reuters reported on November 13 that the S&P 500 fell 0.40% and the Nasdaq fell 0.91% on the day, yet the S&P 500 still rose 2.51% for the week, ending four straight weekly declines. The rebound did not survive the final session, and the reason sat in the bond market rather than in earnings.

Photo by osamu nakazawa on Unsplash

Hot Inflation Forces a Rethink on Rates

Consumer price data released on November 10 showed headline inflation rising 0.4% in October, above forecasts, with the core measure also coming in hotter than expected. Two-year Treasury yields jumped about 19 basis points that day, the biggest one-day move since April 2025, as traders abandoned hopes of a pause.

Policymakers have since leaned toward tightening. One Federal Reserve governor has argued for a December increase, possibly of half a point, and a regional Fed president wants at least two more increases of 25 basis points from a policy rate of 3.75% to 4.00%. Yahoo Finance reported that the 10-year yield stayed above 5% after leaping more than 13 basis points on November 12, and that traders now treat a December hike as a certainty.

The pressure has reached households. Freddie Mac put the average 30-year mortgage rate at 7.11% for the week ended November 12. Investors asking which beaten-down names might still be worth owning can browse 10 Oversold AI Stocks: Where Wall Street Analysts Are Spotting 50%+ Upside .

Chip Stocks Take the Brunt

Semiconductors absorbed the worst of it. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 3.4% on November 13, and technology was the weakest of the 11 S&P 500 sectors with a 1.7% decline. The VIX volatility gauge moved back above 20. A separate Yahoo Finance staff report said chip stocks had shed more than $650 billion in two days as the 10-year yield climbed about 30 basis points in a week to roughly 5.15%, its biggest weekly rise since April 2025.

Other data pointed the same way. The dollar reached a 19-month high, and Reuters reported that October producer prices were up 6.5% from a year earlier, while the two-year yield finished the week near 4.87%, its largest weekly increase in more than two years.

For anyone who wants a longer view of the sector, 10 Best Semiconductor Stocks to Buy for the Next Decade looks past the current swings. The Fed meets on December 9, and the inflation and jobs reports that arrive before then are likely to move stocks more than any single earnings release.

Story Continues

Lumentum made it to our list because it has an average upside potential of 77.0%. Marvell agreed to acquire Lumentum (NASDAQ:LITE) in an all-stock deal announced on November 2, the same day Lumentum reported its fiscal first quarter of 2027. Holders will receive Marvell shares rather than cash.

Revenue was $1.26 billion, more than double the year before, and non-GAAP earnings were $4.57 per share. The company guided fiscal second-quarter revenue to $1.575 billion to $1.625 billion. CEO Michael Hurlston said that "our OCS demand visibility has expanded significantly in recent months," and that the company had won a second major deal for optics built alongside processors. Management also said its cloud module business continues to show strength. Lumentum makes lasers and optical components that move data inside AI data centers.

Needham analyst Alex Henderson cut his price target to $800 from $1,040 on November 3 and kept a Buy rating. The deal is the other debate. Holders have to decide whether the all-stock terms are fair, and the value they receive moves with Marvell's shares. Our earlier look at the company's demand and valuation is in Lumentum (LITE) Can't Meet Demand. Can Its Valuation Hold Up? .

news.Title: What Marvell’s (MRVL) Lumentum Deal Adds to Its Anthropic Growth Story
news.Content:
Marvell Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ:MRVL) ranks sixth on our list of 10 Best Stocks to Buy Ahead of Anthropic's IPO .

The company behind Claude has launched its roadshow for a proposed offering of 825 million shares at $70 to $78 apiece and has applied to trade on Nasdaq under ANT. For public-market investors, the attention extends beyond the debut itself. Anthropic's suppliers already trade on stock exchanges, and their businesses offer several ways to follow the spending behind its expansion.

The question is how much of that opportunity will reach shareholders after the equipment, construction, and financing bills are paid.

There is considerable demand for the offering, but confidence in the business is less uniform. Reuters reported that orders reached roughly six times the available shares during the roadshow, even as investors questioned whether Anthropic could preserve its lead and expand Claude's appeal beyond coding. Those concerns matter to suppliers as well.

A successful fundraising would strengthen a major customer's finances; it would not settle the debate over how much companies will eventually pay for AI or how quickly the industry can earn back its infrastructure spending.

Amazon's Infrastructure Creates an Indirect Opportunity

Marvell sits behind part of the computing infrastructure Anthropic is securing from Amazon. Its custom chips and networking products connect the AI spending story to equipment orders. That makes it an indirect supplier play, with the opportunity tied to the buildout of Amazon's chip ecosystem rather than ownership of Anthropic shares.

The median analyst target of $300 implies 91.38% upside.

Data Center Demand Supports Growth

The latest reported quarter produced $2.739 billion in revenue, up 37% year over year, while data-center revenue grew 46%. Marvell subsequently reaffirmed a $3.15 billion revenue midpoint for the following quarter and narrowed the expected range. Those figures suggest demand is already supporting the business. The longer-term question is how much additional growth comes from custom processors and the faster connections needed as computing clusters become larger and more complex.

Lumentum Deal Brings Expansion and Execution Risks

The proposed Lumentum acquisition adds another layer. Marvell agreed to an all-stock transaction with an implied enterprise value of $115 billion, combining its semiconductor capabilities with Lumentum's optical technologies. The agreement remains subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals. Our coverage of the deal behind TD Cowen's Marvell downgrade captures the disagreement around that expansion.

Story Continues

A broader product offering could help, but integration, dilution and execution make the outcome more complicated than simply adding two growing suppliers together.

Insider Monkey's Q2 2026 database shows 96 hedge fund holders, reflecting meaningful institutional participation. The target leaves room for a recovery in confidence, although the acquisition creates questions that an Anthropic IPO cannot settle. Investors have to judge whether demand for custom chips and optical networking can keep supporting earnings while management prepares a much larger business for its next stage of growth.

news.Title: Can Qualcomm's Deal With Cirrascale Boost its AI Growth Prospects?
news.Content:
Qualcomm Incorporated QCOM is broadening its footprint in the growing data center artificial intelligence (AI) market through a partnership with Cirrascale Cloud Services. The collaboration reflects Qualcomm's efforts to expand its AI business and capitalize on growing demand for AI technology.

Under the agreement, Qualcomm's Dragonfly AI200 platform will undergo real-world workload testing and performance benchmarking to assess its capabilities across different AI applications. Cirrascale will support these activities with managed AI infrastructure, technical services and predictable flat-rate pricing without additional data transfer fees.

Qualcomm's Dragonfly AI200 is designed to handle large language models, multimodal applications and other advanced AI workloads while delivering high performance, improved energy efficiency and lower operating costs. Each card offers 768 GB of LPDDR memory and is architected to support next-generation foundation models at trillion-parameter scale. The platform also features direct liquid cooling, PCIe and Ethernet connectivity, confidential computing and support for leading AI software frameworks.

The initiative underscores Qualcomm's focus on developing advanced AI computing solutions for enterprise applications. Its emphasis on energy-efficient inference technology could help meet the growing need for scalable and cost-effective AI systems.

How Are Competitors Advancing in the AI Market?

Qualcomm competes with Intel Corporation INTC and Advanced Micro Devices AMD. Intel is expanding its AI infrastructure business with its GPU D-Series, designed to support large-scale AI inference workloads. The new accelerator offers up to 480 GB of LPDDR5X memory and aims to improve performance and energy efficiency. Intel is developing Xeon-based rack systems and open software solutions to support the growing adoption of agentic AI.

AMD is advancing in the AI market through its next-generation Instinct MI400 GPUs and rack-scale computing systems. The company introduced its MI450X GPU and reported new AI inference performance results for MI455X. AMD has strengthened its partnership with Meta Platforms, Inc . META to support large-scale AI infrastructure and future computing deployments.

news.Title: Applied Materials vs. Marvell Technology: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
news.Content:
As the race for dominance in artificial intelligence intensifies, choosing the right infrastructure provider is critical. Should you invest in equipment giant Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) or connectivity specialist Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL)?

Applied Materials supplies the tools that actually build the chips, making it a foundational player in the semiconductor ecosystem. Marvell designs the custom chips and networking components that move data between servers. Comparing these two reveals different ways to play the ongoing shift toward high-performance computing and massive data center expansion.

The case for Applied Materials

Applied Materials sells materials engineering solutions used to produce nearly every new chip and advanced display in the world. It serves a concentrated customer base of logic, foundry, and memory manufacturers, including giants like Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) and Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU). Two specific customers accounted for approximately 19% and 15% of net revenue, respectively. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business.

In the 12 months ended Oct. 25, 2026, revenue reached nearly $34.4 billion. This represented growth of roughly 21.4% compared to the prior period, driven by strong demand for advanced chipmaking equipment. Net income totaled approximately $10.1 billion, showcasing the profitability possible at this scale.

As of Applied Materials' October 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.3. This ratio measures total debt against shareholder equity, with lower numbers typically suggesting less financial leverage. The current ratio, which compares short-term assets to short-term liabilities, is roughly 2.3. For those following semiconductor stocks , strong cash flow is vital for R&D. In the fiscal year ended Oct. 25, 2026, free cash flow was nearly $6.2 billion.

The case for Marvell Technology

Marvell Technology operates as a fabless supplier, meaning it designs high-end semiconductor solutions but outsources the actual manufacturing. The company focuses on data center core networks and the network edge, serving original equipment manufacturers and cloud service providers. For its most recent annual reporting period, two customers each accounted for 10% or more of net revenue, and the 10 largest customers collectively accounted for 82% of net revenue. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business.

In the 12 months ended Aug. 1, 2026, revenue reached nearly $9.5 billion. This figure reflects growth of close to 30.6% over the previous 12 months as the company expanded its footprint in AI infrastructure. Net income for the same period was approximately $2.6 billion, marking a significant turnaround from previous years.

Story Continues

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.3. Its current ratio is approximately 2, indicating a solid ability to meet short-term obligations. In the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, free cash flow was close to $1.4 billion. Note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 33.8% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation, since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Risk profile comparison

Applied Materials faces significant geographic concentration, with a heavy reliance on customers in China. This exposure makes the company sensitive to trade policies and export restrictions. It also manages legal risks involving export controls, including a $252 million settlement reached in February 2026 for export violations involving Semiconductor Manufacturing International. Furthermore, its reliance on complex global supply chains creates vulnerability to regional disruptions or inventory obsolescence.

Marvell Technology has high customer concentration. Its 10 largest clients account for nearly 82% of revenue, and it often competes with rivals like Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO). The company is also navigating a massive $115 billion pending acquisition of Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE). This deal introduces risks related to shareholder dilution and the complex process of integrating two large organizations. Additionally, Marvell's dependency on third-party foundries in the Pacific Rim creates supply chain risks if regional political conflicts arise.

Valuation comparison

Applied Materials currently appears to be the more conservative value choice, while Marvell Technology commands a higher premium given its faster growth profile.

Which stock would I buy for 2027?

Marvell and Applied Materials are riding the current tech boom, with both stocks hitting all-time highs earlier this year. They've since pulled back a considerable amount, but they're still handily outpacing the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) by massive margins:

AMAT data by YCharts

There's not a ton of daylight between the two stocks' recent returns. And as for business performance, Applied Materials has a slightly higher net margin, while Marvell is posting stronger revenue growth.

I lean toward Applied Materials in this matchup. Marvell's revenue growth is impressive, but its pending acquisition of Lumentum introduces a fair amount of risk. There's the possibility of dilution, but there's also the potential that the combined company doesn't create the cost-savings and synergies management had hoped for. That could lead to significant writedowns, which would almost certainly impact the stock negatively.

Applied Materials just seems to have less risk, which makes it my pick for 2027 and beyond.

news.Title: Applied Materials (AMAT) May Find a Bottom Soon, Here's Why You Should Buy the Stock Now
news.Content:
A downtrend has been apparent in Applied Materials (AMAT) lately. While the stock has lost 6.3% over the past week, it could witness a trend reversal as a hammer chart pattern was formed in its last trading session. This could mean that the bulls have been able to counteract the bears to help the stock find support.

While the formation of a hammer pattern is a technical indication of nearing a bottom with potential exhaustion of selling pressure, rising optimism among Wall Street analysts about the future earnings of this maker of chipmaking equipment is a solid fundamental factor that enhances the prospects of a trend reversal for the stock.

Understanding Hammer Chart and the Technique to Trade It

This is one of the popular price patterns in candlestick charting. A minor difference between the opening and closing prices forms a small candle body, and a higher difference between the low of the day and the open or close forms a long lower wick (or vertical line). The length of the lower wick being at least twice the length of the real body, the candle resembles a 'hammer.'

In simple terms, during a downtrend, with bears having absolute control, a stock usually opens lower compared to the previous day's close, and again closes lower. On the day the hammer pattern is formed, maintaining the downtrend, the stock makes a new low. However, after eventually finding support at the low of the day, some amount of buying interest emerges, pushing the stock up to close the session near or slightly above its opening price.

When it occurs at the bottom of a downtrend, this pattern signals that the bears might have lost control over the price. And, the success of bulls in stopping the price from falling further indicates a potential trend reversal.

Hammer candles can occur on any timeframe -- such as one-minute, daily, weekly -- and are utilized by both short-term as well as long-term investors.

Like every technical indicator, the hammer chart pattern has its limitations. Particularly, as the strength of a hammer depends on its placement on the chart, it should always be used in conjunction with other bullish indicators.

Here's What Makes the Trend Reversal More Likely for AMAT

An upward trend in earnings estimate revisions that AMAT has been witnessing lately can certainly be considered a bullish indicator on the fundamental side. That's because empirical research shows that trends in earnings estimate revisions are strongly correlated with near-term stock price movements.

Over the last 30 days, the consensus EPS estimate for the current year has increased 3.3%. What it means is that the sell-side analysts covering AMAT are majorly in agreement that the company will report better earnings than they predicted earlier.

Story Continues

If this is not enough, you should note that AMAT currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which means it is in the top 20% of more than 4,000 stocks that we rank based on trends in earnings estimate revisions and EPS surprises. And stocks carrying a Zacks Rank #1 or 2 usually outperform the market. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .

Moreover, the Zacks Rank has proven to be an excellent timing indicator, helping investors identify precisely when a company's prospects are beginning to improve. So, for the shares of Applied Materials, a Zacks Rank of 2 is a more conclusive fundamental indication of a potential turnaround.

news.Title: NVIDIA Q3 Earnings Beat on Data Center Demand & Rubin Ramp-Up
news.Content:
NVIDIA Corporation NVDA posted third-quarter fiscal 2027 non-GAAP earnings of $2.68 per share, up 111% year over year. Earnings beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.50 by 7.20%, reflecting strong demand for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure and a rapid Vera Rubin rollout.

Revenues surged 103% year over year to $115.84 billion, topping the consensus mark of $108.19 billion by 7.07%. Data Center sales drove top-line growth.

NVDA's Data Center Momentum Accelerates

Data Center revenues surged 110% year over year and 21% sequentially to $107.61 billion. Vera Rubin generated nearly $20 billion in its first quarter of production shipments, marking NVIDIA's fastest product ramp. Continued demand for Blackwell Ultra also supported growth.

Hyperscale revenues reached $60.14 billion, rising 71% year over year and 23% sequentially. AI Clouds, Industrial & Enterprise revenues soared 195% year over year and 18% sequentially to $47.47 billion, benefiting from Rubin shipments to neoclouds and frontier labs building their own facilities.

NVIDIA Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

NVIDIA Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | NVIDIA Corporation Quote

NVIDIA's Edge Computing Sales Extend Gains

Edge Computing revenues were $8.23 billion, up 42% year over year and 14% sequentially. Higher sales of Blackwell workstations and computing systems for physical AI applications supported the increase, although elevated memory and system prices continued to pressure consumer PC demand.

Within reportable segments, Compute & Networking revenues totaled $106.0 billion, soaring 108% year over year and 20% sequentially. Graphics revenues surged 62% year over year and 25% sequentially to $9.8 billion, reflecting broader demand across NVIDIA's computing platforms.

NVDA's Margins Benefit From Product Mix

Non-GAAP gross margin expanded 140 basis points year over year to 74.9%, helped by a richer Blackwell Ultra product mix. The metric contracted 10 basis points sequentially as the company began ramping Rubin infrastructure.

Non-GAAP operating expenses rose 52% year over year and 7% sequentially to $8.84 billion, reflecting higher compute infrastructure and employee compensation costs. Despite this increase, non-GAAP operating income surged 116% year over year to $77.88 billion, supported by robust revenue growth.

NVIDIA's Cash Generation Funds Expansion

Cash flow from operating activities reached $48.25 billion compared with $23.75 billion a year earlier and $24.08 billion in the previous quarter. Free cash flow was $43.78 billion compared with $22.09 billion in the year-ago period. The company returned $28.1 billion to shareholders through repurchases and dividends.

Story Continues

Cash, cash equivalents and marketable debt securities totaled $53.51 billion at quarter-end. Inventories increased to $39.72 billion from $31.58 billion sequentially to support Rubin production. Accounts receivable reached $81.03 billion, while days sales outstanding increased to 64 from 60, reflecting shipment timing and extended payment terms for certain customers.

NVDA's AI Commitments Expand With Demand

Supply and capacity commitments increased to $390 billion from $279 billion in the second quarter, primarily due to multiyear memory procurement. Cloud service and data center lease commitments totaled $102 billion, reflecting investments to support product development and the company's infrastructure needs.

Additional neocloud commitments totaled $32 billion, contingent on partners securing financing and deploying systems. Maximum gross exposure under guarantees reached $118 billion, including $105 billion in credit support tied to an Ohio data center campus. Management said it had made no payments on these guarantees.

NVIDIA Raises Its Fiscal 2028 Growth View

For the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027, NVIDIA expects revenues of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%. The outlook includes an additional week and assumes no Data Center compute revenues from China. GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins are projected at 71-72%.

Non-GAAP operating expenses are expected to be approximately $10.7 billion, while GAAP expenses are projected at $11 billion. Management raised its fiscal 2028 revenue growth forecast to approximately 75% from 70%, citing stronger demand and additional supply capacity. It anticipates gross margins of 72-73% in fiscal 2028.

NVDA's Zacks Rank & Stocks to Consider

NVIDIA currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).
